# Changelog

Session-by-session record of significant changes. Most recent first.

---

## 2026-10-07 — Cross-mode defaults (Tristan's decisions of 2026-10-06)

Tristan answered the cross-mode triage decisions on 2026-10-06 (decisions 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 10; 4, 7 and 9 stay open as ISSUE-332, 333 and 334). Merged on `fix/load-accounting`: lane A in `3ca725b`, lane M in `f98c4c4`. All unit-tested, none device-verified. Full suite at `f98c4c4`: 311 files, 4350 tests passed (merge commit message). Follow-ups are ISSUE-330 to ISSUE-353.

- **Triathlon and cycling readiness counts from plan start when nothing was recorded before it (decision 1; `ad38030`).** Per-discipline CTL and ATL (`estimateDirectPerDisciplineCTLFromActivities`) are decay-weighted sums over a 120-day window started at zero, so every day before plan start read as rest for an athlete with no history. Steady training (50 TSS every other day) read run ATL/CTL 4.41 / 3.43 / 2.63 / 2.26 on days 7 / 14 / 21 / 28 (regression test `tri-readiness-observed.test.ts`), labelled Overreaching with "Run load is high relative to your baseline. Reduce run volume this week.", and the tri suggestion gate offered to swap the day's quality session while the Home ring read the same training as safe. `triLoadObservedDays` (`tri-benchmarks-from-history.ts`) returns the completed days since plan start when no activity of any sport predates it; launch stores it as `triConfig.fitness.loadObservedDays`. `observedDisciplineLoad` (`fitness-model.triathlon.ts`) divides each stored sum by the share of its window weight that falls on observed days, and `perDisciplineAcwrRaw` withholds the ratio until 14 observed days (`ROLLING_ACWR_MIN_OBSERVED_DAYS`), as running does. The under-3-weeks history gate now counts observed weeks (it read `fitnessHistory.length`, always 12). An athlete with any earlier record is unchanged, so a runner of years who starts swimming keeps the swim ramp warning. Stored CTL/ATL/Form display values are unchanged.
- **Off-ladder triathlon downgrades step one rung (decision 3a; `92d662e`, `acb4ce0`, `81a9ff8`).** Over-under and hill rides go to sweet spot, VO2 micro-interval rides to threshold intervals, open-water swims to an endurance swim (`OFF_LADDER_DOWNGRADE_RUNG`, `triathlon-constants.ts:523`), priced, named and described like a ladder step. The readiness row and the cross-training overload builders choose sessions with one classifier, `isTriQualitySession` (`tri-suggestion-apply.ts:300`). A step that would add planned load is refused (`raisesPlannedLoad`, judged by rate at the session's minutes). That holds back neuromuscular sprints: **the approved vlamax to sweet spot mapping is not shipped**, because `loadForBike` prices vlamax at 1.10 TSS/min and sweet spot at 1.5 (an 87-min session would go from 96 to 131 TSS under a "Downgrade" label). vlamax sessions now get no downgrade and no 15% overload trim (ISSUE-335). The overload modal's "-N TSS" for a downgrade is the real change (`triDowngradeTssReduction`, stored load minus the landing rung's load); the flat 25% `DOWNGRADE_TSS_REDUCTION` is removed.
- **Triathlon sessions without heart rate use the canonical load table (decision 8a; `be82b8b`).** Tri per-discipline fitness valued an HR-less session on a private per-minute scale (an unrated hour: swim 54, ride 60, run 66, other sports 36 TSS) while the weekly and daily load numbers used `TL_PER_MIN` (69). `triActivityTss` now uses `normalizeiTrimp` when iTRIMP exists, else minutes × `TL_PER_MIN[rated RPE]` (RPE 5 unrated) for every sport. `withTriRatedRpe` attaches the rating `computeWeekRawTSS` reads, and `inAppGpsRunActivities` attaches the rating under the record key. HR-less "other sport" load rises about 1.9×, unrated rides 15%, swims 28%, runs 5%, so tri cross-training ATL/CTL, the cross-training readiness bar, the cross-dominant readiness sentence and the tri capacity CTL move. Guard: Load Currency Anchor 10.
- **Mark as Done counts as load in triathlon, cycling and Just-Track (decision 2a; `7e835cf`, `8d2bcc0`, `6bcd0b0`).** The tri detail modal's `setRated` writes a manual in-app record through `recordPlannedSessionDone` (`in-app-activity.ts:620`): planned duration × `TL_PER_MIN[rated RPE]`, with bike and swim tagged by `manualSport` so Signal A uses the cycling 0.55 or swimming 0.20 runSpec. It reaches the Home strain ring, the week debrief, the holiday return and tri plan adherence. A synced ride, swim or run supersedes the record in place, searching every plan week (`supersedeInAppCrossSession`). No record is written when a synced activity already completes the session (`isSessionCompletedByActivity`: a fuzzy link to another key, or brick detection). Skip drops the record. A brick is one bike-tagged record. `manualDoneTriActivities` still deposits the tick into per-discipline CTL once.
- **HYROX cross sessions ticked with no recording count as load (decision 5a; `69d9a80`, `34608fc`).** The bike, row erg and swim injury offers write the same record (cycling, rowing, swimming), count as load and pass the MTL completion test. They carry no `musculoTendonLoad`, and the MTL sums read `wk.triWorkouts` only, so they add 0 MTL and do not move `resolveMtlAdherence` (open decision, ISSUE-330). A new 'row' supersede family lets a synced rowing session replace a rowing record.
- **HYROX stations recorded in the app weigh as strength (decision 10a; `b170dc6`).** `resolveActualSport` resolves the in-app `'hyrox'` activity type to strength (runSpec 0.35), the same weight as the session's watch HIIT copy; it was generic_sport (0.40).
- **Synced activities are filed by the athlete's local day (decision 6a; `1fb1d2e`, `2003593`, `14a2236`, `6e91cce`, `9a550b3`).** `weekIndexForDate` filed rows by UTC calendar day while plan weekdays are local, so a late-Sunday session west of UTC or an early-Monday one east of UTC landed in the neighbouring week and on the neighbouring day's strain, and a HYROX station could count twice. One rule in `src/utils/local-date.ts` (`isOnLocalDay`, `localMondayKey`, `calendarDaysBetween`) now covers the matcher and its unspent-twin dedup, Activity Review dates and buckets, the fitness-model today, strain, daily-load and to-baseline readers, the strain page, the strain day on Home, Readiness, capacity strain and the daily coach, Stats, the wizard review and tri past-race scan, sleep insights, adaptive recovery (its "today", `addDays` and the k_user recency weight), commute drift, the coach context, Apple weekly history, the plan-anchor reconcile, `derivePlanStartDate`, the activitySync current-week window, the timing-check weekday and `restoreHistoryFromServer`. The Home ring and its strain page read one computation, `computeDayStrainTSS` (`fitness-model.ts:855`), for the same local day's activities and steps. The HYROX station and guided-strength upgrades search every plan week (`findInAppGymSessionAcrossWeeks`). Unchanged: actuals already stored keep their week; Strava weekly history keeps the edge function's UTC weeks; physiology and manual-entry "today" keys stay UTC (ISSUE-331).

## 2026-10-06 — Cross-mode verification fixes (triathlon, cycling, HYROX, Just-Track)

Four verifiers checked the recent changes in each non-running mode; a triage pass split the gaps into four fix lanes and ten decisions for Tristan (answered in the 2026-10-07 entry above). Merged on `fix/load-accounting`: lane M in `a0f7fd7`, lane P in `370691a`, lane A in `63cd6f9`, lane F in `48c9cf7`. All unit-tested, none device-verified.

- **Running plan changes run in running mode only (`8d55b39`).** `hasRunningPlanWeek` (`week-resolve.ts:194`) gates `resolveWeekForPlanChanges`, `getWeekWorkoutsForPlanChange` and `triggerACWRReduction`, so Just-Track, triathlon, cycling and HYROX no longer size or write running mods against the running engine's week, which they never show. It fixes: a Just-Track GPS run opening the reduce modal on a phantom Easy Run (a regression from batch 2 `5f5b4d4`); timing suggestions on a phantom Threshold after a heavy day (a stale one is cleared on the next Strava or Garmin sync; Apple syncs do not run `mergeTimingMods`); ACWR Reduce cutting a phantom week and clearing the unspent items in Just-Track and HYROX; HYROX overflow opening the running modal; the silent Tier-1 trim writing "Auto:" mods on tri easy runs and HYROX commute runs. Just-Track and HYROX hide the Home adjust button and the recovery advice sheet. HYROX overflow is logged and continues to the RPE prompt.
- **A GPS run in triathlon, cycling or HYROX completes the card it was started from (`f8d5b9f`).** `handleCompletedRecording` matches the started card among the run sessions of `resolveTriWeekWorkouts`, writes the in-app record under the slot key with a completion rating (no running VDOT change), and runs `reconcileTriCompletions` in triathlon. The watch copy replaces the record in place, so the card stays done (the HYROX case was a batch-2 regression). Impromptu runs are offered the week's tri or HYROX run sessions. In-app GPS runs count toward tri per-discipline run CTL (`inAppGpsRunActivities`), and `manualDoneTriActivities` skips a session that has a record at its own key.
- **`parseDistanceKm` no longer reads a minutes token as miles (`9874349`).** The miles pattern matched "min", so "10 min easy warm-up" parsed as 10 miles. Synced HYROX Tempo and Interval runs now auto-match their slot on duration. Running mode changes too: minute-prescribed sessions such as "26min @ MP" (41.8 km before) or "5×4min" no longer parse to a mileage, which corrects the Mark as Done record distance, the GPS completion modal's planned distance and the distance score in `findMatchingWorkout`.
- **A card Skip in triathlon, cycling or HYROX leaves that day's planned load (`1f9ac75`).** `getPlannedDayTSSContext` honours `wk.rated[id] === 'skip'` in those modes (Home strain target). Running still prices a rated skip, because its CTL-gap re-anchor reads this context.
- **HYROX sessions carry their own slot ids (`e8cf76a`, `16c639d`).** `generateWeekSessions` stamps `W{week}-{type}-{idx}` through `stampTriWorkoutIds`, added sessions get `adhoc-` ids, and `HYROX_GENERATOR_VERSION` is 14. Before, a week's two "Easy Run" sessions shared one key: one tick showed both done and the second synced run went to review. The launch regen moved to `src/state/hyrox-plan-regen.ts` (`applyHyroxGeneratorRegen`). It carries `adhoc-` and `holiday-` sessions, gives legacy added sessions an id instead of deleting them, and re-keys name-keyed ratings, records, matches and GPS recordings (`rekeyNameKeyedHyroxSlots`). An activity under a shared name that no single session can claim goes to Activity Review.
- **HYROX muscle-tendon load reads every completion (`01253a4`, `7f1d081`, `777d1ce`, `db234a6`, `bfd89a8`).** `isMtlSessionCompleted` (`mtl.ts:107`) counts a session with a match link or an activity record on its slot key (sync, GPS run, Mark as Done, quick done). Before, actual MTL was always 0: the Stats MTL card stayed empty, the MTL readiness term never switched on, and every week advance cut the next week toward deload volume (week 2: 220 to 172 min). Pre-plan weeks are now valued at the athlete's mean completed-week MTL, and the ratio is withheld until 14 days of plan weeks are complete (`computeMtlAcwr` / `hyroxMtlAcwr`; the chronic gate of 15 is kept as `MTL_ACWR_MIN_CHRONIC`), so a plan-compliant athlete no longer reads 3.06 in week 2. That one computation feeds Home and Readiness readiness, the Stats Load ratio row and tiles, and the MTL page. The MTL page shows the current week (it showed next week) and the Readiness MTL card shows the week's completed MTL (it showed station matches only). The write-only `hyroxConfig.weeklyActualMTL` accumulator is gone.
- **HYROX readiness, forecast and adaptation read the same MTL (`0ff5726`, `f6d0f6f`, `a35528f`).** The daily coach passes `hyroxMtlAcwr`, so the label and sentence under the ring agree with the MTL-floored score (before: coach 65 On Track beside a 34 Ease Back ring). The forecast "Training fitness" factor and staleness Signal 2 compare chronic MTL with what the plan prescribed over the same completed weeks (`computeMtlChronicVsPlan`); the old anchor, 70% of the band MTL cap, read a compliant athlete as undertrained (+5% in week 1). The factor reads "Chronic MTL is N% of the load the plan prescribed through week W." The effort multiplier's under-duration guard reads the slot record. With slot ids, the HYROX execution loop is live from generator v14: next-week volume moves 0.85× to 1.15× with session RPE, HR-derived matcher ratings included (ISSUE-340).
- **HYROX commute runs carry a duration (`6ffed3b`)** at the generator easy pace (`hyroxEasyRunPaceSecKm`), so Mark as Done on a commute records load and the day target no longer uses a 60-minute fallback. The AI Coach plan skeleton (feature off) prices HYROX weeks with the planned-day pricer (`0c882ed`; it sent 0).
- **Triathlon and HYROX effort scores read completed weeks only (`fed8bfc`).** `hyroxTrailingEffortScore` and `triTrailingEffortScore` started at `wks[s.w - 1]`, the week in progress (s.w is 1-based); they now start at `wks[s.w - 2]`, like running's `getTrailingEffortScore`. Mid-week, the HYROX plan note no longer shows "Load raised N% this week" from the current week's own ratings, and a mid-week injury save no longer regenerates the week from partial ratings.
- **Triathlon and cycling suggestions act on the current week and change what they propose (`6b0fa24`, `f648e8a`, `b64ca99`, `cc84818`, `2f82add`, `9efef09`, `4f8e8e9`, `2332e60`, `2ae3335`, `3d91eeb`, `b66ac22`).** Five detectors read `wks[s.w]` (next week) as the current week: the readiness lookahead, the readiness and RPE "today" targets, the cross-training overload detector (which therefore never fired for the current week) and the volume-ramp check. On Mondays the RPE flag read this week's Sunday, still ahead, as yesterday. `computeDecayedTriCarry` had the same default. Accepted suggestions step the canonical ladders and re-price the session: runs one pace category down `RUN_PACE_LADDER` (threshold to marathon pace, not the unmatched 'tempo'), bikes and swims one rung down `BIKE_INTENSITY_LADDER` / `SWIM_INTENSITY_LADDER` with watts or CSS pace retargeted. Swap to easy and trim update the stored load (a 50-min threshold run swapped to easy reads 35 TSS, not 100) and set status 'reduced', so the session stays on Home Today. One Apply changes a session at most once and the modal shows one row per session (`oneRowPerSession`). Detectors propose only changes the apply step makes (`canApplyTriSuggestion`; 88 of 1226 overload proposals in generated plans were silently skipped before). Answered proposals are not re-proposed that week (`Week.triSuggestionsHandled`). The Adjust overlay's baseline moves with the session. Tri run paces retarget from the generator's easy pace (`triRunEasyPaceSec`). Volume-ramp suggestions are off (`TRI_VOLUME_RAMP_SUGGESTIONS_LIVE = false`): mid-week they compared partial actuals with next week's full plan and accepted trims compounded (87, 74, 63, 54 min), ISSUE-337.
- **Just-Track (`28ace08`, `280962b`, `5f1596b`).** Return to plan, after starting Create a training plan, lands back on Just-Track: `upgradeFromTrackOnly` no longer clears `s.trackOnly` (the plan build does), and `restoreJustTrackIfNoPlanBuilt` writes back the Just-Track onboarding record (`JUST_TRACK_ONBOARDING`, shared with the goals tile). Before, a synced run bound to a phantom W1-easy-0 slot, a HYROX pick left a blank HYROX Plan tab and a cycling pick switched on cycling copy. Completing the upgrade as a no-event running plan now builds the plan. The Plan tab lists each activity once (`trackOnlyWeekLog`, built on `collectWeekActivities`): a GPS run no longer shows twice and History rows no longer double km and the session count.
- **iOS 15: no regex lookbehind in app code (`ec7bfb9`).** The deployment target is iOS 15.0 and WKWebView parses lookbehind only from iOS 16.4; a lookbehind literal is a SyntaxError for its whole module. `f648e8a` added one to `retargetDescriptionPace` (`workout-scaling.ts`), which `home-view.ts` and `main.ts` import statically, so the app would not have loaded on iOS 15 to 16.3. Rewritten there and in `coach-tools.ts` and `coach-view.ts`. Guard: `src/no-regex-lookbehind.test.ts`.
- **Tests**: new files listed per feature in `docs/FEATURES.md`. Each lane's last reported full-suite run was green. `ec7bfb9` and `fed8bfc` landed after those runs with their own tests; the `f98c4c4` suite (2026-10-07 entry) covers them.

## 2026-10-06 — Load accounting batch 2 (audit lanes A, F, M and P)

Second batch of fixes from the 2026-09 load-accounting audit (`docs/audits/2026-09-load-accounting/`, untracked and local to Tristan's working tree). Merged on `fix/load-accounting`: lane F in `4e0db20`, lane M in `e918c79`, lane A in `f2b1227`, lane P in `c0d0fb5`. All unit-tested, none device-verified. Merge-time fixes: in `syncAppleHealth` the Strava gate runs before the onboarding sex gate (Apple workouts off means nothing to hold), and a held call re-enters `syncAppleHealth`, so it still ends with the post-sync pending step; `getWeekWorkoutsForPlanChange` took the audit-D3 mode gates of `getWeekWorkoutsForReview` (replaced by `hasRunningPlanWeek` in the cross-mode fixes above). Full suite at `c0d0fb5`: 278 files, 4075 tests passed (merge commit message).

- **Strava connected turns Apple workouts off (S1; `0d395b6`, `3f049cc`, `8a2ace7`).** The audit's duplicate stress test showed Apple next to Strava double counting rides, swims, HIIT and strength. `appleWorkoutsEnabled(s)` (`src/data/sources.ts:57`) gates `syncAppleHealth` and `syncAppleHealthDeepHistory`, which covers launch, the HealthKit observer, foreground resume, Account Sync, the onboarding review step and the tri DB-empty backfill. While Strava is connected none of them reads HealthKit workouts, runs `matchAndAutoComplete`, uploads to `garmin_activities` or overwrites the history baselines. Sleep, HRV, resting HR, steps, respiratory rate, SpO2, VO2max and cycling FTP keep syncing. Disconnecting Strava turns Apple workouts back on. Account → Apple Watch reads "Sleep and recovery. Workouts come from Strava."
- **Apple/Strava duplicates collapse once and stay collapsed (S1).** `collapseAppleStravaTwins` (`cross-source-twins.ts:317`) removes Apple copies of sessions Strava holds, in every week. Same-session rule `isSameSession`: start within 10 min and the same activity type or durations within 15% (the `cleanupDbDuplicates` constants). A slot only the Apple copy completed is bound to the Strava copy under its own key (`bindStravaToSlot`) in running, triathlon and HYROX, including a Strava copy in the neighbouring week or still awaiting review. When both copies completed slots, one keeps the completion. Removed ids are kept in `s.supersededGarminIds`. The collapse runs at launch and after each launch Strava sync (`src/data/apple-strava-twin-cleanup.ts`), and inside `matchAndAutoComplete` after any batch carrying Strava rows, so a late or paused twin collapses in the same session. The first post-sync pass sets `s.appleStravaTwinCleanupDone` and forces one `cleanupDbDuplicates` pass (90-day window). `matchAndAutoComplete` also drops incoming Apple rows whose session Strava holds (`dropAppleRowsWithStravaTwin`).
- **Apple-only users: pending activities processed after every Apple sync, 28-day lookback (S2; `70d2fb2`, `07fe4f0`).** `syncAppleHealth` ends with `processPendingAfterAppleSync` (`activitySync.ts:129`) on the zero-workout and the normal path, so this week's cross-training and unmatched runs no longer sit at `'__pending__'` with zero load until Review is tapped. The routing matches the Strava sync: a single same-day item is matched silently, a batch opens Activity Review at most once a day, and nothing opens while the wizard is up. The incremental window goes from 14 to 28 days through the shared `ACTIVITY_SYNC_LOOKBACK_DAYS` (`activity-sync-window.ts`), which Strava and Garmin also read. `matchAndAutoComplete` reports re-enrichment, Strava upgrades and stale-pending resolution as `changed` on every return path, so a sync that only adds heart rate to a matched workout re-renders (Strava and Garmin too). `mergeTimingMods` still does not run after Apple syncs (ISSUE-346).
- **Walks, hikes and rows never take a planned run slot; Apple workout types mapped (S3; `458b631`, `53f78b5`).** `findMatchingWorkout` treated the matcher's walk bucket as a run, so a walk, hike, row, kayak, paddleboard, wheelchair or golf session could complete any unrated same-day run slot, Long and Threshold included. One rule, `isActivityCompatibleWithSlot` (`matching.ts:81`), governs every auto-match (`matchItemToSlot`), the matching screen's pre-assignments and its taps; the walk class fills a cross slot by sport name only. Just-Track review offers no slots, HYROX review matches `wk.triWorkouts`, and `matchAndAutoComplete` builds no running week in HYROX. The walk class is costed as its own sport (`resolveSportForActivity`: rowing, hiking, kayaking, paddleboard; walking, golf and wheelchair keep walking). `HealthExtrasPlugin.swift` now names Apple HIIT, core training, pilates, dance, jump rope, boxing, kickboxing, martial arts, racket and ball sports, climbing, golf, skiing, snowboarding, skating, surfing, sailing, paddle and water sports, and `mapWorkoutType` maps each to the Garmin string for the same sport. HIIT becomes 'HIIT' (gym bucket, HYROX station matching), core training files as strength, and `SPORT_ALIASES` gains `dance` to dancing (Garmin DANCE too). Needs a native rebuild.
- **Plan changes are built from the current plan and replace, not stack (P1; `43a27e4`, `5f5b4d4`).** Running mode. Cross-training review and auto-process, the silent Tier-1 trim, ACWR Reduce, the excess-load adjustment, the GPS extra-run suggester, manual log, timing suggestions and the readiness recovery change size and write their change against `resolveWeekForPlanChanges` (`week-resolve.ts:182`): the canonical resolver with the plan layers only (generator arguments, accepted changes, moves). Illness, holiday and bridge layers stay display-only and scale a cut once at render. One mod per workout through `upsertWorkoutMod` (`src/workouts/workout-mods.ts`); a replaced mod is chained on `WorkoutMod.previousMod` and `removeWorkoutMods` restores it, so every undo keeps working. User Adjust mods are never cut by automatic changes, and holiday days and illness rest days are never offered. Timing Apply (`acceptTimingSuggestion`) writes the new type and RPE, keeps earlier cuts and works on moved sessions. The debrief Ease back / Keep ramping toggle opens on the choice the rollover would commit (`debriefAcwrInitialChoice`), so a carried Keep ramping survives Continue, with the line "Keep ramping carries over from last week." Excess records are scrubbed under every id an activity carried (`src/calculations/excess-records.ts`).
- **Downgrades step one pace category down, for every session type (P2; `0997f68`, Tristan's rule of 2026-10-05).** New canonical running ladder `src/constants/intensity-ladder.ts`: `RUN_PACE_LADDER` (recovery, easy, marathon pace, threshold, vo2; each type on the rung of its `TSS_RPE_BY_TYPE` row), `stepDownRunType` and `RUN_GENERATOR_RPE`. The day-after timing check now also covers marathon pace, float and progressive sessions. A steady long run one step down goes to recovery pace at the same distance, not marathon pace (ISSUE-328); a fast-finish long run goes to an easy long run at the same distance with the finish dropped. An accepted suggestion carries the generator RPE and a description at the new pace. In the cross-training suggester, progressive steps to easy (no more "N km @ MP"), an already-eased session steps one more rung instead of straight to easy, and a cut long run keeps type 'long', so a later light session does not cut it again. Prior-day tiers (50 / 75 / 100 / 125 TSS) and distance rules are unchanged.
- **The week total is derived, never stored (F6, audit B18; `0bd7dd8`).** `wk.actualTSS` was an add-only running total kept by 11 writers: re-review re-added items (60, 120, 180, 240), a last-week re-review wrote into the current week, and remove, reconcile drops and Discard never subtracted. `computeWeekActualTSS` (`fitness-model.ts:661`) returns the week's canonical Signal B (`computeWeekRawTSS`, the Plan Week Load bar's number before carry). Its readers: the holiday snapshot (`preHolidayWeeklyLoad`) and holiday-week average (bridge length, VDOT/FTP/CSS detraining), the week-end zone carry, the AI Coach running skeleton `actual_tss` (past and current week, null for future), the sleep hard-week insight (`recentWeeksActualTSS`, 4 weeks ending at the current week; it read the plan's final weeks), the main-view load surfaces and the Plan bar. `actualTSS` is gone from the `Week` type, a source-scan test rejects writes, and `loadState` strips stored values (`stripRetiredWeekTotals`).
- **Race taper targets reach 0.55 in race week (F7, ISSUE-317(a); `cb05a86`, tests `fb1ca07` and `ea80faf`).** `resolvePlannedWeekPhase` passes a 1-indexed race-taper position to `taperMultiplier`. The running part of the weekly target steps 0.75 / 0.65 / 0.55 over a 3-week taper and 0.70 / 0.55 over a 2-week taper (was 0.85 / 0.75 / 0.65 and 0.85 / 0.70); a 1-week taper keeps 0.70. The formula, 0.85 − 0.30 × position / taper length, is unchanged (Mujika & Padilla 2003; Bosquet et al. 2007). Running surfaces show it: the Plan week card, the Adjust-week strip and its modal, Load & Taper, the week debrief and the Stats forecast. The cross-training budget is still added unscaled, so in the `planned-week-target.test.ts` fixture (history median 400, 300 TSS of weekly cycling) race week reaches about 0.81 of a base week. Triathlon, cycling and HYROX compute the same ramp but show no weekly target; it reaches them only as the AI Coach `planned_week_tss` (Signal A). For a running user already in the taper, the live carry re-judges earlier taper weeks against the lower targets, so carry can appear in the current week.
- **Onboarding Strava and Apple syncs wait for the athlete's sex (F8; `bb9577c`, `fb8fd3e`).** The connect-data step runs before the sex question, so with no sex from Strava or HealthKit the post-connect 28-day sync, the OAuth-return backfill and a mid-wizard Apple sync stamped rows with the male β 1.92, about 1.23× high once a woman answered. `src/data/trimp-sex-gate.ts` holds them (`isTrimpSexPending`) until the answer is final: for triathlon, cycling and HYROX when about-you is left; for running and fitness once a sex is known or schedule is answered; Just-Track never holds. `releaseHeldTrimpSyncs` runs at each wizard step change, at onboarding completion, on the mid-plan Return to plan button, after the Strava profile prefill and after the HealthKit profile seed. The tri past-race Strava scan waits for released syncs. Rows cached before this change keep their stamp (ISSUE-318).
- **In-app GPS runs and Mark as Done count as load, once (M3, audit B9; `170ef1b`, `46b678d`, `2223f4a`, `ec595c0`).** A GPS recording and a run-card Mark as Done write an activity record, a `guided-` `GarminActual`: GPS at the recording's start, recorded time (pauses excluded) and distance; Mark as Done at the planned duration and distance at the rated RPE, stamped at local noon of the planned day and never later than now. HYROX run Mark as Done and station quick done do the same at `estimatedDurationMin`. A later Strava, Apple or Garmin copy supersedes the record in place when it is the same recording (start within 4 h, duration within 15%) or falls on a Mark as Done record's local day (0.5 to 2.0× duration); both checks search every plan week. A Mark as Done on another day merges automatically only for a run first seen once its week is past. A synced activity of another sport never supersedes or drops an in-app record (`isSameSportAsInApp`), and on a double-run day the reconcile no longer unticks a ticked run for another slot's activity. Non-run cards and future-week cards keep rating-only Mark as Done. Gym quick done for the beginner, novice and returning templates still logs 0 load (ISSUE-343).

## 2026-10-05 — Load accounting batch 1 (audit lanes A, F and M)

Fixes from the 2026-09 load-accounting audit, re-validated against this branch before any code changed (`docs/audits/2026-09-load-accounting/REVALIDATION.md`; the audit pack is untracked and exists only in Tristan's local working tree until he decides whether to commit it). Merged on `fix/load-accounting`: lane A (Apple) in `443b561`, lane M in `3ee615c`, lane F (load) in `d4588bd`. All unit-tested, none device-verified. Follow-ups and open decisions are ISSUE-317 to ISSUE-329.

- **Apple Health asks for heart rate, and physiology keys days by local date (audit D4, X4; `c00f8f7`, `c8961a3`).** No HealthKit request included `heartRate` since `ae0545e`, so every Apple workout was costed on duration alone. `heartRate` is now in `CORE_READ_TYPES` (the connect flow and every physiology sync). The workout sync also asks once before its first HR read, guarded by the new `appleHeartRatePermissionRequested` flag, so users connected under an earlier build see one re-prompt. Physiology days are now device-local dates (`src/utils/local-date.ts`). They were the UTC date of a GMT string, a day off for UTC+ mornings and UTC- evenings. A night stays on its local wake date, pre-midnight part included (it used to be dropped), with one sleep source per night (a staged source wins). Reads pass `limit: 0` (previously 1000 quantity and 4000 sleep samples, oldest first, which cut off the newest days) over a window aligned to local midnight, and recent days refresh newest-wins instead of freezing at the first sync of the day. Overlapping iPhone and Watch steps count once. Apple never overwrites Garmin or manual sleep: `PhysiologyDayEntry.appleValues` records Apple's gap-fills, and Garmin writers release a field through `releaseAppleOwnership` (`src/data/physiology-provenance.ts`).
- **Weekly load targets follow deload and taper weeks (audit A10, A11; `6769c78`).** New canonical helper `src/calculations/planned-week-target.ts` (`computePlannedWeekTarget`, `computeCurrentWeekCarry`, `resolvePlannedWeekPhase`). Each surface used to build its own target from `wk.ph` with no taper position: deload weeks kept their base/build/peak target, every taper week targeted 0.85×, and Stats alone used 1-indexed positions, so following the plan exactly read "under plan". Deload status now comes from the generator's own inputs (running: `isDeloadWeek` by ability band, or `forceDeload`; tri/HYROX: every 4th non-taper week). Only the plan's last contiguous 'taper' run is the race taper, at its 0-indexed position (0.85 / 0.75 / 0.65 over 3 weeks). Continuous-mode and double-periodisation 'taper' weeks are recovery weeks and take the tier deload row. `computeDecayedCarry` now scores each past week against its own target, which removes the phantom carry on the first taper Monday (83 TSS in the regression test). Carry applies to the current week only, so Load & Taper no longer shows it on future weeks. Every caller (Plan card and Adjust strip, Load & Taper, debrief, excess adjustment, ACWR projection, week-advance settle, launch carry-over, daily coach, Stats forecast) routes through the helper, and an anchor test blocks new raw callers. The tri/HYROX deload rule moved unchanged to `plan_engine.ts:isFourWeekCycleDeloadWeek`. Batch 2 moved the taper position to 1-indexed, so race week reaches 0.55 (Tristan, 2026-10-05; see the batch 2 entry above, ISSUE-317(a)).
- **Signal A counts each activity once, at its own sport's runSpec (audit B3, X7, X9, B20; `1ed0fbe`, `02f1383`, `3e699ed`).** Synced cross-training entered Signal A at full weight through its `garminActuals` twin, and overflow `unspentLoadItems` were added on top (60-min ride: A 98 vs B 60 in the regression test). New `listWeekSignalAEntries` returns one entry per activity and `computeWeekTSS` sums it. The sport is what the device recorded (`resolveActualSport` / `resolveAdhocSport`, `cross-training/activities.ts`), never the plan slot it filled. `unspentLoadItems` no longer count as load anywhere (A, B, daily B, the Load & Taper breakdown, the legacy main-view chart), and the breakdown no longer adds surplus run slices on top of the matched run. Sleep daily load, strain, and the Rolling Load and Strain activity lists count each activity once after a Strava upgrade, which keeps the twin's `garmin-<id>` key but rewrites its `garminId` (sleep load read 120 vs 60). Removing an activity drops its excess-load records, including any written under its pre-upgrade id. The coach fitness trend compares Signal B with Signal B (`computeSameSignalCtlHistory`). The running CTL-gap re-anchor values planned gym at the strength runSpec, so a fully completed week with strength no longer reads as behind (ratio 0.954 in the test) and no longer cuts next week's volume. Running CTL history shifts down once for cross-trainers.
- **ACWR: unrecorded days are missing, not rest, for athletes with no load seed (audit B1, B17; `83ecd5f`).** Without `s.signalBBaseline`, `computeRollingLoadRatio` filled days no plan week covers with 0: steady training read 1.87 'high' on plan day 14, the week advance cut week-3 quality, and the ease-back L_max was undersized. Any archive entry also switched the 14-day guard off (4.00 'high' from day 0 for no-history Strava users and for plans rebuilt after 5 days). The guard now counts 14 observed days across the live plan and archives (`ROLLING_ACWR_MIN_OBSERVED_DAYS`), and chronic is built from the athlete's own observed whole weeks. `computeACWR` reports 'unknown' instead of falling back to the zero-started weekly EMA. The Rolling Load drill-down reads `computeReadinessACWR`, so its numbers match the Readiness card, and its chart draws recorded days only. The Load Ratio weekly trend (`computeWeeklyAcwrHistory`, moved into `fitness-model.ts`) bias-corrects the unseeded EMA. The session-generator caption reads readiness with the Home ring's history depth and tier ACWR ceiling. The ratio is unchanged for seeded athletes; their Rolling Load page now matches the Readiness card and draws recorded days only.
- **Planned check-ins and replaced runs are not load; the Plan tab prices runs like the day target (audit B8, B11, B2 remainder; `8fa3acc`).** (1) A picked post-deload check-in (`benchmark-` id) counted as done load at once and again when the run synced. New `isPlannedAdhocId` (`src/workouts/planned-adhoc.ts`) names the planned prefixes `adhoc-`, `holiday-` and `benchmark-` once. Every load reader skips them, `resolveWeekWorkouts` renders check-ins as 'Added' cards, the popup stops once a check-in is chosen, and re-picking replaces an undone pick instead of stacking. (2) A fully replaced run ('0km (replaced)') priced as a 1-TSS training day through the 1-minute duration floor, which deflated `perSessionAvg` and produced "Big session today" from steps. New `computePlannedWorkoutSignalBTSS` prices 'replaced' and 'skipped' at 0. Tri/HYROX drop 'skipped' sessions; their 'replaced' (swapped, still to do) stays priced. A running skip recorded only as a rating stays priced, because the CTL-gap adherence reads the same context. (3) The Plan-tab per-workout planned TSS (`planCardPlannedTSS`) reads the same pricer as the day target (easy and long at 0.92 TSS/min, was 0.65), so on-plan easy runs no longer read about 140% in red on the card and in activity detail. Activity detail's no-HR estimate reads the rating from the activity's own week.
- **Female training load no longer reads about 19% low (audit B12; `499bc31`, `8c2955f`).** The iTRIMP-to-TSS normaliser hard-coded the male Banister β (1.92) while the producers used 1.67 for women, so an hour at threshold scored about 81 TSS. The normaliser now uses the athlete's own β (`trimp.ts:getBeta`). For women with a personal normaliser, CTL/ATL, ACWR, strain, weekly load and cross-training cuts rise about 21 to 25%; male and unset profiles are unchanged. One resolver, `trimp.ts:resolveBiologicalSex`, feeds every producer and the normaliser, including mid-wizard: sex used to reach `s.biologicalSex` only at plan initialisation, so the onboarding Strava sync and backfill stamped a woman's history with the male β. The module normaliser is bound to live state (`bindAthleteNormalizerToState`), so an Account HR edit or an in-session physiology/LT sync takes effect without a relaunch. Still open: Strava rows the server already cached with the male β read about 1.23× high for existing Strava-onboarded women (ISSUE-318); the 15000 fallback has no sex-specific derivation and stays sex-neutral (ISSUE-319); the onboarding connect-step sync, which runs before the sex question, is held until the sex is final since batch 2 (F8, entry above).
- **Fast-finish long run back on the long-run day (audit X5; `24a6649`).** The fast-finish long run is `t: 'progressive'` and the scheduler found the long run only by `t === 'long'`, so every peak week put it on Tuesday, pushed a quality session to Saturday and left Sunday without a long run. The generator now stamps optional `Workout.longRun` on the long-run slot in every variant, and `isLongRun()` (`src/workouts/long-run.ts`) reads it in the scheduler and every long-run rule: timing-check sub-ladder, cross-training Replace exclusion and no-downgrade rule, long-run reduce and race priority, injury long-run bans and the graduated-return rule, skip warning, skip carry and long-run TIM charge, matching screen, GPS pace tiebreak, drift note trigger. Title, description and load are unchanged. Tri/HYROX unaffected.
- **Launch repair no longer inflates VDOT for non-running users (audit X11; `5f6584c`).** `loadState` ran the 2026-04-13 "one-time" s.v repair on every launch, resetting s.v toward s.iv whenever s.v < 0.9 × s.iv. Only the running init writes s.iv, so tri, HYROX and cycling users carried the store default 50, and any run VDOT under 45 was pushed up on every load (44 to 47.6, or straight to 50 in week 1). In weeks labelled taper (race taper, continuous-mode block deload, double-periodisation recovery) and run-blocking-injury weeks `refreshBlendedFitness` skips its write-back, so the inflated value stuck (the implementer's probe forecast a 70.3 run leg about 11 min fast). The repair's root cause was fixed in the same April commit, so the repair was removed rather than gated. s.v is now written by `refreshBlendedFitness`, the detraining paths (`advanceWeekToToday`, `showWelcomeBackModal`, which has no caller today, and the holiday return `showHolidayWelcomeBack`), the one-time short-holiday repair at launch (`main.ts`, guarded by `_holidayRepairDone`) and plan init (`initialization.ts`, `initialization.triathlon.ts`, `ui/events.ts`). Full list with line numbers in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (Key Types, VDOT/fitness).
- **Tests**: 25 new or extended test files for this batch, all passing (listed per feature in `docs/FEATURES.md`). The lane F merge also raised one `coach-tools.test.ts` timeout to 20 s, because its dynamic import of the coach context builder can exceed the 5 s default under full-suite load. Full suite at `d4588bd`: 3777 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed.

## 2026-10-05 — Onboarding: Continue says why it is blocked when a race date, time or PB is typed

Tristan reported: "if you manually put in a time, you can't progress onto the next page when inputting a race". Five steps each had their own cause and shared one root problem: input refused with no visible reason, or a lost tap. Commits `16cca9e` and `0dec641` (review follow-up). No plan logic or week ranges changed.

- **Race target, custom date**: a date under the distance floor (marathon 8 weeks, half 4 weeks) or past 52 weeks was refused only through the native validation bubble, which fades on desktop and may never show in WKWebView. The reason now sits under the field and the Continue hint states the rule. The picker's min/max come from the same `calculateWeeksUntil` check, a refused or cleared date is removed from state, and the field reacts to typing as well as the picker. Accepting a date no longer re-renders the step, which tore down the iOS wheel picker.
- **HYROX setup**: once a previous time is typed, its format is required. The reason now sits next to Continue, a tap scrolls to the missing field (usually the format pills), and the amber prompt updates live. "1:12" is no longer stored as a 72-second finish: anything under 8 run legs × the existing 3:10/km HYROX run floor (`HYROX_FINISH_FLOOR_SEC`, 25:20) asks for h:mm:ss. A field that stops parsing clears the stored time.
- **Triathlon past race**: the missing field is named above Continue and in its card, which scrolls into view. Time boxes use the digit keypad. Splits read as typed: a sprint run "24:50" is mm:ss (it became 24 h 50 min) and a swim "0:32:00" is accepted. No distance pill is pre-selected, because a past race is often a different distance.
- **Manual entry**: Continue no longer misses its tap while a PB field is focused. The blur inserted the experience notice above the button, which moved about 125 px mid-tap. Unreadable PB text is flagged instead of dropped, and "0:00" is not stored.
- **Review**: Return saves an inline PB edit, a readable draft lights Build, and Build saves it first. An unreadable draft shows "Use mm:ss, e.g. 22:30, to continue." (h:mm:ss for half and marathon) while typing, in place of a prompt to add the PB the user just typed (`0dec641`).
- Triathlon and cycling setup date fields also react to typing.
- **Tests** (`src/ui/wizard/steps/`): `race-target-custom-date` (8), `hyrox-setup-continue-gate` (13), `tri-past-race-continue` (9), `manual-entry-continue` (5), `review-pb-draft` (5), `setup-date-input-events` (2), all passing. The race-date path was checked in the iPhone 17 Pro simulator (Safari, against a harness of the fixed step); the rest awaits device verification (`docs/DEVICE_TESTS.md`).

## 2026-09-15 — HYROX race projection silently dropped its adherence factor

Found by a multi-agent audit and verified by hand before fixing.

- **Defect**: `computeAdherence` in `race-projection.hyrox.ts` read `(wk.garminActuals ?? []).length`, but `garminActuals` is `Record<string, GarminActual>` (state.ts:616), not an array. `.length` was `undefined`, `Math.min(undefined, planned)` produced `NaN`, and the consumer's `adherence < 0.95` is `false` for `NaN`, so the up-to-4% adherence debit never applied. A `const wk: any` cast on the line above is what hid it from `tsc`.
- **User-visible effect**: a HYROX athlete from week 4 on saw a race-day projection that never moved however many sessions they skipped. The factor multiplies every discipline and feeds the "Projected -X min by race day" line in `hyrox/forecast-view.ts`.
- **Fix**: `Object.keys(wk.garminActuals ?? {}).length`, dropped the `any` cast (typecheck still clean without it), and guarded the consumer on `Number.isFinite` so a non-finite adherence can never silently skip the debit again.
- **Tests**: added 4 cases to `race-projection.hyrox.test.ts`; there was previously no coverage of this factor at all. Confirmed 2 of the 4 genuinely fail when the bug is reintroduced. The other 2 pass either way (a NaN adherence also omits the factor) and are documentation, not guards.
- Suite 3519 passed / 0 failed; typecheck and `lint:ui` clean.
- **Build 29 is unaffected** and remains in review. This ships in build 30.

## 2026-09-10 — Fixed wall-clock rot in adaptive-recovery tests (15 failures)

Found while gating a fresh App Store build: `src/calculations/adaptive-recovery.test.ts` had 15 failing tests. **Not a product regression** — `adaptive-recovery.ts` was unmodified.

- **Root cause**: `pruneImpactLog` (adaptive-recovery.ts:348) and `backfillHistoricalImpacts` (:659) both cut against `todayIso()` with a 90-day window (`IMPACT_LOG_MAX_DAYS`), and neither accepts an injectable clock. The test file anchored its fixtures to a hardcoded `2026-05-01` / `2026-04-01`, which by 2026-09-10 are 132 and 162 days old, so every fixture entry was pruned on insert and the assertions saw an empty log. These tests were a time bomb that fired 90 days after they were written.
- **Fix**: re-anchored `isoOffset`'s default and the 11 per-test `today` constants to `new Date()`, changed the one date assertion to `isoOffset(0)`, and moved the two `backfillHistoricalImpacts` fixtures to `isoOffset(-30)`.
- **Latent false pass fixed too**: "skips sessions with no usable post-session physiology" asserted `skipped: 1` and passed, but was being skipped on the *age* check, never reaching the physiology check it claims to test. It now exercises the intended path.
- A prior session had already patched exactly one of these tests with the same `new Date()` fix and left a comment naming the cause, but did not sweep the other 15.
- Suite now 3,515 passed / 0 failed / 28 skipped; typecheck and `lint:ui` clean.

## 2026-08-04 — ISSUE-315: cross-account leak on the same device (sign-out cleared disk, not memory)

Tristan signed up a fresh test account on a phone holding his real account; the new account inherited the old plan. The 2026-07-26 sign-out fix cleared localStorage but the page never reloads, so the in-memory store and all background sync timers survive the account boundary — `savePlanSettings()` reads `getState()` and upserts under whoever is signed in, so the first post-sign-in `saveState()` (425 call sites) re-persisted and *uploaded* account 1's state as account 2's backup, re-stamping the owner.

- **Fix: hard reload at every account boundary** (`main.ts` auth listener). SIGNED_OUT → clear caches + `location.reload()` (auth wall); SIGNED_IN for a different user → owner-mismatch wipe + reload (clean bootstrap: restore new user's backup or wizard). Kills memory, timers, in-flight syncs. Loop-safe via the launchedUserId duplicate-suppression.
- Account-deletion confirmation survives the reload via a one-shot `mosaic_deletion_toast` flag (`account-legal.ts` sets it, `auth-view.ts` shows it on the wall).
- Server residue: accounts created during the buggy window can hold another account's snapshot in `user_plan_settings` — purge manually.
- Suite: 3499 green; the 15 failures are all the pre-existing `adaptive-recovery.test.ts` WIP whose fixed-date fixtures age past the real-clock 90-day prune (was 10 on 07-26, +5 as more days elapsed — the documented 2026-06-22 failure mode, unrelated to this change). NOT device-verified.

## 2026-07-26 — Account-required auth: kill "continue without an account", fix sign-out data leak

Login / logout was unreliable and a signed-out phone showed the previous account's plan. Root cause was two conflated "no account" mechanisms plus a per-device cache that was never invalidated at an account boundary. Decision (Tristan): go account-required, no guest.

- **Removed the "Continue without an account" button** (`auth-view.ts`) and its handler. That button set `mosaic_simulator_mode` — a **dev/testing flag** that short-circuits bootstrap before any Supabase session, so every `!isSimulatorMode()`-gated feature (sync, tri history, Strava, DB reads) silently no-ops. It was never a real guest mode. Simulator mode survives as a console-only dev flag (`localStorage.setItem('mosaic_simulator_mode','1')`); no UI entry.
- **Bootstrap is now account-required** (`main.ts`). No session → render the auth wall; removed the silent `signInAnonymously()` fallback and the offline anonymous-retry (`scheduleOfflineAuthRetry`, deleted). Returning users are unaffected — `getSession()` reads a cached session from localStorage and works offline, so they still launch straight in. ISSUE-228 offline resilience now lives at the wall: the auth form catches network errors and shows a retryable message rather than a dead screen, and never mints a throwaway user.
- **Sign-out now clears the per-device cache.** The `SIGNED_OUT` listener (`main.ts`) runs `clearState()` + `setLocalStateOwner(null)` + `resetGarminCache()` + `resetStravaCache()` for *every* sign-out path (button, forced invalid-token logout, account deletion), then renders the auth wall. The server (`user_plan_settings`, keyed by `user_id`) stays the per-person source of truth and restores on the next sign-in. This is what makes data follow the person, not the phone. The account-view sign-out handler (`account-view.ts`) was hardened with a local-scope fallback for network hiccups and no longer double-renders.
- **`getValidSession` no longer mints an anonymous user as a last resort** (`supabaseClient.ts`). It throws `SESSION_EXPIRED` (every caller already catches it). Previously a background sync firing right after sign-out could create a throwaway anon account and yank the just-signed-out user back into the app — re-breaking logout.
- **Account-deletion clear fixed** (`account-legal.ts`): was `localStorage.removeItem('marathonSimulatorState')` (hardcoded key, left the owner stamp). Now `clearState()` + `setLocalStateOwner(null)`.
- Guest plumbing (`isGuestAccount`, guest banner, "Save your account" upgrade) is left in place but dormant for *new* users — `is_anonymous` is never true under account-required. It still fires for *existing* anonymous users, which is what makes the migration path below work.
- **Migration soft gate for existing guests** (`account-required-notice.ts`, new). Existing anonymous users get a one-time launch modal: "Mosaic now uses accounts. Save your history before you lose it." Because upgrade-in-place (`updateUser`) only works while the anonymous session is alive, a guest who reinstalls / clears storage / signs out *before* upgrading orphans their data (backed up under a now-dead anonymous `user_id`). "Save my account" opens the guest-upgrade flow (preserves the `user_id` and all data); "Not now" dismisses and the passive banner keeps nudging. Gated to guests with real data (any completed workout), once-only via `s.accountRequiredNoticeSeen` set on create (not dismiss) + a module-level session guard, mirroring the feature-reveal once-only rule. Fires from `launchApp` after `isGuestAccount` is refreshed. New users never see it.
- tsc + `lint:ui` clean; full suite green except 10 pre-existing `adaptive-recovery.test.ts` failures from concurrent recovery-model WIP (that module imports none of the auth files). **NOT device-verified** — needs a TestFlight build to confirm sign-in / sign-out / fresh-account-clean and the guest-migration modal on a phone.

## 2026-07-26 — Branded auth emails + signup redirect landing on `localhost:3000`

A tester's confirmation email arrived as the stock Supabase template from `noreply@mail.app.supabase.io`, and clicking the link produced `http://localhost:3000/#error=access_denied&error_code=otp_expired`.

- **Redirect diagnosis (no code fix, dashboard config).** `auth-view.ts:303` requests `emailRedirectTo: 'https://mosaicrunning.run/auth-success.html'`, but Supabase only honours a redirect that is in the Redirect URLs allowlist and otherwise falls back to **Site URL**. The browser landed on `http://localhost:3000` — a string that appears nowhere in this repo, and not Vite's port (5173) — so it can only be the stock default Site URL. Fix is Dashboard → Authentication → URL Configuration: Site URL `https://mosaicrunning.run`, allowlist `https://mosaicrunning.run/**` and `http://localhost:5173/**`.
- **The `otp_expired` was a second click, not a broken flow.** `auth.users` shows the account confirmed and signed in 2m04s after the email was sent. Confirmation tokens are single-use: the first click redeemed it and dumped the user on the dead `localhost:3000`, which looks broken, so the link got clicked again and the spent token returned `access_denied`.
- **Branded templates**, `supabase/templates/{confirmation,recovery,email_change}.html` — table-based, fully inline CSS, 600px, bulletproof button, preheader text. Visual language mirrors `public/auth-success.html` (same `#f9f9f7` canvas, white card, 20px radius, `MOSAIC` text wordmark) so the email and the landing page read as one piece. Neutral near-black button, no accent colour.
- `email_change.html` exists because `supabase.auth.updateUser({ email, password })` (`auth-view.ts:289`, `save-account-overlay.ts:122`) is the **guest-to-account upgrade** path, which fires the email-change template rather than confirmation. Its copy is deliberately generic: a guest upgrading has no previous address, so Supabase's default "confirm the update of your email from X to Y" wording reads as nonsense there. No magic-link or password-reset template — the app calls neither `signInWithOtp` nor `resetPasswordForEmail`.
- `supabase/config.toml` gained `[auth.email.template.*]` blocks as the checked-in source of truth, but those apply to **local development only**. Hosted projects take templates from the Dashboard or `PATCH /v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth`, so `npm run push:auth-emails` (`scripts/push-auth-emails.mjs`) pushes them via the Management API, touching only the `mailer_*` fields. It refuses to push a template missing `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`. Deliberately not `supabase config push` — config.toml does not mirror every remote auth setting, so a full push can reset the ones it omits.
- Custom SMTP via **Resend**, sending as `Mosaic <noreply@mosaicrunning.run>`. `npm run push:auth-emails -- --smtp` sets `smtp_host/port/user/pass/sender_name/admin_email` (`smtp.resend.com:587`, username the literal `resend`, password the API key, per Resend's SMTP docs). Opt-in and separate from the template push because rotating credentials should be deliberate, and because pushing SMTP before the domain is verified in Resend makes every auth email fail silently. The key is read from `RESEND_API_KEY` and never checked in.
- **Applied in the Supabase dashboard**: Site URL `http://localhost:3000` → `https://mosaicrunning.run`, and `https://mosaicrunning.run/**` + `http://localhost:5173/**` added to the Redirect URLs allowlist. Note the allowlist already contained a bare `https://mosaicrunning.run` entry, which matches only that exact URL and therefore never matched the `/auth-success.html` path. The wildcard is what fixes it.
- **DNS (Namecheap, `dns1/dns2.registrar-servers.com`)**: Resend had been sitting in `Failed` for 2 months because only 1 of its 3 records was ever published. A malformed leftover record (`send._domainkey.onboarding` holding an SPF *value*, i.e. DKIM host crossed with SPF value) was rewritten into the real DKIM record: TXT `resend._domainkey` = the 216-char `p=MIGf…IDAQAB` key, verified as a well-formed 1024-bit RSA key via `openssl pkey` before publishing and confirmed live via `dig`. The SPF TXT on `send` was already correct.
- **The MX gap was not a UI bug**: Namecheap removes MX/MXE from the Advanced DNS type dropdown entirely while Mail Settings is "Private Email" (option values skip 8/9). Creating any MX requires switching Mail Settings to "Custom MX", which drops `mx1/mx2.privateemail.com` unless re-added. The switch happened with the inbox records carried over as editable rows, the `send` → `feedback-smtp.eu-west-1.amazonses.com` (prio 10) MX added, and `dig` confirms both root MX (inbox intact) and send MX resolve. **Resend domain status: Verified** ("ready to send emails") after 2 months of Failed.
- Resend API key `supabase-auth-smtp` created (Sending access, scoped to mosaicrunning.run). The key never entered the agent context: Resend's copy button put it on the clipboard, and the push ran as `RESEND_API_KEY=$(pbpaste)` with a format guard, alongside `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=$(security find-generic-password -s "Supabase CLI" -w)` (the CLI's keychain token — no new Supabase token needed). **Push complete and verified via Management API read-back**: `smtp_host smtp.resend.com`, port `"587"` (API requires a string, script fixed), sender `Mosaic <noreply@mosaicrunning.run>`, all three subjects + templates live. Auth emails now send branded from the Mosaic domain. NOT yet tested with a real signup.
- `public/auth-success.html` now reads the URL hash: on `#error=…` (e.g. `otp_expired` from a second click on a single-use link) it swaps the green tick for a neutral state explaining the link was already used and the account is most likely confirmed. Previously it showed "Email confirmed" unconditionally, including to users whose click had just failed.
- **Tester 404 on verify, root cause = domain/project split**: `mosaicrunning.run` (www) is attached to the **mosaic-landing** Vercel project (`~/Documents/mosaic-landing`, no git remote, deployed via CLI), while `auth-success.html` only existed in the app project (`mosaic-theta-lac.vercel.app`). So the email link 404'd on the landing site. Before the allowlist fix this was masked by the localhost:3000 fallback. Fix: copied the hardened `auth-success.html` into mosaic-landing and deployed to production (`vercel deploy --prod`) after hashing local vs live files to confirm the working tree matched what was deployed (no unintended changes shipped). Verified live: 200 + error branch present, landing root unchanged. TRAP: the app's `public/` is NOT served on mosaicrunning.run — any page referenced by `emailRedirectTo` or other absolute mosaicrunning.run URLs must exist in the mosaic-landing project.

## 2026-06-22 — Pre-onboard sessions resurfaced as "Missed" once week 1 rolled into the past

- A user who onboarded on a Sunday (week 1 = 15–21 Jun) saw the whole of week 1 flagged "Missed" the next day. Root cause: `dropPreOnboardSessions` (`src/ui/workout-status.ts`) only suppressed pre-onboard days while the onboarding week was the *current* week (`if (viewWeek !== currentWeek) return workouts`). The moment week 1 became a past week, the dropped Mon–Sat sessions reappeared — and `plan-view.ts` marks every day of a past week as past → "Missed". The reduced-partial-first-week semantics evaporated overnight.
- Fix: removed the current-week guard. `firstTrackedDow` is already week-agnostic (returns the onboard-day offset only for the week containing `planCreatedAt`, and 0 for every other week), so the drop now self-restricts to the onboarding week whether it is current or past. Pre-onboard days were never schedulable, so they now render as empty Rest rows in retrospect, never "Missed". The headline Sessions/Distance/Load counts derive from the same dropped list, so they stay correct too. Applies to running, triathlon, and HYROX (all three resolvers call this helper).
- `plan-adherence.ts` already called `firstTrackedDow` per-week (not gated to current), so the pro-rata denominator was already correct. Tests: inverted the old "no-op for any week other than the current one" assertion and added a non-onboarding-week no-op case. tsc + 67 status/adherence tests + 236 UI tests green. NOT device-verified.



- Three tests failed only because the wall-clock moved past their hardcoded fixtures; the production windowing was correct. `adaptive-recovery.test.ts` "log-space aggregation" anchored its sessions to a fixed `2026-05-01`, so its two `-40`/`-46`-day outliers (the entire signal pushing `k` above default) aged ~92/98 real days old and got dropped by `logSessionImpact`'s 90-day `pruneImpactLog` (which uses the real system clock, no injectable override). The two `sleep-insights.test.ts` cases dated nights `2026-06-13/14/15`, now 7–9 real days old, so `computeRecoveryScore`'s intended `>3`-day staleness gate returned `hasData:false` / `score:null`.
- Fix is date-relative fixtures, not a code change: the log-space test anchors `today = new Date()` (offsets stay inside the prune window, fit math unchanged); the sleep tests use a new `isoDaysAgo(n)` helper for nights 0–2 days ago. Both the 90-day prune and the 3-day staleness gate are intended production behaviour — verified there is no windowing regression.
- The test-3 "received object" error was just `score: null` from the documented `noData` return (typeof null === 'object'), not a code-path bug.

## 2026-06-22 — Manual Apple Health "Sync" pulls full history (recover training without resetting)

An Apple Watch user whose rides/swims/runs never backfilled could only fix it by **resetting** — which throws away their plan — because the manual "Sync" button ran the same cheap 14-day incremental window the background syncs use, while only a reset cleared `appleHistoryFetched` to force the full re-pull.

- The Account → Apple Watch **"Sync"** button now pulls the **full history** (`syncAppleHealth({ forceFullHistory: true })`): it clears `appleHistoryFetched` + `appleDeepHistoryFetched` so the full backfill window + deep (>52w) pull re-run, then re-derive bike/swim/run benchmarks from real activity. The non-destructive equivalent of a reset.
- Automatic launch / foreground / observer syncs are unchanged — they stay on the cheap 14-day incremental path. Only the explicit tap forces the full pull. Dedup (the `apple-<id>` matched key) makes re-pulling existing workouts a no-op, and `aggregateAppleHistory` recomputes from scratch, so forcing it is idempotent.
- Why it matters: this is what lets the forecast derive his bike speed / CSS / run VDOT from his watch instead of falling back to a manual past-race anchor and the cycling-inflated watch VO2max. Surfaced while debugging a real triathlete whose Ironman forecast leaned on manual entry because his activity history hadn't ingested (Endurance read S 0 · B 0 · R 0).
- `appleHealthSync.ts` (`forceFullHistory` option), `account-view.ts` (`btn-sync-apple`). **Native HealthKit path — NOT device-verified.** DEVICE_TESTS Tier 1 item added.

## 2026-06-18 — Apple Watch triathletes now pull history (Apple → Supabase upload)

- Bug: an Apple-Watch-only triathlete saw swim/bike/run = 0 sessions, 0 across "Recent weeks", and a flat per-discipline CTL chart on the Stats screen even though the on-device Apple Health sync ran fine. Root cause: the **triathlon** fitness pipeline (`deriveTriBenchmarksFromHistory` / per-discipline CTL / `fitnessHistory` / CSS / FTP / PBs) derives **exclusively** from the Supabase `garmin_activities` table via `loadActivitiesFromDB` (main.ts:482), with a Strava-only backfill fallback. Strava and Garmin both write to that table (edge function / webhook); Apple Health was the **only** source that never did — its workouts live on-device in HealthKit and only ever reached local `s.wks[].garminActuals` (which the tri pipeline doesn't read) plus the running-shaped `historicWeeklyTSS`/`ctlBaseline` aggregates. So the tri pipeline saw zero activities and stayed slider-based.
- Fix: new `src/data/appleActivityUpload.ts` → `uploadAppleActivitiesToDB(rows)`. When the Apple sync converts HealthKit workouts to `GarminActivityRow[]`, it now upserts them into `garmin_activities` (source `'apple'`), making Apple a first-class DB source the tri pipeline reads — identical to how Strava's rows reach it. Wired into `syncAppleHealth` (backfill + incremental) and `syncAppleHealthDeepHistory` (appleHealthSync.ts).
- Bulletproofing: **idempotent** (upsert on the unique `apple-<sourceId>-<start>` `garmin_id`; later HR/power/route enrichment upgrades the row in place); **canonical-source safe** (an `apple-` id can never collide with a `strava-`/Garmin id, and any Apple row within ±10 min of an existing non-Apple row is suppressed so a Strava+Apple user never double-counts — Strava wins, matching the `sync-activities` window); **user-scoped** via the `garmin_activities_own` RLS policy (`user_id = auth.uid()`, works for anonymous sessions); **non-fatal** (auth/table/network failure warns and no-ops, and a failed dedup read skips the upload rather than risk a blind double-count).
- Same-launch population: added an Apple branch to the tri-init DB-empty fallback (main.ts) mirroring the existing Strava one — if the DB is empty and Apple Health is connected, `await syncAppleHealth()` (which now uploads), then reload `activityLog`, so per-discipline fitness derives on this launch instead of the next.
- On-device diagnostic: `syncAppleHealth` now stamps `_lastWorkoutSyncDiag` (`getLastAppleWorkoutDiag()`) — `bXX pulled=N hrEnriched=M uploaded=K window=Nd first=X`, or `pulled=0 … HealthKit returned no workouts`, or `threw: …`. Surfaced as a muted line under Account → Apple Watch (refreshes on the Sync button). TestFlight has no console, so this tells apart the two failure modes that both render as "0 sessions": HealthKit returning no workouts (permission/empty) vs workouts pulled but not reaching the DB. Temporary debug surface; remove once confirmed on a phone.
- Guard: `src/data/appleActivityUpload.test.ts` (7 tests for the ±10 min canonical-dedup, inclusive boundary, before/after neighbour, unparseable-start). Full suite 3503 green, tsc + lint:ui clean. ❌ Not device-verified (HealthKit is device-only; no-op on web).

## 2026-06-17 — Accumulated time-on-feet softens the run durability cap (user idea)

- A user suggested time on feet is important the way TSS is. Investigation: the metabolic side is already captured by canonical TSS (duration × rate), so adding it as a parallel load would double-count and break the Load Currency Law; it is not a form of leg load either (leg load is eccentric muscle *damage*, time-on-feet is sub-damaging connective-tissue *adaptation*). The one genuine gap was that the long-run durability cap read only the single *peak* long run, ignoring repeated long-run exposure.
- `applyLongRunCap` (`run-durability.ts`) now also reads `qualifyingLongRunCount` (runs ≥ 70% of the distance threshold in the 12-week window) and softens the peak-shortfall penalty: `penalty = MAX_PENALTY × peakShortfall × (1 − consistencyCredit)`, `consistencyCredit = min(1, count / 8)` (target ≈ one long run every 10 days, Pfitzinger). Softening can only lower the penalty, never raise it. Self-consistent: a short-peak sparse runner earns zero credit (no run can qualify below the peak) and keeps the full penalty; full credit zeroes it. Decision shape per Tristan: soften the peak (not blend/replace), Pfitzinger 10-day target, display in the durability drill-down + an injury-risk note.
- New helpers `getRunDurationsSec` / `countQualifyingLongRuns` / `getQualifyingLongRunCount` share one traversal so peak and exposure never disagree. All four `applyLongRunCap` call sites updated (3 in `blended-fitness.ts`, 1 in `initialization.ts`).
- Display: the Forecast durability drill-down (`forecast-chip-detail-view.ts → pageDurability`) adds a "Long runs (time on feet)" bar + count-vs-target row + a context line explaining the softening; the injury-risk view (`injury-risk-view.ts`) appends a one-line note when long-run consistency is below half the target (running mode, once load data exists). `RunDurabilityResult` gained `qualifyingLongRunCount` / `consistencyTarget` / `consistencyCredit`.

## 2026-06-17 — Triathlon forecast projects at the planned dose, not the next 4 weeks (ISSUE-297, tri Lesson 1)

The tri race-day forecast now understands the training you're going to do, properly. It gains each discipline's fitness over the weeks to race and closes the race-readiness gap — but it was sampling the dose from a fixed **next-4-week look-ahead**. Early in a plan that window sits in the low-volume base phase, so the build was under-credited: the projected bike/run got dragged by the durability cap (a demonstrated ~36 km/h cyclist forecast at ~34).

- **Two-term dose, read straight from the plan** (no invented constants — the full base→build→peak→taper ramp is already in `state.wks[w].triWorkouts`):
  - *Fitness gain* (the horizon) reads the **build-phase mean** — the average weekly dose across remaining non-taper weeks (`plannedBuildDoseByDiscipline`). Cumulative dose drives marker adaptation, so the block average is the right input.
  - *Race-readiness penalty closure* reads the **peak the plan holds** (`plannedPeakDoseByDiscipline`, mean of `'peak'`-phase weeks). Race-distance readiness is a function of the highest sustained volume reached, not the mean.
- **Taper never sheds fitness.** Taper weeks (and block-cycle deloads) are excluded from both doses — freshness, not build dose — but the existing taper invariant (`projected == current` inside the taper window) is untouched. Verified.
- **Display follows the engine.** The tri Forecast training chip relabels "Planned next 4 weeks" → "Average build week" and reads the same build dose; its caption now explains the readiness penalty closes at the plan's peak-week rate (`forecast-chip-detail-view.ts`).
- Propagation probe (week 1 of a ramping 70.3): `bikeExecutionFactor` 0.60 → 0.86, so the durability cap relaxes in proportion to the volume the plan delivers. Guards: `tri-volume-by-discipline.test.ts` +10; full suite green (3478). SCIENCE_LOG §CG. **Not device-verified** — confirm the forecast moves with the plan on a real early-plan triathlete.

## 2026-06-17 — ACWR response policy: keep-ramping vs ease-back, intelligent load reduction (ISSUE-295)

When training load runs hot (ACWR above the tier safe ceiling), the plan no longer silently bumps fitness or silently cuts two quality sessions. Two changes:

- **Fitness number left honest.** VDOT describes demonstrated fitness (tracking); ACWR is forward-looking risk (planning). A hot week no longer holds back the fitness anchor. The escalation risk is fixed at the plan layer instead. No change to the VDOT writeback.
- **Offer, not impose.** The week-debrief "plan toggle" was cosmetic (Accept ignored the selection — the reduced plan always committed). It now persists the choice (`wk.acwrChoice`) and the generator honours it: **Keep ramping** leaves the week intact, **Ease back** applies an intelligent reduction. Default-until-chosen is eased (safe).
- **Intelligent ease-back ladder** (`computeAcwrEaseBack`, `src/calculations/acwr-ease-back.ts`). `L_max = safeUpper × chronic` (only constant is the existing tier `safeUpper`); the week sheds exactly its overshoot via: (1) strip intensity (quality → easy, fast-finish long run → steady), distances kept; (2) trim easy/midweek volume; (3) shorten the long run only as a last resort. Replaces the blunt "drop 2 quality + freeze long run" (`plan_engine.ts`); caution band unchanged.
- **Escalation.** Mild high remembers a keep choice across the episode (no re-nag). At very high (ratio ≥ 1.6) or 3 consecutive high weeks the choice is cleared so the safe default returns and the debrief re-surfaces it with firmer copy. Logic extracted to the pure, tested `resolveAcwrEpisodeChoice`.
- **Hardening:** final taper (race) week is exempt (protects the ISSUE-298 primer); the debrief prefers the rollover-stamped chronic/safeUpper so preview == commit; copy is honest when the ladder can't reach the ceiling.
- Guards: `acwr-ease-back.test.ts` (11) + `generator.acwr-easeback.test.ts` (3, gating integration); full suite green (3492). SCIENCE_LOG §CF. **Not device-verified** — confirm both choices commit the right week in-app before closing ISSUE-295.

## 2026-06-17 — New users no longer hit a 406 on the plan-restore query

- **Problem.** `restorePlanFromSupabase` (`src/data/planSettingsSync.ts`) read `user_plan_settings` with `.single()`. PostgREST returns **406 Not Acceptable** whenever `.single()` matches zero rows — which is every brand-new user's first launch, before any plan has been saved. The error was already handled (`return false`), so it was functionally harmless, but it logged a 406 on every new account and polluted error monitoring.
- **Fix.** `.single()` → `.maybeSingle()`, which returns `data: null` with no error for zero rows (it errors only on 2+ rows). Behaviour is identical (null → returns false); the spurious 406 is gone.
- **Verified in-browser.** A fresh anonymous user with no row: `restorePlanFromSupabase()` returns false and the `user_plan_settings` request returns HTTP 200 (was 406). Confirmed it was the only `.single()` call in the client. tsc clean. Pure client change, no migration or deploy.

It was reverted the same session: that path resets `s.w = 1` / `planStartDate = this Monday` and only heals the position when `reconcilePlanAnchorToEarliestActivity` finds a logged activity (welcome-back.ts:305 returns false with none) — unsafe for exactly the sparse-activity users the detector targets (a zero-completion user still trips it, floors to 1 run, and the rebuild destroys the race countdown). Also surfaced: there is no runs-per-week editor in Settings, so the note's original "lower it in Settings" pointer was false. New `isScorableTriSession` filter counts only swim/bike/run/brick on both sides. Running adherence was already clean (denominator = `s.rw` runs, numerator filters non-runs).
