## 2026-06-17 — Mid-week onboarding: reduced partial first week, starts today (all modes)

- **Problem (raised by Tristan)**: a user onboarding any day other than Monday still got a Monday-anchored week 1 that showed the days before they joined as blank/uncompletable cards, and silently penalized them for sessions on days they never had. The plan should start the day they onboard, credit anything they already trained this week, and give a naturally-lighter first week.
- **What already worked**: pre-onboard activities this week already flow into week 1 and count toward load — `weekIndexForDate` maps a Mon/Tue run to week 1 and `computeWeekTSS` credits every actual (`activity-matcher.ts`, `fitness-model.ts`). No change needed for crediting.
- **Fix**:
  - New canonical filter `dropPreOnboardSessions` (`ui/workout-status.ts`), keyed off the existing `firstTrackedDow`: for the current week it removes sessions scheduled on days before the onboarding weekday. Applied in the three render resolvers — running `resolveWeekWorkouts`, the shared tri/cycling/HYROX `resolveTriWeekWorkouts`, and the running plan/Home paths that read them. Week 1 now begins today; full load resumes the next Monday.
  - Adherence (`plan-adherence.ts`): the onboarding week's run denominator is pro-rated by the schedulable fraction of the week (`s.rw × firstTrackedDow / 7`, real quantities, no invented constant) so the dropped days don't read as "missed" once week 1 is scored. This also fixes a latent bug — the flat `s.rw` denominator already penalized mid-week onboarders.
  - Week-advance auto-skip (`events.ts`): the unrated-session gate now filters pre-onboard days, so advancing out of week 1 never prompts or feeds phantom RPE-5 load for sessions that never existed.
- **Late-week (Sat/Sun) onboards**: explored anchoring week 1 to *next* Monday for a clean full first week, but rejected it — a future `planStartDate` breaks two launch invariants: `weekIndexForDate` drops pre-start activities (`daysDiff < 0 → null`, so a lead-in run wouldn't credit) and `reconcilePlanAnchorToEarliestActivity` pulls the anchor back the moment a lead-in run is logged (causing `s.w` drift). Instead the anchor stays this Monday and the natural partial-week mechanism leaves a chill 1–2 session week 1 (the lead-in), with the first full week landing next Monday. Same experience, no invariant risk.
- **Out of scope (deliberate, "first week doesn't need to be perfect")**: type-aware dedupe (a long run already done this week does not auto-drop the planned one). The already-done run still credits to load as an unplanned activity.
- **Tests**: `workout-status.test.ts` +7 (filter behaviour across onboarding weekdays, no-op cases); `plan-adherence.test.ts` +2 (onboarding-week denominator). Full suite green (one unrelated timeout under parallel load, passes standalone). tsc + ui-lint clean.
- **Not device-verified.**

## 2026-06-17 — Reviewer-demo race date landed on Saturday in UTC-ahead timezones

- `demoRaceDate()` rolled the race forward to Sunday using **local** date accessors, then serialised with `toISOString()` (UTC). In any UTC-ahead timezone during the late-night window the serialised calendar day fell back one day, so the seeded `selectedRace.date` was stored as a **Saturday**, not the intended Sunday. Fixed by rolling to Sunday with UTC accessors (`setUTCDate`/`getUTCDay`) so the rolled day survives UTC serialisation. `src/state/demo-data.ts`.
- The regression test (`demo-data.test.ts`) asserted `getDay()` on a UTC-anchored date-only string, which itself reads Saturday in the Americas. Switched to `getUTCDay()` so the assertion is timezone-independent. The failure was a real defect, not date staleness.

## 2026-06-17 — Ironman long run builds to a 2:30 ceiling + key-session alternation

- **Problem (raised by Tristan)**: an Ironman plan only ever prescribed a ~20 km long run, despite the IM run leg being a full marathon. Root cause: the long run was a fixed 45% share of a bike-dominated run budget (35% of weekly hours), so it could never reach marathon-relevant durability without ~16 h/week.
- **Science** (SCIENCE_LOG §CD): the IM marathon is run on pre-fatigued legs after ~180 km of cycling; the limiter is *durability* (Maunder 2021), and only running loads the legs eccentrically — bike volume can't substitute. The long run builds to 2:30 (the Friel/Fitzgerald sweet spot), below standalone-marathon's ~30 km because total three-sport load caps run volume and the brick carries run-on-fatigue specificity.
- **Fix**:
  - `triLongRunTargetMin` — IM long run ramps from a 90-min week-1 anchor to a **150-min (2:30) peak**, replacing the 0.45-share derivation. 70.3 and shorter keep the share model.
  - `triWeekEmphasis` — IM build/peak weeks **alternate** by parity: run-emphasis weeks run the full long run and ease the standalone long ride to a **75% maintenance floor** (`TRI_KEY_SESSION_MAINTENANCE`); bike-emphasis weeks reverse it. The peak long run and peak long ride never collide (Banister supercompensation). The brick is untouched.
  - Funding reallocates minutes (reduced long ride → longer long run) and is **time-budget-conserving** — a new test confirms no IM week (10/12/14/18 h) exceeds its weekly hours cap.
  - `DURABILITY_THRESHOLDS.ironman.longRunSec` raised 2.0 h → 2.5 h so the tracking durability bar agrees with the plan target (`MAX_DURABILITY_PENALTY` unchanged at +5%).
  - Plan view shows a current-week consultant-tone note on every IM build/peak week: it names which key session leads, then sets the expectation that the brick and long run sit back to back so **the long run lands on tired legs by design** ("the Ironman marathon is run on a depleted system"). Stops a user reading the deliberate fatigue as a fitness problem.
  - The **long-run card itself** carries a short in-the-moment caption ("Run this on tired legs from the brick. Training the marathon on a fatigued system is the point.") via a new `coachNote` slot on `renderTriWorkoutCard` (modelled on the `legLoadNudge` muted note — neutral, no accent/emoji). Gated to IM brick weeks, active cards only.
- **Brick = the long ride + a transition run** (coaching call, Option A): build/peak weeks were stacking a standalone long ride *and* a separate medium brick (the engine generated both; the "brick replaces the long bike" scheduler comment was never honoured). With the coach hat on, the canonical IM weekend is one long-bike day with a transition run off it, paired with the next-day long run. The engine now **pops the long ride and wraps it as the brick**; `brickFrac` drops its bike term so the redundant second ride's hours fold into a longer single ride (no extra time, verified within the weekly cap). The alternation now eases the *brick's ride* on run weeks. Applies to all brick distances; off brick weeks (base/taper) the long ride stays solo.
- **Tests**: `plan_engine.triathlon.test.ts` 26 passing (incl. weekly-cap conservation across 10–18h IM); full suite green (3446 passing). tsc + ui-lint clean.
- **Not device-verified.**

## 2026-06-17 — Race week is sharpening, not training: final-week primer (all modes)

- **Problem (dogfood)**: a 14-week half-marathon plan prescribed a full **Threshold 3×8** (24 min of threshold work) on the Thursday of week 14, three days before a Sunday race. That is a build-phase session inside race week. Audit: running carried the full bug, tri/cycling a partial version, HYROX was already correct (the model mirrored).
- **Root cause (running, `plan_engine.ts`)**: `pickPhaseVariant` rotated taper like build, so the blind rotation could land the heaviest variant (`thr_3x8`) in race week; and the `×0.60` taper multiplier reduced the *target* minutes but a rep-based variant renders `reps × repMin` straight off the variant, so the structure stayed 3×8 while `workMinutes` said 12.
- **Fix (running)**: `pickPhaseVariant` now treats `taper` like `base` (draws the lightest variant subset — fixes non-final taper weeks, no new constant). The **final** taper week (`phase === 'taper' && weekIndex >= totalWeeks`) seats a fixed primer: `TAPER_PRIMER_THRESHOLD` = 3×2 min @ threshold (marathon/half/10K) or `TAPER_PRIMER_VO2` = 4×1 min (5K, whose taper priority is vo2). The taper preserves fitness and sheds fatigue (Mujika & Padilla 2003; Bosquet 2007); a few minutes of quality keeps the athlete primed without the residual fatigue of a 24-min block.
- **Fix (triathlon / cycling, `tri-intensity-profile.ts`)**: the taper quality-slot *count* was already right (taper zeroes the run slot at every distance); the *flavour* wasn't gated, so the remaining taper bike/swim slot could still draw VO2/over-under. `gateForBase` → `gateLowIntensity` now fires for base **and** taper, capping the taper kind to sub-threshold (`sweet_spot`/`tempo` bike, `threshold` swim/run). Cycling-only mode inherits this via the shared tri engine. Duration was already cut by the phase multiplier; this caps intensity.
- **Day placement**: left unchanged. Once the session is a short primer, the existing mid-week (Tue/Thu) placement 3–5 days out is standard race-week practice (Pfitzinger/Daniels). The size was the problem, not the day.
- Coach-set primer rep schemes (3×2, 4×1) under Tristan's "act as a coach" delegation, grounded in priming literature; the only new numbers. SCIENCE_LOG §CE.
- Guards: `plan_engine.taper-primer.test.ts` (4 tests — half/marathon → `Threshold 3×2`, 5K → `VO2 Builder 4×1`, build threshold still full). tsc + full workouts suite (367) green. **NOT device-verified.**

## 2026-06-17 — Triathlete run predictions: a recent race now anchors over the watch VO2max (ISSUE-297 tri analogue)

- **Symptom (dogfood)**: a triathlete with a real 70.3 (run 1:55 half) and an Apple Watch VO2max of 56 saw running paces far too fast — easy 4:45/km, threshold 3:58/km, projected marathon 3:33 — plus a too-fast Ironman run leg. His 1:55 half implies run VDOT ~42–45; VDOT 56 is sub-19 5K shape.

It ranks ABOVE the watch in `getPhysiologicalVdot` (below the standalone-run mosaic estimate, so a better event still wins), caps the blend's VO2 predictor (`effectiveVo2max`) so EVERY blend path yields — including the tri run-leg race time that recomputes off the watch directly — and floors/caps the engine in `refreshBlendedFitness`. The VO2 stats card still shows the true watch number; only the run predictions yield.

Separate, still-open display bugs: the tri bike target rendering as "6:34" (a run-pace `targetPaceSecPerKm` leaking onto a bike leg) and the swim showing faster than the actual split. ## 2026-06-16 — Triathlon weekly hours cap now binds the full plan (was overshooting ~60%)

- **Symptom**: a user set "max 10 hours" on triathlon mode and got a week of ~16 hours.
- **Root cause (two defects)**: (1) the cap (`triConfig.timeAvailableHoursPerWeek`) sized only the solo swim/bike/run sessions; the brick (~2.8h at peak), gym (up to 1.5h), and commute runs were generated and stacked *on top* with no accounting against it. (2) commute workouts carried no `estimatedDurationMin`, so the scheduler's `workoutMinutes()` defaulted each slot to **60 min** regardless of distance — a 4 km commute counted as a full hour, and bidirectional commutes counted two.
- **Decision (Tristan)**: "max hours" now means **total prescribed time** — solo S/B/R + brick + gym + commute all sum to ≤ the cap. This supersedes the §AM additive-commute model (commutes were deliberately on-top transport); the accepted trade-off is that heavy commuters now get a thinner structured plan.
- **Fix** (`plan_engine.triathlon.ts`): a one-line budget solve, no invented constants. Reserve gym + commute (commute at its real `distanceKm × easyPace` duration) and the brick's `brickFrac` share, then size solo S/B/R from `sbrMin = (capMin − gym − commute) / (1 + brickFrac)`. The four components sum back to the cap by construction. Commute slots now carry a real `estimatedDurationMin`.

## 2026-06-16 — Scroll-then-tap bug: removed 20 unguarded `touchend` tap handlers

- **Symptom**: on iOS/touch, lifting a finger at the end of a scroll fired a click on whatever link/row was under it ("it clicks wherever you stop scrolling").
- **Root cause**: 20 clickable elements across `methodology-view`, `stats-view`, `strength-progress-view`, and `triathlon/stats-view` bound *both* `click` and a `touchend` handler that did `e.preventDefault(); action()` with **no movement guard**. The `touchend` fired on every finger-lift over the element regardless of scroll, and its `preventDefault()` even suppressed the browser's native click-after-scroll cancellation.
- **Why they were unnecessary**: the viewport meta (`width=device-width, user-scalable=no, maximum-scale=1.0`) already disables the iOS 300ms tap delay, so plain `click` is instant. Every site had a paired `click` handler directly above the deleted `touchend`; each target is a `<button>` or a `cursor:pointer` div (click-on-div is proven to work on device — `.plan-card-header` is click-only).
- **Fix**: deleted the 20 inline `touchend` handlers; the surviving `click` handlers respond instantly and the browser natively suppresses click-after-scroll. The 4 legitimate `touchend` handlers (drag-reorder in the 3 plan views, web-overscroll-bounce) were left untouched — they already have movement/scroll guards.
- **Follow-up (same day, reported on the Stats page)**: the "Your Numbers" info buttons (`ⓘ` next to Lactate Threshold / VO2 Max, `wireInfoButtons`) used `touchstart → e.preventDefault(); handler()`, which fires the instant the finger lands — starting a scroll on the button toggled the info box. Removed it; the button is a real `<button>` with `touch-action:manipulation` so `click` is already instant. This was the only action-firing `touchstart` in the app (the 3 remaining are drag-reorder hold timers).
- tsc clean, `lint:ui` clean, tests green. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-16 — Plan periodisation: load apex lands in the peak phase, continuous mode climbs, mix bars weight by load

Three parked plan-shape bugs (see `docs/HANDOVER_PARKED_PLAN_BUGS.md`), all in the plan engine / plan-shape derivation, independent of the ISSUE-297 prediction work.

- **Bug 3 (ISSUE-287) — load apex was landing in the BUILD phase, not PEAK.** Root cause was not the phase intensity multipliers (they move weekly load only ~5%); it was **workout-variant rotation**. The blind `(weekIndex - 1) % len` rotation scattered the high-load variants — chiefly the `fast_finish` progressive long run (~30 TSS over steady) — across the plan, so the heaviest week often landed in build, ahead of the single peak-phase week of a short plan. Fix: `pickPhaseVariant` (plan_engine.ts) biases variant selection by phase — peak draws the heaviest variants, base/deload the lightest, build/taper keep full rotation. Deload weeks also draw the lightest variants (genuine recovery, removes the post-deload bounce). No load constant invented; only *which existing variant* a phase draws changed. Found + flagged a latent bug en route: `long_with_blocks` was never wired to a distinct format and renders identically to `long_steady` (so it is ranked load 0, not the high rank its name implies). Result: the TSS apex now lands in the peak phase for every length/distance probed (9/12/16/18 wk × 10k/half/marathon). Guard: `plan_engine.apex.test.ts` (12 cases). Also added a muted inline "compressed plan" caption under the coach-contract load chart for event plans of ≤12 weeks (continuous plans excluded).
- **Bug 1 — continuous mode "ramped in circles".** Endless plans repeat Base→Build→Peak→Taper via `i % 4`; each cycle peaked at the same low level. The geometric volume-budget ramp (`weekVolumeBudgetKm`, archetype `weeklyRampPct`) only engages with a baseline + archetype, which a continuous user who hasn't synced lacks. Fix (generator.ts): for continuous mode only, fall back to the plan's own starting volume `s.wkm` (the same freq-derived estimate the prediction uses — not invented) + the neutral `'unknown'` archetype (7% ramp). Per-cycle peak now climbs toward the readiness-capped ceiling then plateaus (rw=4: 261→287→287→296 TSS). Honest limitation: at 2 runs/wk the sessions are already at their physiological caps (long run ~63 min) so there is no room to add volume — the climb is correctly negligible; ≥3 sessions are needed to express progressive overload. Event plans unaffected (they still read detected values only). Guard: `plan_engine.continuous.test.ts`.
- **Bug 2 — coach-contract session-mix bars stuck at 50/50 in low-frequency plans.** A count-based aerobic-vs-quality split collapses to 50/50 when there are only 2 sessions (1 easy + 1 quality every phase). Fix: `SessionBucket` now carries `load` (canonical TSS); `renderSessionShift` weights the split by load, not count. The phase shift is visible again (event rw=4: base 36% → peak 87% quality → taper 45%; continuous rw=3: base 45% → peak 83%), and the taper correctly reads as quality-dominant by load (volume drops, intensity maintained). Guard: `plan-shape.test.ts`.
- Files: `src/workouts/plan_engine.ts` (`pickPhaseVariant`, `variantWork`, `LONG_VARIANTS.load`, `variantPhase`), `src/workouts/generator.ts` (continuous baseline fallback), `src/calculations/plan-shape.ts` (`SessionBucket.load`), `src/ui/wizard/steps/coach-contract.ts` (load-weighted split). SCIENCE_LOG §CA. tsc + ui-lint clean; 341 workout + plan-shape + coach-contract suites green. **NOT device-verified** — verify by regenerating a short (9-12 wk) plan and a continuous plan in-app and confirming the load chart crests under the Peak label and continuous blocks step up.

## 2026-06-16 — Deleted PBs can no longer resurrect (ISSUE-297 RC3)

- **Symptom.** Enter a PB (e.g. a 2:00:00 marathon), delete it, and the plan stays anchored to it. Cause: `effectivePhysiologyPbs` merged `Math.min(s.pbs, s.onboarding.pbs)` (fastest-wins), so deleting from one store left it winning from the other; and the Strava/Apple auto-fills would silently re-detect a deleted effort from history.
- **Fix.** New per-distance deletion tombstone `s.deletedPbs` (optional state field). `isPbTombstoned(deletedPbs, key, candidate)` suppresses any candidate that isn't *genuinely faster* than the deleted time. Applied at three points: `effectivePhysiologyPbs` (read backstop — also fixes the engine, since `pbDerivedVdot` reads it), and the Strava (`review.ts`) + Apple (`appleHealthSync.ts`) auto-fills (no silent re-add). `recordPbDeletion` sets the tombstone and clears the value from BOTH stores + PB dates; `clearPbTombstone` runs on explicit re-entry so re-adding a deleted PB always works.
- Wired into the review-step PB editor (the real delete site; the other handlers listed in the diagnostic only display PBs). `recordPbDeletion` triggers a `refreshBlendedFitness` so the engine/prediction recompute immediately.
- Guards: `physiological-vdot.test.ts` "PB deletion tombstones (ISSUE-297 RC3)" (4 cases). tsc clean, full suite green (only the parallel agent's in-flight `connect-data.ts` fails). ISSUE-297 now fully addressed in code (RC1 + forecast + RC3); **NOT device-verified.**

## 2026-06-16 — Race predictions: engine no longer buried by low volume; forecast credits the plan's ramp (ISSUE-297 RC1 + forecast)

- **Symptom (Tristan dogfooding).** A 20:00 5K with ~8 km/wk, marathon target, was shown a ~3:50–4:00 marathon that collapsed the global engine VDOT 50 → ~40, a 20-week forecast barely faster than today, and a *different* answer on each recompute. Root cause: a race-readiness (low-volume) penalty was being written back into the capacity number `s.v`, then read on the next refresh (path-dependent).
- **Fix 1 (RC1) — engine vs readiness separation.** `refreshBlendedFitness` (`blended-fitness.ts`) and `initializeSimulator` (`state/initialization.ts`) now floor the engine VDOT at demonstrated cross-distance PB capacity (`pbMedianVdot`), standing down only on *demonstrated recent slowness* (a recent run projecting below capacity). Low training volume no longer lowers the engine — it moves the prediction/forecast only. The engine is now a pure function of demonstrated fitness, so repeated refreshes are deterministic (no feedback loop). Today's race estimate (`blendedRaceTimeSec`) stays honestly slow off thin volume.
- **Fix 2 — forecast credits the planned volume.** Two-term model: cumulative training dose drives the engine gain (build-phase mean, unchanged); race-approach sustained volume drives marathon-specific endurance. The forecast anchor is now a `blendPredictions` evaluated at `computePeakWeeklyKm` (the exact peak the plan engine ramps toward, `plan_engine.ts:409`), so the low-volume/specificity penalty lifts in proportion to the mileage the plan actually delivers — full relief ≥30 km/wk, partial in the 20–30 km band (a thin-data beginner is never over-credited). `computePeakWeeklyKm` exported with a narrowed input type; `pbMedianVdot` split out of `pbDerivedVdot` so init can compute capacity from its local PBs.
- **No new constants** — every threshold already existed; each term is just fed the volume it is physiologically a function of (Coyle 1984; Mujika & Padilla 2000; Banister; Joyner & Coyle 2008). Same mechanism matches both observed cases (40:00-10K/52 km plan → ~3:10 ground truth; 8 km/wk → honest-slow today, faster forecast).
- Guards: `blended-fitness.test.ts` "engine/readiness separation + peak-volume forecast (ISSUE-297)" (5 cases) + rewritten `initialization.durability.test.ts` engine-holds-at-capacity. `tsc` clean, full suite green (the only failures are the parallel agent's in-flight `connect-data.ts` and order-dependent flakes in their untracked `plan-shape-chart.ts`, none touching these files). ## 2026-06-16 — Readiness "ease off": threshold tempo collapsed to its warm-up + card didn't repaint

- Device repro (Week 1, Base, sleep 25, readiness 51): tapping "Take it lighter today" → "Convert to easy run" turned a `2km warm up · 13min @ 4:12/km (~3.1km) · 2km cool down` threshold tempo (~7 km / 33 min) into **"2km @ easy"**, and the card only repainted after switching to Plan and back.

- Root cause 1 (the 2 km): `applyRecoveryAdjustment` computed the session distance with `todayRun.d.match(/(\d+\.?\d*)km/)`, which returns the **first** `km` token. For a structured session that token is the warm-up (2 km), so the 3.1 km threshold block and 2 km cool-down were thrown away. The sheet's own copy promises "Same distance, Zone 2 only", so this directly contradicted intent.
  - Fix: derive the full distance via `parseWorkoutDescription(todayRun.d, s.pac)` (sums WU + work + CD ≈ 7 km), keeping the first-token regex only as a no-paces fallback. The "Convert to easy run" subtitle in `home-view.ts` (`showRecoveryAdviceSheet`) was fixed the same way so the label matches the result. The 'reduce' (20% cut) branch was wrong for structured sessions too and is fixed by the same change.
- Root cause 2 (the lag): `applyRecoveryAdjustment` ended with `render()` (`renderer.ts:145`), which only patches the Plan dashboard's stat elements by id and never rebuilds the workout card. Replaced with `rerenderAfterRecoveryAdjustment()` — `renderHomeView()` on Home, `renderMainView()` on Plan. The same fix was applied to the `triggerACWRReduction` modal callback (`main-view.ts:2417`) for the elevated-ACWR path.
- Guard: regression test in `parser.test.ts` pins the exact structured tempo to >6 km (was returning 2 km). tsc + lint:ui clean, 52 parser/events/suggester tests green. Code-complete, NOT device-verified.

This is the deliberate alternative to a full Monte Carlo cone (running/tri have one): a HYROX cone would need defensible per-station improvement variance we don't have, so we use the existing factor band instead.
- **Calibration banner (low + medium).** Every non-high-confidence forecast now shows an inline banner that states, in plain terms, that a station assessment makes the prediction more accurate, and names the protocol so they do it right ("each station at half distance, race effort"). `low` (cross-format or seed-dominated) → strong `Provisional forecast` + "Test your stations"; `medium` (partially calibrated) → soft `Sharpen your forecast` + "Calibrate the rest" with the `X of N stations calibrated` count. Replaces the caveat that was buried behind the confidence badge. CTA routes to the Stations factor page (the calibration entry point, which carries the half-distance protocol copy).
- **Target-modal parse + copy.** The "Set a target finish" modal read `1:00` literally as 1 min 0 sec, so a user meaning 1 hour got a nonsensical back-calc. `parseHhMmSs` now reinterprets a 2-part value as `h:mm` when the `mm:ss` reading is below the competitive population floor and the `h:mm` reading lands in a plausible window (floor to 4 h); a live echo (`Target: H:MM:SS`) under the input always shows the resolved interpretation. The unrealistic-target warning no longer prints raw seconds (`~3360s`) — header reads `About 56 min faster than realistic` and the caveat dropped the seconds figure entirely.

## 2026-06-16 — Apple Health connect: false "could not be reached" was a timeout counting human sheet-time

Root cause of the recurring "approve → no data → can't retry" report (device, TestFlight). The card body the user saw was the **`sync-error`** branch ("Apple Health could not be reached"), NOT the `no-data` branch every prior fix targeted. `sync-error` can only be produced by the UI's 20s `Promise.race` timeout. The connect required passing through **two** sequential iOS permission sheets (capgo physiology, then the HealthExtras VO2/power/routes sheet at `appleHealthSync.ts:135`), and the 20s clock counted the time the user spent reading and approving both — which a human cannot beat. Timeout fired → false error; the pinned `_connectInFlight` promise then made every re-tap re-ride the dead promise ("only works once").

- `connectAppleHealthInner` now decides success on the capgo physiology read **alone** (one sheet), sets `appleHealthConnected` immediately, then fires the HealthExtras permission + VO2/FTP reads as **fire-and-forget** (enrichment, not a gate). The second sheet no longer delays or blocks the result.
- The gating read is bounded by an internal `withTimeout` (`CONNECT_PHYSIOLOGY_TIMEOUT_MS = 90s`, resolves `false`) so the in-flight guard always clears and retries are always possible, even if the capgo native bridge hangs.
- Removed the premature 20s UI race in `connect-data.ts:triggerAppleHealth`; it now awaits the (always-resolving, internally-bounded) connect directly.
- Native `HealthExtrasPlugin.swift requestPermissions`: the `[weak self]` auth callback now resolves the call (best-effort) instead of silently returning when `self` is deallocated — a latent permanent-hang path.
- Recovery copy now gives the correct manual path (Health app → profile → Privacy → Apps → Mosaic; or Settings → Privacy & Security → Health → Mosaic). The "Open Settings" deep-link can only reach Mosaic's *own* settings page, which does NOT show Health toggles (confirmed on device).

tsc + connect-data/capgo tests + ui-lint green. **NOT device-verified** — needs `cap sync ios` + rebuild (native Swift change). Do not mark resolved until confirmed on a phone.

## 2026-06-16 — Range sliders no longer steal-scroll on iOS (touch-action: pan-y)

- **Symptom.** The goal-time slider in the wizard "What are you chasing?" modal was "incredibly hard to swipe — it kept scrolling down" on iPhone. The thumb rarely caught the gesture; the modal scrolled instead.
- **Root cause.** Range inputs had no `touch-action` declaration, defaulting to `auto`. Inside a vertically-scrolling modal, WKWebView can't disambiguate a horizontal thumb-drag from a vertical scroll and resolves the ambiguity as a scroll, so the slider almost never wins the gesture.
- **Fix.** Added a global `input[type="range"] { touch-action: pan-y; }` rule (`src/styles.css`). Horizontal gestures are now handed to the slider thumb; vertical swipes still scroll the surrounding modal. Applied globally rather than per-site so it covers every slider — the `.m-slider-glass` goal/plan-duration/RPE sliders plus the un-classed safety, injury-modal, activity-RPE and wizard-schedule range inputs — and no future slider can reintroduce the bug.
- The plan day-reorder "kept scrolling" symptom is a different, intentional mechanism: a 350ms long-press hold gate (`plan-view.ts`, "Hold and drag to reorder") that deliberately lets pre-hold movement scroll the page. Kept the gate, but it gave no feedback that the hold had completed, so users didn't know the card was armed to move.
- **Drag-arm affordance.** When the hold completes the card now lifts (`scale(1.03)` + drop shadow) and fires a medium Taptic Engine haptic (`fireSelectionHaptic` in `utils/platform.ts`, native-only, lazy-imported). Reset on touchend, touchcancel, and the scroll-abandon path. Makes it obvious the finger can now move the card.
- **Scroll-freeze once armed.** After pop-out, the page kept scrolling while the user tried to place the card: iOS classifies the gesture as a scroll on the first move and then ignores later `preventDefault`s. Fix: `preventDefault` fires on the first move *after the hold* (before the 8px drag threshold), so iOS never starts a scroll. Applied to all three plan-views — running, triathlon, HYROX — and triathlon/HYROX also gained the lift + haptic + touchcancel reset they were missing (mirror-rule parity).
- CSS + interaction change. **Device-verified** on iPhone (2026-06-16): slider drags cleanly and the popped-out card freezes the page while placing.

## 2026-06-16 — Glass-card text ghost fixed app-wide (node-replace, not textContent)

- **Symptom.** The onboarding "Reading your training" loading screen showed garbled overlapping titles, e.g. "LcReading your physiologyry" — the old step label's glyphs bleeding through the new one. Recurring across multiple prior fix attempts (opacity cross-fade, note-line cross-fade, fade-timing match) — none held.
- **Root cause (the one that actually matters).** The label sits inside a `backdrop-filter:blur(24px)` glass card *over animating whisper rings*. On WKWebView the cached raster is keyed to the **backdrop-filter compositing layer**, not the individual text node — the layer holds its rasterised descendant text and composites new glyphs on top of the stale bitmap. Opacity fades never invalidate that layer; **and neither does replacing the text node** (a fresh node's text still paints over the cached layer). Confirmed on a fresh device build: node-replace alone still ghosted.
- **The fix that works: take the text OUT of the backdrop-filter subtree.** Both loading cards now put the blur on a dedicated EMPTY background layer (`position:absolute;inset:0;backdrop-filter:blur(24px)`) with all text in a sibling `z-index:1` content layer that has NO backdrop-filter ancestor. The glass look is identical (the blur panel still samples the rings behind it), but the text now re-rasters as normal DOM. This is the canonical pattern for changing text on a glass surface — keep the blur and the changing text in separate layers.
- **Belt-and-suspenders helper.** New `src/ui/raster-safe-text.ts` still REPLACES the node on swap (`swapFadedText` for fades, `setRasterSafeText` for instant counters) — harmless now that the text isn't under backdrop-filter, and it's the right tool for any future text that *is* forced under a glass layer.
- **Sites fixed (cross-cutting, one pass).**
  - `wizard/steps/review.ts` — onboarding "Reading your training" loading card: blur moved to a background layer; text in a sibling layer; uses shared `swapFadedText`.
  - `wizard/steps/initializing.ts` — "Building your plan" loading card: same layer split, PLUS a timing bug fixed (it swapped text at 220ms into a 450ms fade, so text changed while ~half-visible — overlap even off WKWebView). Now `swapFadedText` with `fadeMs` matched to the 0.45s CSS transition.
  - `import-activity-modal.ts`, `strava-history-guide.ts`, `screenshot-import-modal.ts` — status / progress lines (`Reading archive… 4/12`) inside `backdrop-filter:blur(16px)` glass dialogs; now go through `setRasterSafeText` (re-queried by id each call since node-replace detaches cached refs).
  - Left alone: `history-claim-overlay.ts` — no `backdrop-filter` ancestor, so not at risk.
- tsc clean; `lint:ui` clean. NOT device-verified — needs confirmation on an actual iPhone (the raster bug only reproduces on WKWebView).

## 2026-06-15 — Marathon plans: long run builds to race-readiness; volume periodises under the hours cap (ISSUE-286)

- **Symptom (real device plan)**: an 18-week marathon plan peaked at **week 2**, drew a flat/jagged sawtooth load line with no arc, topped the long run out at **~18 km / 89 min**, and ran ~452 km total — under-built for a marathon. The coach-contract chart was verified faithful; the plan engine was the problem.
- **RC1 — long run never reached marathon-readiness**: `longRunMinutes` (`plan_engine.ts`) ramped a fixed 90-min marathon base across only 80%→100%, maxing at ~95 min — so the ability cap never bound and the long run never approached the 30 km the app's own predictor (`LONG_RUN_THRESHOLD_SEC.marathon = 165 min`) calls "ready". Fix: marathon long run now ramps linearly from the 90-min week-1 anchor up to a distance-aware ability ceiling (`longRunCapMin`: beginner 150, novice/intermediate 165, advanced/elite 180 min). Shorter distances unchanged. Same cap reused in `computePeakWeeklyKm`.
- **RC2 — flat budget under a tight hours cap**: `effectiveWeeklyBudgetMin` took `min(ramp, hoursCap)` per week, so a tight hours target pinned every week flat and the "peak" landed on whatever week the session-mix noise was highest (week 2). Fix: cap the *peak* destination, then ramp toward it with the existing geometric fraction — restores a base→build→peak→taper arc. New budget is always ≤ the old, so the hours cap is never loosened; plans with no hours target are byte-identical.
- **RC3 — zero easy volume credited for a 3-run marathon**: `computePeakWeeklyKm` computed `easyCount = 0` for a marathon at 3 runs/wk, over-tightening the budget. Fix: floor at 1 for marathon when `runsPerWeek ≥ 3`. Cross-training stays scheduled alongside.
- **Effect (rw=3 probe)**: peak week 11→**14**, peak km 37→**51**, total 452→**588**, peak long run 18 km/89 min → **32 km/159 min**. Tight-hours-cap front-loaded peak (wk 5) → wk 14.
- Also fixed a latent bug in `load-currency-anchors.test.ts` (tri fixture used the non-existent `raceType` field instead of the canonical `distance`; the uncommitted tri intensity-profile work newly reads `tri.distance` and crashed on the `undefined`). SCIENCE_LOG §BW. `tsc` clean, plan/workout suite (326) green. Not device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Reset Plan now sticks: clear the Supabase backup too (old plan kept coming back)

On the next launch, `restorePlanFromSupabase()` wrote that stale row straight back — unconditionally in the `SIGNED_IN` handler (`main.ts:307`) and whenever localStorage looked empty (`main.ts:328`). The reset wiped local state, the cloud restored over the top. Verified the *local* path is correct by reproduction in simulator mode (which bypasses cloud): `wks 16→0`, `hasCompletedOnboarding true→false`, no `wizard-return-btn` — confirming the bug is cloud-only.
- **Fix**: new `deletePlanSettings()` (`planSettingsSync.ts`) deletes the user's `user_plan_settings` row; `reset()` (`events.ts`) awaits it before `location.reload()` so the delete isn't cancelled by the navigation. `softResetState()` also now clears the local state-owner stamp (`setLocalStateOwner(null)`) so a stale owner can't trigger a cross-user re-restore. Best-effort and no-op for anonymous/sim sessions (no user). `tsc` clean.

## 2026-06-15 — Wizard bootstrap crash fixed: `STEP_ORDER` temporal-dead-zone (entry-module cycle)

- **Symptom**: `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'STEP_ORDER' before initialization` thrown from `initWizard` (`controller.ts:74`) via `launchApp` → `bootstrap`. Surfaced as an unhandled rejection in `coach-contract.test.ts`, and a latent cold-bootstrap risk in the wizard.
- **Root cause**: a circular import through the auto-bootstrapping entry module. Six views and the onboarding `review` step imported two small helpers (`isSimulatorMode`, `awaitStartupSyncs`) from `@/main`. But `main.ts` also imports the wizard controller (`initWizard`) **and** runs `bootstrap()` at module load. That closed the cycle `controller → renderer → review → main.ts → bootstrap() → launchApp() → initWizard()`. When a wizard module was the evaluation entry point (e.g. a unit test importing one step), `main.ts` evaluated for the first time *mid-way through* `controller.ts`, auto-fired `bootstrap()` (jsdom reports `readyState === 'complete'`), and called `initWizard()` before `controller.ts` had reached its `STEP_ORDER` const — TDZ crash.
- **Fix**: moved `isSimulatorMode` + the startup-sync coordination (`trackStartupTask`, `awaitStartupSyncs`, new `signalLaunchAppComplete`) into a new **leaf module `src/app/runtime.ts`** that imports nothing from the heavy UI/data graph. Repointed all 7 importers (6 views + `review.ts`) to `@/app/runtime`. Nothing imports `@/main` any more, so `main.ts` is a pure entry point that boots exactly once.
- **Guard**: `src/app/entry-isolation.test.ts` greps every source module and fails if any import resolves to `@/main`, making the regression class unrepresentable.
- Secondary win: a single wizard-step test no longer transitively boots the whole app — `coach-contract.test.ts` import time dropped ~47s → ~2s. Full suite green (the lone HYROX `buildPlanSkeleton` timeout is a load-induced flake; passes in ~1s in isolation, unrelated to this change). `tsc` clean, `lint:ui` clean. Not device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Onboarding review: no population claims off the bare-baseline VDOT (the "Faster than 81% with no data" bug)

- A runner who reached "Here's what we found" with no PBs, no confirmed weekly volume, and no synced fitness still saw a confident **"Faster than 81% of male runners"** plus a projected "1:48:07 half marathon", and a VO2max "Higher than 28% of men aged 20-29" bar. Root cause: both the Field position row and the VO2max placement bar render off `getPhysiologicalVdot(s).vdot`, which walks a priority chain ending in `tanda-fallback` — the bare `s.v` baseline (default 50, or a stale value carried in localStorage from a prior onboarding/plan). The card itself honestly captions that tier "Rough estimate from recent training", but the two surfaces then made population-percentile and race-time *claims* off the same soft number. `hasRunningFitnessSignal` is true for any non-null `s.v`, so nothing gated them.
- Fixed by gating both surfaces on `physio.source`: when the source is `tanda-fallback` or `none` (no measured signal), `renderFieldPositionRow` returns `''` and the VO2max FRIEND placement bar is suppressed. The VO2max *value* still shows with its honest "add a PB or sync HR to refine" caption; only the percentile/projection claims are withheld. Every higher tier (`override`, `device`, `mosaic-running`, `hr-calibrated`, `lt-derived`, **`pb-median`**) is a real signal and renders as before — so the instant a PB is entered inline, the chain flips to `pb-median` and both rows reappear with a PB-grounded projection. `tsc` clean, `lint:ui` clean. Not yet device-verified.
- Same gate extended to the post-onboarding surfaces. New canonical helper `hasRealRunningFitnessSignal(s)` (`physiological-vdot.ts`) — true only when `getPhysiologicalVdot` resolves above the `tanda-fallback` tier (override / device / mosaic / hr-calibrated / lt-derived / pb-median). The **Forecast** standard-distance grid (`race-forecast-view.ts:getStandardForecastHTML`) now gates on it instead of the permissive `hasRunningFitnessSignal`, so a baseline-only user sees "No predictions yet / Import run history" rather than projected 5K–marathon times. ## 2026-06-15 — Onboarding "Here's what we found" Field position: real PB, not a premature projection

- Two problems on the Athlete profile → Field position row (`review.ts:renderFieldPositionRow`). (1) It read runtime `s.rd` to pick the comparison distance, but the plan isn't built until "Build my plan", so `s.rd` was still the default `'half'` — a marathon athlete was placed against the half-marathon field. (2) More fundamentally, it projected current VDOT to a finish time ("projects to a X:XX marathon") on a screen that comes *before* the prediction reveal. That projection is a raw Daniels conversion with no durability cap, so for the marathon it both pre-empted the prediction screen and read optimistically (the durability gap is widest at the marathon), producing two disagreeing marathon times.
- Fix: place the athlete with a **real race result** instead of a projection. New `reviewRaceDist(state)` resolves the goal distance from onboarding state (mirrors `initialization.ts:400-404`: event → `state.raceDistance`, no-event → focus-derived). New `pickPlacementPb()` then chooses the PB at the goal distance when present, else the strongest PB by VDOT, drawn from the canonical `effectivePhysiologyPbs(s)`. Caption changed from "Current fitness projects to a …" to "Based on your {time} {distance}." Percentile and age grade now derive from that actual PB (`runnerFieldPlacement` / `ageGradeForTime`, replacing the `…ForFitness` projection variants).
- Interaction with the same-day `tanda-fallback`/`none` guard (entry above): that guard suppressed the row when the VDOT came off a stale `s.v`. The PB-only rewrite **subsumes it for this row** — placement now derives strictly from a real PB via `effectivePhysiologyPbs`, so a soft/stale VDOT can never back a percentile claim, and no-PB users get no row. Behavior change to note: a user with a device VO2max / LT but no race PB previously saw a projected row; they no longer do (the VO2max placement bar still shows). That is consistent with the new "no projections on the review screen" stance. Trade-off: an athlete who has improved since their last race is slightly undersold here, but current fitness surfaces on the very next (prediction) screen — staging reads as "proven placement now → forward prediction next". `tsc` clean, 35 fitness-placement tests pass.

## 2026-06-15 — Prediction engine: "no training data" no longer read as "detrained" (the 2:00 marathon → 2:22 bug)

- **Symptom.** A user whose only data was a 2:00:00 marathon PB was predicted **2:24:54** (25 min slower than a time they have actually run). A 20:00 5K runner with no other data and 3 runs/week + 1 speed was predicted **4:02:39** for the marathon. Both felt wrong.
- **Root cause.** Three penalties (`marathonSpecificityPenalty` ×1.15, `applyLongRunCap` ×1.05, `noLongRacePenalty` ×1.01) all key off the *absence of synced training history*. At onboarding a brand-new user always has zero history, so `resolveWeeklyKmSignal` returned `0` and `getLongestRunSec` returned `0` — and the penalty code reads those zeros as "the athlete does zero running / has detrained". Absence of data was being treated as positive evidence of detraining.
- **Fix 1 (no-data gate).** `initialization.ts` now passes `undefined` (not `0`) for the weekly-volume signal when there is genuinely no history (`weeksCovered === 0` and no typed volume), so the marathon-specificity penalty stays dormant until real data lands. Real low-volume users (history present) are unaffected — the penalty still fires for them.
- **Fix 2 (demonstrated-PB floor).** New `demonstratedPBFloor` (`predictions.ts`) — a prediction can never come out slower than a PB at the *exact* target distance unless there is positive detraining evidence: a real weekly-volume signal < 30 km/wk, OR a recent run that itself projects slower than the PB. Applied inside `blendPredictions` and again after the durability cap in `initialization.ts`.
- **Result.** 2:00 marathon-only → **2:00:00**. 20:00 5K-only marathon → **~3:31** (Riegel ceiling + 1% no-long-race, no phantom penalties). A *returning* runner with a 1:28 half PB but a recent 24:00 5K still correctly predicts ≥1:30 (recent race is real evidence). The §BN thin-data 5K→half durability cap is preserved (no same-distance PB to floor against).
- Tests: 3 new regression cases in `predictions.test.ts`; `initialization.volume.test.ts` + `initialization.durability.test.ts` updated to the corrected behaviour. Full suite green (3340). SCIENCE_LOG §BV. NOT yet device-verified.
- **Follow-up — prediction and plan now share one volume assumption.** The no-data path no longer passes a phantom value: it sizes the athlete from their stated runs/week via the *same* `freqVolumeEstimate` the plan uses for starting volume (`s.wkm`), so the race estimate and the plan can't assume different weekly km for one person. The estimate is provenance-tagged — it sizes the soft marathon-specificity penalty but is **not** allowed to override a demonstrated same-distance PB (only *measured* or *stated* low volume can; an assumption must never beat a proven time). Net: 4-runs/week 5K→marathon unchanged (40 km/wk ≥ 30, no penalty); only ≤3-runs/week marathon hopefuls now correctly carry a mild penalty with no typed km, closing the "say nothing to dodge it" loophole. `blendPredictions` gained a `weeklyRunKmIsEstimate` flag; 2 more regression tests (3343 green). Next: thin-data onboarding sliders (longest run + volume estimate) and cross-training softening of the 5K/10K discount. NOT device-verified.
- **Follow-up — other sports now help short-distance predictions (not the marathon).** A heavy cross-trainer's watch LT/VO2 are genuinely current (cycling/rowing/swimming maintain VO2max + LT — Mujika & Padilla 2000; Bassett & Howley 2000), so `lowVolumeDiscount` now softens in proportion to aerobic cross-training — but **only for sub-marathon targets**. The marathon-specificity penalty and the long-run durability cap are untouched: marathon endurance is run-specific and does not transfer, so a fast-5K footballer with no long runs is still predicted to fade at 42 km. Two literature-derived, tunable constants: cross-training erases at most 60% of the discount (`CROSS_MAINTENANCE_CAP`, residual = un-maintained running economy, Conley & Krahenbuhl 1980), full effect at ~3 effective aerobic sessions/week (`CROSS_MAINTENANCE_PER_SESSION`, Hickson 1985). Signal is the existing intensity-weighted `effectiveCrossSessions`; onboarding passes the precise value, the refresh derives it from `epw − rw` so both agree. Also hardened the post-onboarding refresh (`blended-fitness.ts`) to mirror the no-data + provenance + post-cap-PB-floor logic so it can't re-break the headline fix seconds after onboarding. 3 cross-training regression tests; full suite 3356 green. SCIENCE_LOG §BV. NOT device-verified.
- **Follow-up — honesty caption for estimate-based predictions; thin-data sliders dropped.** Decision with Tristan: the proposed "longest run + weekly volume" onboarding sliders were dropped. The audience is near-empty (the app is watch-first; Apple Health / Strava / bridged-Garmin users all give real runs via the review-step backfill, which holds on a loading screen until it lands), and for the rare no-watch user the runs/week estimate already covers them and sharpens the moment they log a run. The higher-value move for that user is easy watch-connection, not a manual-entry screen worth a fraction of what a watch provides. Kept only the honest signal: new optional `s.blendedFromEstimate` (set when the blend had no measured run data), surfaced as a muted caption on the forecast header — "Estimated from your training profile. Refines as your runs sync." Clears automatically once real runs sync and the refresh re-runs. tsc + `lint:ui` clean; full suite 3361 green. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — A terrible sleep score now moves readiness in weeks 1–3 (the "sleep 25, readiness 65 On Track" bug)

- A user in Week 1 of a fresh plan logged "I slept terribly" (sleep 25/100) and readiness stayed at 65 / On Track with "Good balance of load and recovery." Two bugs combined:
  1. **`calculations/readiness.ts`** — when `weeksOfHistory < 3`, `computeReadiness` early-returned a hardcoded `65 / On Track` and discarded sleep, HRV, strain, and leg-load entirely. The guard exists because TSB / ACWR / momentum need ≥3 completed weeks of logged load to be trustworthy, but it also threw away recovery signals that are valid from day one. Fix: replaced the early return with an `insufficientHistory` flag that neutralises only the freshness and load-safety sub-scores to 65 and skips the ACWR hard floor; the recovery composite and the sleep / HRV / strain / leg-load floors now run normally. A 25/100 night in week 1 now pulls readiness to ~51 (Manage Load) with driving signal "recovery". New sentence under insufficient history leads with "Recovery is low. Keep today easy…" when recovery binds, otherwise the baseline-building message (also fixed its em-dash to comply with the copy rules).
  2. **`calculations/daily-coach.ts`** — read sleep from `physiologyHistory` only, so a no-watch user's manually-logged sleep (stored in `recoveryHistory`) never reached the coach sentence or its internal readiness call. The displayed sentence ("Good balance…") was computed as if no sleep existed. Fix: folded manual sleep in via the canonical `mergeManualSleepHistory` (mirrors home-view / readiness-view) for the sleep-score reads, `recoveryResult` (with the `manualSleepScore` option), `sleepHistory`, and `getSleepInsight`.
- Mirror rule: `calculations/tri-readiness.ts` had the same manual-sleep gap (read `physiologyHistory` directly). Folded `mergeManualSleepHistory` in there too so a no-watch triathlete's check-in night reaches the per-discipline readiness engine. The score fix flows through automatically since tri readiness calls the shared `computeReadiness`.
- Tests: 2 new regression tests in `readiness.test.ts` (terrible sleep tanks week-1 readiness; insufficient history does not fire the noisy ACWR floor). 3330 pass, tsc clean. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Native GPS now tracks distance immediately (the "0.00 km despite permissions" bug)

- On iOS, a live Quick Run recorded 0.00 km / `--:--` pace despite the user granting location permission — the elapsed timer ran but distance never moved. Root cause: the `@transistorsoft/capacitor-background-geolocation` SDK boots in its battery-saving *stationary* state. `start()` alone emits no `onLocation` events until the SDK's motion-detector decides the device is moving, which for a runner starting from a standstill can take ~200m of movement — or never fire if Motion & Fitness permission was declined. `NativeGpsProvider.startWatching` called `start()` but never `changePace(true)`, the documented fitness-app pattern to force the SDK into the active 'moving' state on demand.
- Fix (`gps/providers/native-provider.ts`): after `start()` resolves, call `changePace(true)` so location services engage the moment the user presses Start; surface start failures through the existing error callback.
- Secondary fix (same file): `requestPermissions()` returned `state.enabled !== undefined`, which is always `true` — so a user who *denied* location still got `true`, the native provider started, and the app recorded 0.00 km forever instead of falling back to timer-only mode. Replaced with an explicit `requestPermission()` call, accepting only `AUTHORIZATION_STATUS_ALWAYS` / `WHEN_IN_USE`; a denied user now drops to the timer fallback (elapsed time, no distance/pace).
- Requires `cap sync` + a device rebuild to verify — native plugin behaviour is not reproducible on web or in node tests. `NSMotionUsageDescription` and the location keys are already present in `Info.plist`.

## 2026-06-15 — Garmin-style "Acquiring GPS… → GPS ready" gate before a run starts

- Tapping Start Run (or "Start session" on a workout) no longer begins the clock immediately. It now arms GPS acquisition and shows a pre-run gate: an amber pulsing status while searching ("Acquiring GPS", with live fix accuracy in metres), flipping to a green "GPS ready" with a "Start run" button once a fix of acceptable accuracy (≤ 30 m, the same threshold at which distance counting begins) lands. The run clock starts only on the user's confirm tap, so elapsed time and distance both begin from a locked signal instead of the run's first ~200 m being lost while the SDK acquires. Soft gate by design: a quiet "Start anyway" lets indoor/treadmill/poor-signal users begin before lock, and a denied/unavailable location arms a timer-only fallback ("Start timer-only run").
- Architecture: `GpsTracker` gains an `arm()` / `confirmStart()` lifecycle alongside the existing `start()` (unchanged, so all prior tracker tests and the auto-advance behaviour are preserved). `arm()` holds in `acquiring` without setting the clock or accumulating distance and never auto-advances on a good fix; `confirmStart()` starts the clock and lets the next fix seed the route. New `isArmed()` / `isGpsReady()` / `cancelArm()`; the magic `30` accuracy literal is now the `ACCEPTABLE_ACCURACY_M` constant shared by the distance gate and "ready". `gps-events.ts` replaces `startTracking()` with `armTracking()` + `confirmStartTracking()` + `cancelTracking()` + `isArming()` / `getArmingData()`; guided voice now starts at confirm, not during acquisition. `record-view.ts` renders the gate (checked before the tracking branch because an armed tracker reports `acquiring`, which counts as active) and tears down the GPS watch if the user leaves the tab mid-acquisition. 7 new tracker tests; `tsc` + `lint:ui` clean. Web-rendered gate not yet device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — GPS auto-pause now re-renders the record controls (the "no unpause" bug)

- A running recording could sit in a speed-based auto-paused state while the on-screen button still read "Pause" and the elapsed timer was frozen, with no apparent way to resume. Root cause: `GpsTracker` fires `onAutoPause`/`onAutoResume` listeners when it detects you've stopped (`AUTO_PAUSE_STOP_SPEED_MPS = 0.5` for 5s, on by default), but `startTracking` in `gps-events.ts` only wired `onUpdate` and `onSplitComplete` — the auto-pause callbacks were never registered, so nothing re-rendered when the tracker auto-paused. Reproduced trivially by standing still while testing.
- Fix: wire `onAutoPause`/`onAutoResume` to the same re-render path the manual Pause/Resume toggle uses (`gps-events.ts`), at both the real-GPS and timer-fallback tracker sites. The button now flips to "Resume" on auto-pause and back to "Pause" on auto-resume; manual resume from an auto-paused state already worked (`resume()` clears the auto flag).
- Added an **Auto-pause** preference (Account → Preferences, default on). Off keeps the run clock running through stops, for people who don't want speed-based pausing. New optional state field `gpsAutoPause` is read at run start (`armTracking` passes it into `GpsTracker` at both construction sites) and applied mid-run via `setActiveTrackerAutoPause` → `GpsTracker.setAutoPauseEnabled` (which immediately resumes if currently auto-paused).

## 2026-06-15 — Race goal survives in-place plan rebuilds (forecast persistence fix)

- **Bug** (Tristan): "Goal times don't seem to always persist to the forecast page." A user-set goal would silently vanish from the forecast and revert to the initial-prediction fallback line ("your initial prediction" instead of "your goal").
- **Root cause**: `initializeSimulator` unconditionally cleared `s.raceGoalTimeSec` (running), and the triathlon/HYROX inits rebuilt `triConfig`/`hyroxConfig` from scratch without carrying `targetFinishTimeSec`. That clear is correct for a genuine re-onboarding to a *new distance* (the 2026-06-04 incident: a sub-3 marathon goal carried onto a fresh half plan). But `initializeSimulator` also runs for **in-place rebuilds at the same race** — runner-type change, add-sessions regen, mode toggle back (`account-view.ts`, `main-view.ts`). Those wiped the goal too, which read as "didn't persist."
- **Fix**: clear the goal only when the race **distance/format actually changes**.
  - Running: capture `prevPlanDist = s.rd` before overwriting it, then `if (prevPlanDist !== targetDistStr) s.raceGoalTimeSec = undefined` (`src/state/initialization.ts`).

## 2026-06-15 — HYROX splits: phone-friendly results copy/paste

- **Friction** (Tristan, on phone): the station-split paste step told users to "go to your result page" with no way to get there, and assumed a clean "Select All → copy". Mobile Safari has no Cmd+A and won't reliably show "Select All" on a rendered results page, so a perfect copy is unrealistic and most users would skip the splits.
- **Fixes** (both surfaces — onboarding `hyrox-setup.ts` and the standalone `log-prev-time-modal.ts`):
  - Added a bordered "Search hyresult.com →" link (mirrors `strava-guide-open`, no colour, `target="_blank"`) pointing at `https://hyresult.com/`. Chosen over the official `results.hyrox.com` (Tristan's call) because hyresult has a prominent name-search and a clean per-athlete "Timings" tab that copies far better than the official portal. Copy directs users to search their name and open the Timings tab.
  - Added a one-tap "Paste from clipboard" button (`navigator.clipboard.readText()`, graceful fallback to the manual box if blocked/empty — no new Capacitor plugin, works in WKWebView + browsers behind the tap gesture).
  - Auto-parse the moment text lands in the box (`paste` event + the clipboard button), so the "Parse" button is now a fallback rather than a required second tap.
  - Reworded the copy to lower the precision bar: "A rough selection is fine. We pull out the station times and ignore everything else." Partial reads now report "Found 6 of 8 station times. Add the other 2 below" instead of implying failure.
  - **Low-confidence flagging**: the parser now returns per-station provenance (`stationSource`). Times from the structured "In / Out" timestamp pair are reliable; times from the looser "name → nearest time" fallback can mis-grab a cumulative/diff column on a whitespace-collapsed mobile copy. Fallback-sourced fields get an amber (`--c-caution`) "check this" border and the status names how many to review; the flag clears the moment the user focuses the field. All fields were already editable with validation — this points the eye at the ones most likely wrong.
  - **"Does it add up" breakdown** (Tristan, onboarding only): the single "Total time" readout (which awkwardly flipped between station-sum and parsed race-total) is now a three-row breakdown — **Station total**, **Running + roxzone**, **Finish time**. The splits section only renders once a finish time exists, so the finish anchors the remainder: Running + roxzone = finish − stations, shown once all 8 stations are in (held with a "N in" prompt while partial). If the stations sum to more than the finish (a split typo), the run row goes to 0:00 in caution amber with "Your stations add up to more than your finish time." Removed the `totalDisplayMode`/`setRaceTotalDisplay` mode machinery in favour of a single state-driven `refreshTotalDisplay`. The `log-prev-time-modal` mirror has no total display at all (leaner surface) — left as a follow-up.
- **Refactor**: extracted the pure parser into `src/ui/wizard/steps/hyrox-results-parse.ts` (no DOM/window imports) so it's unit-testable; imported by both surfaces. The parser extraction logic is unchanged — it already tolerated junk lines and partial copies by scanning for station names anywhere in the text.

## 2026-06-15 — Apple Health connect auto-advances onboarding

- **Stuck** (Tristan, device report): on the "Show us where you're at" connect step, an Apple Watch user could tap "Apple Watch / Apple Health", connect successfully, and then have no obvious way forward. The Apple picker tile only morphed the faint "Continue without uploading" link into "Continue →"; unlike the Strava/Garmin OAuth-return paths, it never auto-advanced. The Garmin and No-watch tiles navigate to a new screen on tap, so the Apple tile uniquely left the user on the same screen with only a muted link to find.
- **Fix**: `markAppleHealthConnected()` (picker-tile branch, `connect-data.ts`) now mirrors the OAuth-return contract — morph Continue, set `skippedStrava:false`, then `maybeOfferAccountSave(() => nextStep())` to progress onwards immediately. The morph fires first so the connected status shows behind the account-save overlay (anonymous users); non-anonymous sessions advance straight through.
- **Scope guard**: the Garmin "connect both" hub branch is unchanged — it stays to nudge Strava (mirrors the Strava-return hold). The Back-into-step re-entry path calls `markContinueReady` directly (not `markAppleHealthConnected`), so backing into a step with Apple already connected does not bounce the user forward.
- **Connect memory parity** (Tristan question): confirmed `appleHealthConnected` is a persisted, typed state field (`state.ts:1079`), set on a successful connect and never cleared — both launch (`main.ts:1496`) and the connect step read it. Fixed one outlier: the picker-tile re-entry (`connect-data.ts`) checked only the physiology source, not the combined `hasPhysiologySource(s,'apple') || !!s.appleHealthConnected` flag every other site uses, so a supplementary-Apple user (non-Apple primary) could be re-offered the connect instead of seeing the remembered connected state.
- **Regression guard**: new `connect-data.test.ts` (11 tests, jsdom — first jsdom test in the repo; added `jsdom` devDep) mocks the native bridge (`isNativeiOS` / `connectAppleHealth`) and locks every branch: Apple-success auto-advances + marks `skippedStrava:false`, no-data/sync-error show recovery without advancing, web shows the iOS-app fallback (never the native connect), Garmin/No-watch route to the history hub, the deliberate-skip double-tap, and connect-memory on re-entry (incl. the parity fix). The auto-advance test fails against the pre-fix code. Full suite 3320 green.
- **Live browser walkthrough** (Playwright, iPhone viewport): picker renders the three tiles; Apple tile on web shows "Apple Health needs the iPhone app" (no dead tap); Continue double-tap arms then advances to the next step. Only console error is a benign Supabase 406 (empty snapshot row on a fresh anon account), unrelated.
- tsc + lint:ui clean. Logic + web paths verified by test and browser. The native HealthKit connect → auto-advance still needs final device verification (browser/node can't load `@capgo/capacitor-health`).

## 2026-06-15 — Manual sleep log now reaches readiness (no-watch users)

- **Symptom** (Tristan, dogfood): with no watch attached, logging a bad night's sleep barely (or never) moved the readiness score.
- **Root cause**: a data-flow mismatch. Manual sleep is written to `s.recoveryHistory` (`main-view.ts`, `home-view.ts`), but every `computeReadiness` caller passed `sleepHistory: s.physiologyHistory ?? []` — which holds only device (Garmin/Apple) nights. The earlier "merge manual into recovery" fix (`physioForRecovery`) was applied **only** to `computeRecoveryScore`, and it merged just *today's* manual night. Consequences: the sleep-cap decay never saw a multi-night manual bad-sleep streak, the 14-day chronic sleep average never accumulated manual nights, and a manual-only user never cleared `computeRecoveryScore`'s 3-night floor, so the recovery composite stayed "no data" and manual sleep only leaked through the weak fallback path.
- **Fix**: new canonical helper `mergeManualSleepHistory(physiology, recovery)` in `sleep-insights.ts` folds all `source: 'manual'` recovery nights into the physiology-shaped sleep history (device sleep wins per date; manual only fills uncovered dates or device rows with no sleepScore). Both readiness surfaces (`readiness-view.ts`, `home-view.ts`) now feed this merged array to **both** `computeRecoveryScore` and `computeReadiness({ sleepHistory })`, so the two surfaces stay in sync. Also fixed `coach-workout-modal.ts`, which previously ignored manual sleep entirely (read `lastPhys?.sleepScore`).
- 6 new tests (`sleep-insights.test.ts`); 3305 passing, tsc + lint:ui clean. NOT device-verified.

- **Problem 1 (stuck — on-demand/track-only)**: the commute step ("Do you run to work?") had a dead Back button. Track-only users have no race, so `race-target.ts:66` auto-skips itself forward (`nextStep()`) whenever `trackOnly === true`. The commute Back branch sent track-only users to `race-target`, which immediately bounced forward to commute again (`controller.ts:290`, race-target + trackOnly → commute). Net: Back did nothing, user stuck on commute.

So Back from the race picker silently jumped over the connect/PB screen. The "immediately-preceding step" comment was stale (`connect-data` + `about-you` sit between them in `STEP_ORDER`).
- **Fix 2**: race-target Back now goes to `manual-entry` if Strava was skipped, else `connect-data`, mirroring the forward routing.

Triathlon, cycling, and HYROX were already fully correct. No Back branch now targets an auto-advancing step (`race-target`/`initializing`), so the bounce/stuck class is eliminated.

## 2026-06-15 — Onboarding loading screen: overlapping label text on iOS (beta-user report)

- **Symptom**: the "Reading your training" loading card showed garbled, overlapping titles ("LcReading your physiologyry") — two step labels ghosted on top of each other.
- **Root cause**: the step label cross-fades via opacity over a `backdrop-filter` glass card, but the `textContent` swap fired after 220ms while the CSS fade ran for 0.45s. The old text was still ~50% visible at swap time, and WKWebView never re-rastered the half-faded old glyphs, so the new label painted on top of them. Same backdrop-filter-over-motion re-raster cliff documented in RUNBOOK.
- **Fix** (`src/ui/wizard/steps/review.ts`): swap the text only after the old text fully reaches opacity 0 — fade duration and swap delay now share one constant (`LABEL_FADE_MS = 240`, matched to the CSS transition). Added a `labelFadeTimer` guard so rapid step changes cancel any in-flight swap instead of stacking, and the timer is cleared on fresh mount so a stale swap can't fire against a detached node.
- Not yet device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Apple Health connect stuck on "Connecting…" (concurrent-attempt deadlock)

- **Problem**: in onboarding connect-data, a user who tapped the **Apple Watch tile** (granting HealthKit), then switched to **Garmin** and tapped **"Connect Apple Health"** in the hub before the first read resolved, fired two concurrent `connectAppleHealth()` calls. Two simultaneous capgo HealthKit reads deadlock the native bridge so neither resolves, and `triggerAppleHealth`'s `try/catch` only handles throws — not a hung promise — so the button stuck on "Connecting…" forever with no recovery path.
- **Fix** (three layers, `appleHealthSync.ts` + `connect-data.ts`):
  1. **In-flight guard** — `connectAppleHealth()` now returns the live promise if an attempt is already running, so a second tap rides the first instead of launching a concurrent native read.
  2. **Timeout race** — `triggerAppleHealth` races the connect against a 20s timeout (`APPLE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`); a hung read now falls back to the recovery card instead of sticking. A late real result still completes its state writes via the in-flight guard.
  3. **Already-connected guard** — the early-return now also checks the `appleHealthConnected` flag, not just the labelled `'apple'` physiology source. A Garmin/Strava user keeps their existing primary source, so connecting Apple sets the flag but never claims the source; the old check missed that and re-ran a full sync on every tap.
- tsc + lint:ui clean. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Conservative starting volume for beginners (30-min run cap)

- **Problem**: starting weekly volume (`initialization.ts:525`) was `runsPerWeek × 10 km` with no fitness/experience awareness, so a true beginner (incl. the no-PB seeded beginner from §BS) opened week 1 at ~30 km across 3 runs ≈ 10 km/run — a ~75-min run at a beginner's easy pace. Injury/adherence risk for "running under 6 months".
- **Fix**: for `beginner` / `total_beginner` / `hybrid` with no detected history, cap the starting per-run to **30 min at easy pace** (NHS Couch-to-5K graduation standard) via `cappedBeginnerStartWeeklyKm` (`beginner-fitness.ts`); the plan ramps up from there. Capping by *duration* auto-scales by pace from one rule: true beginner (VDOT 28) → ~11 km/wk at 3 runs; fit hybrid (VDOT 35) → ~15 km/wk. Never raises volume (returns the cap only when below the default); detected-history users keep their real volume.
- Science: `SCIENCE_LOG.md §BT`. 5 new unit tests (10 total in `beginner-fitness.test.ts`); full suite 3299 green; tsc + lint clean. Verified end-to-end: no-PB beginner now opens at 11 km/wk (was 30), seed + estimate copy intact, no NaN. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Coach contract: a personalised "here's how your plan works" beat after the reveal (all 3 modes)

- **Why**: the initial onboarding felt impersonal, so users skipped through it. We wanted a coach moment that explains the plan is built in phases, is not fixed, and adapts to training load, recovery, and real life (sport, festivals, illness, injury, less time).
- **What**: new step `coach-contract` (`src/ui/wizard/steps/coach-contract.ts`) — the last beat before entering the app, after the plan exists, in **all three plan modes**: running `plan-preview-v2 → coach-contract → workout-preview → main-view`; triathlon `tri-plan-forecast → coach-contract → main-view`; HYROX `initializing → coach-contract → main-view`. The CTA calls `nextStep()` so the controller routes per mode.
- **RUNNING is a rich showcase, all derived from the real generated plan** (the "visualise real data" rule): (1) **phase ribbon + weekly-training-load area chart** with the line **colour-changing by phase** (base→taper); load (TSS) not km, because km under-counts minute-prescribed quality work (see km-artifact note below); (2) **per-phase session-mix as coloured vertical stacked columns** (base→taper left-to-right; easy/long = blues, tempo/speed = amber/coral; quality grows up the column toward race day); (3) **runner-type bias** surfaced truthfully (`applyRunnerTypeBias`: speed-biased → more threshold, endurance-biased → more VO2); (4) **cross-training** "your sport, built in" card with REAL `computeUniversalLoad` numbers (e.g. 60-min cycling ≈ 40 TSS ≈ 3.9 km easy), honest framing (scheduled alongside; load adaptation fires on logging, not a planning-time km cut); (5) a **"Built to flex around you"** adaptivity showcase (coloured dots) — adjust any session's length (rewrites pace targets), swap or generate a session, log anything and we rebalance — plus a rewritten life-events contract that explicitly covers **injury / illness / travel** (the old "your sport… any sport" row made no sense — those are the user's planned sports, not disruptions). TRIATHLON / HYROX keep personalised text cards with the same framing.
- **km-vs-load artifact found (Tristan flagged "why is week 1 the highest mileage?")**: weekly **km** under-counts build/peak weeks because their quality sessions are minute-prescribed (`marathon_pace "26min @ MP"` → 0 km; `vo2 "5×4min (~1km)"` → ~1 km), while base threshold sessions carry km warm-up/cool-down — so a km chart invents a "volume drop". Charting **weekly TSS** (canonical Load Currency) fixes it: the real arc climbs base ~420-470 → build 493 → peak 497 → taper 322→301, with recovery-week dips. ⚠️ The **Stats forecast KM chart (`buildForecastKmChart`) has the same under-count** — flagged, not yet fixed.
- **Shared `plan-shape.ts`**: extracted `plannedWeekKm` + `parseDistanceKm` out of `stats-view.ts` into `src/calculations/plan-shape.ts` and added `derivePlanShape()` (per-week km, phase segments, session-mix counts). Stats now imports `plannedWeekKm` from there, so the coach page and the Stats forecast charts read identical km from one source.
- **Personalised from real data**: `commonKnowFragments()` gates every shared clause on a real signal — `ctlBaseline ≥ 20`, `hrCalibratedVdot.confidence !== 'none'`, `recurringActivities` sports (via `SPORT_LABELS`/`SPORT_ALIASES`), `commuteConfig.enabled`. The "when life gets in the way" sport row leads with their actual sport. Absent signals fall back to honest generic phrasing.
- **Copy is centralised + tweakable**: running wording lives in `buildRunningView` + its section builders; tri/HYROX in `buildTriContent` / `buildHyroxContent`. Page shell (style, header, CTA) is shared.
- **CTA fix**: the plan-ready page button was "See your sessions" but now leads to the coach page, so it reads "See how it works"; the coach page's button is "See your sessions" (running) / "Start training" (tri/HYROX).
- **Voice deviation (intentional, user-requested)**: first-person coach voice, a deliberate departure from the app's third-person consultant default, kept tight and padding-free. No em dashes, no emoji, monochrome, no accent colour.
- **Wiring**: `OnboardingStep` type; renderer case; `plan-preview-v2` CTA → `coach-contract`; controller forward branch (running → workout-preview, tri/HYROX → complete+main-view), `tri-plan-forecast` → `coach-contract`, HYROX `initializing` → `coach-contract`; mode-aware back-nav; `initWizard` migration allowlist. Visual continuity with the screen before it.
- tsc clean (0 errors); `lint:ui` clean. NOT device-verified — needs a dogfood run through onboarding in each mode; copy not yet reviewed by Tristan.
