## 2026-06-15 — Beginners without a PB are no longer walled out of onboarding

- **Problem**: a running plan needs a fitness anchor, so `initialization.ts` failed with "No personal bests provided" and review disabled "Build my plan" when `pbs` was empty. That blocked exactly the users least likely to know a 5K time — true beginners and cross-sport hybrids.
- **Fix**: for `beginner` / `total_beginner` / `hybrid`, seed a conservative DERIVED 5K instead of blocking (`beginner-fitness.ts`): VDOT 28 (beginner band floor, ≈ 32:30 5K) or VDOT 35 (hybrid → novice floor). Anchors are the documented Daniels/Pfitzinger band floors already in the codebase — not invented. `initialization.ts` seeds it + sets `startingFitnessEstimated`; `review.ts` lets these levels through with an honest note instead of the blocking hint; `plan-preview-v2.ts` flags the prediction as an estimate. Marked so it yields to real runs (the launch blend already folds in real pace/HR/volume) and is overwritten the moment a real PB is entered.
- **Other levels unchanged**: "novice — occasional 5/10K", "intermediate — raced before", etc. still require a real PB (they imply a known time).
- Science: `SCIENCE_LOG.md §BS`. 5 new unit tests; full suite 3294 green; tsc + lint clean. Verified end-to-end in-browser: no-PB beginner builds an 8-week 5K plan, starts at VDOT ~27.3, no NaN, honest estimate copy on review + plan-preview. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Plan drag-to-reorder: doubled/ghost cards on iOS fixed (beta-user report)

- **Symptom**: dragging a session to reorder on the iOS app showed two overlapping translucent cards in odd positions (screenshot: a "Running Strength A" ghost floating over Mon/Tue plus another near Wed).
- **Root cause**: the workout cards carry `draggable="true"` for desktop HTML5 drag. In WKWebView (and mobile Safari) that same attribute makes the OS lift its **own** native long-press drag preview, which renders on top of our custom `_touchClone`. Two ghosts at once.
- **Fix**: new `isTouchPrimary()` in `src/utils/platform.ts` (native shell or `(pointer: coarse)`). On touch-primary devices the plan views set `card.draggable = false` so only the custom touch DnD runs; desktop keeps the attribute for mouse drag. Applied in `src/ui/plan-view.ts` (running) and `src/ui/triathlon/plan-view.ts` (tri). HYROX cards never had `draggable`, so no conflict there.
- **Deeper fix (running only)**: the touch DnD was wired inline in `wirePlanHandlers` (initial render) but the post-reorder local re-render goes through `wireCardScopedHandlers`, which only re-wired the desktop HTML5 drag. So after the first touch reorder the touch handlers were gone *and* `draggable` reverted to `true` (native ghost returned). Extracted the touch DnD into a module-level `wirePlanCardTouchDnd(root, viewWeek)` now called from both paths, so reorder works repeatedly and the draggable disable re-applies on every re-render. Tri (`wireTriDayList` re-wires both) and HYROX (full re-render) never had this divergence. Removed the dead `_touchDraggingCard` flag (its swipe-handler consumer was already gone).
- **Authoritative fix (the real lever)**: `el.draggable = false` in JS does NOT reliably stop the native lift on iOS. The native WKWebView drag preview is driven by the `-webkit-user-drag` CSS property, which was absent from the whole codebase. Added a `@media (hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)` rule in `src/styles.css` setting `-webkit-user-drag:none` + `-webkit-touch-callout:none` + `user-select:none` on `.plan-workout-card`, `.tri-workout-card`, `.hyrox-workout-card`. This is render-path independent (never needs re-applying) so it can't regress through a re-wire. Verified the rule survives minification into the built CSS bundle.
- Three independent layers now: `isTouchPrimary()` + JS `draggable=false` (both render paths), the shared touch-wiring helper, and the CSS `-webkit-user-drag` suppression.
- **Ship note**: web-asset-only change (JS + CSS), so it needs a `npx cap copy ios` (or `cap sync`) + app rebuild to reach the device. Not yet device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Onboarding intro/transition perf: prewarm the hero, opacity-only ring entrances (beta-user report)

Tristan tested on iPhone: the "Adapts to everything you do." intro slide jolted then froze on load, tapping through slides felt laggy, and step-to-step transitions across onboarding felt slow. Root cause was the page-flair ring background animating `transform: scale()` on stroked SVG rings, which forces a per-frame re-raster on WKWebView (the documented iOS cliff, RUNBOOK → Backgrounds stuttering, Cause 1).

- **Killed the click-wave on intro slides** (`welcome.ts`): tapping Next no longer re-fires `triggerRingWave` (it scaled all 5 rings to 1.8x/2.4x every tap). The background is now a persistent, independent backdrop; only the card content swaps.
- **Prewarm the hero during name entry**: `renderSlides` → `buildSlides(host, …)` can now build the heavy slides DOM off-screen (opacity 0, fixed) ~600ms after the welcome screen settles, so the cold build + first raster happens while the user types their name instead of on the "Build my plan" tap. At reveal, `playIntro()` replays the ring bloom + pulse + drift on warm DOM (class remove/reflow/re-add) so the wow still plays live, and fades the prewarmed layer in over the welcome screen. Fast-tap fallback builds cold in the container if prewarm hasn't run.
- **Opacity-only `'small'` ring entrance** (`page-flair.ts`): the default entrance used by EVERY non-intro wizard step now fades in (opacity 0→1) instead of scaling `0.85→1`. Removes the per-transition re-raster across all 19 steps. Only the prewarmed intro hero (`entrance:'large'`) keeps its scale bloom. Matches the team's "entrance keyframes never transform" rule (tab-entrance perf precedent).
- Typecheck + `lint:ui` clean. NOT yet device-verified — needs an on-device pass to confirm the intro is smooth and transitions feel snappy.

## 2026-06-15 — OAuth callback idempotent: kills the `invalid_state` error page after a successful connect (beta-user report)

Tristan connected Strava on device and the in-app Safari sheet showed raw JSON `{"error":"invalid_state","details":null}` (on the `*.supabase.co` callback host). The connection itself had succeeded — the error was cosmetic but alarming.

- **Root cause**: `strava-auth-callback` (and `garmin-auth-callback`) `DELETE`d the ephemeral `*_auth_requests` row on success. On native iOS the SFSafariViewController can't navigate the `mosaic://oauth` redirect, so it lingers and re-requests the callback URL (or the user reloads — note the reload button in the screenshot). The second hit finds no row → `invalid_state`. `details:null` confirmed the DB query succeeded with zero rows (not a DB error), i.e. the row had already been consumed by the first, successful run. No TTL/cron purges the table, so the only way the row vanishes is a prior successful callback.
- **Fix — idempotent callbacks**: stop deleting. New `consumed_at` column (migration `20260615_oauth_idempotent_callback.sql`) on both `strava_auth_requests` and `garmin_auth_requests`. The callback now: (1) looks up the row; no row → friendly HTML page with a `mosaic://oauth` "Return to Mosaic" button instead of raw JSON; (2) row already `consumed_at` → replay the success redirect (the single-use provider `code` is NOT re-exchanged); (3) otherwise atomically claim the row (`update … where consumed_at is null`) so two near-simultaneous hits can't both run the token exchange, then proceed. Opportunistic purge deletes consumed rows older than an hour so the table doesn't grow.
- Mirrored across both Strava and Garmin callbacks (mirror rule). Deploying the new functions also lands the previously-staged `mosaic://oauth` allowlist (ISSUE-284).
- **DEPLOYED to prod 2026-06-15**: `consumed_at` column added to both `*_auth_requests` via the Management API (scoped — deliberately NOT `db push`, which would have applied 9 unrelated pending migrations), then both callback functions deployed. No client/`cap sync` change. Not yet device-verified. (Side notes: prod has 10 local migrations unapplied since `20260507`; the Supabase access token is valid again — the "revoked" note was stale.)
- **Follow-up same day — "Safari cannot open the page because the address is invalid"**: a second device report. Cause: SFSafariViewController refuses to follow an HTTP **302 to a custom scheme** (`mosaic://`). First tried a 200 HTML page doing the hop via `location.replace(...)` in JS — but hit a hard blocker: the **Supabase edge gateway force-rewrites every response Content-Type to `text/plain`** (verified twice via curl, even with a `Headers` instance), so the HTML rendered as raw source and the script never ran. Two walls at once.
- **Resolution — proper native OAuth via ASWebAuthenticationSession** (Tristan chose this over a web-bridge workaround; matches the "native app is the priority" stance). New `@mosaic/web-auth` Capacitor plugin (`ios-plugins/web-auth/`, mirrors `@mosaic/health-extras`): a thin Swift wrapper around `ASWebAuthenticationSession` exposing `start({url, callbackScheme})`. iOS's purpose-built OAuth view monitors navigation, intercepts the first `mosaic://` URL (including the 302 redirect target), dismisses itself, and returns the callback URL to JS — no SFSafariViewController, no deep-link round-trip, no HTML. `src/data/oauth-native.ts` rewritten to `runNativeOAuth(authorizeUrl)` returning the callback params; `startStravaConnect`/`startGarminConnect` re-enter with `?strava=connected`/`?garmin=connected` (same handler as web). Removed the `@capacitor/browser` open + `appUrlOpen` listener (main.ts). Edge `successRedirect` reverted to a plain 302 → `mosaic://` (ASWebAuth catches it). `Package.swift` name `MosaicWebAuth` matches Capacitor's derivation (verified in the generated iOS Package.swift — no case-mismatch blocker). Typecheck + 3308 tests green, `npx vite build` + `cap sync ios` run. **NEEDS a TestFlight repush** (native plugin): Xcode rebuild + archive + upload. Edge functions already redeployed. Not device-verified.

## 2026-06-15 — Apple Health connect: dead-end error → honest inline recovery (beta-user report)

Tristan tapped "Apple Health" in onboarding and got a tiny red dead-end ("Permissions not granted. Open Settings → Privacy → Health → Mosaic"); a second report showed the hub's "Connect Apple Health" button doing nothing at all. Two root causes:

- **Conflation**: `connectAppleHealth` treated *any* empty physiology result as `permission-denied` (`appleHealthSync.ts`). But HealthKit deliberately never tells an app whether a read was denied vs simply empty (`getRequestStatusForAuthorization` returns `.unnecessary` for both once answered — verified in the capgo plugin's `readAuthorizationStatus`, `Health.swift:606`). So the "denied" claim was unprovable. Renamed the reason to honest `'no-data'`; the copy no longer asserts denial.
- **Off-screen feedback**: the failure wrote to `#cd-apple-error`, a `<p>` at the very bottom of the page. In the Garmin hub it sits below every card → the button looked completely dead. And iOS never re-presents the permission sheet once answered, so re-tapping Connect silently re-fails forever.

Fixes:
- **Native `openAppSettings()`** added to the health-extras Swift plugin (`UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`) + TS wrapper in `healthExtras.ts`. One tap into iOS Settings; copy points the rest of the way to Privacy & Security → Health → Mosaic (HealthKit toggles don't render on the app's own settings page).
- **Inline recovery cards** (`connect-data.ts`): on no-data, a recovery card appears *next to the button tapped* — picker phase gets a full card (Open Settings + "Use Strava or upload instead" → jumps to the hub); the Garmin hub gets an inline slot inside the Apple Health card (Open Settings; Strava/upload already on-screen). Hub Connect button now shows a "Connecting…" state.
- Removed the dead `#cd-apple-error` element. **Needs `cap sync ios` + device rebuild** (new native method) before the Open Settings button works; not yet device-verified.

## 2026-06-13 — Phone polish: Match Activities "stuck", native Strava/Garmin OAuth, safe-area sweep

Three reported phone issues.

**1. Users stuck on "Match Activities."** The only way forward was a small "Save" chip in the top-right header that collided with the status-bar icons; users scrolled looking for a bottom action and found none. Added a persistent **full-width bottom action bar** (`matching-screen.ts`) carrying the primary Save (`Save · N to Excess Load` when items are unplaced), with `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`. Removed the top-corner chip; header is now back + centered title only. Verified in-browser (full-width button pinned bottom, fires the save handler).

**1b. Match Activities auto-opens at most once per day, and never on plan day 1** (`activitySync.ts → processPendingCrossTraining`, the single funnel for both launch and sync). Two gates: (a) if `daysSinceStart(planStartDate) < 1` it returns early — on the first day of a plan (which may not be a Monday) there is no elapsed planned-session day to reconcile, so the screen would only confuse; (b) a new `Week.autoReviewShownDate` (local YYYY-MM-DD) caps the auto-open to once per calendar day — a new activity (or anything still unmatched) re-opens it once the next day, but it never re-nags on every launch/sync within a day. The "Review" button (home + plan) reopens it on demand any time. Verified against the real funnel: day-1 suppressed, day-4 shows once, same-day repeat suppressed, next-day shows again; full unit suite 3289 green; 5-mode onboarding sweep 35 renders 0 crashes.

**2. Strava "the application couldn't be opened" → refreshed to start.** Root cause: native OAuth was disabled, so connect ran `window.location.href = stravaUrl` with `appOrigin: capacitor://localhost`; after auth iOS can't reopen that scheme, and the whole-WebView navigation cold-reloaded onboarding. Enabled the native deep-link path (`NATIVE_OAUTH_ENABLED = true`): in-app browser + `mosaic://oauth` return via `appUrlOpen` (app stays alive; onboarding survives, with the existing `oauthPending` self-heal as backstop). Ran `cap sync ios` so `@capacitor/app` + `@capacitor/browser` register natively (`AppPlugin` + `CAPBrowserPlugin`). Routed account-view's two inline OAuth starts (which hardcoded `capacitor://localhost`) through the native-aware `startStravaConnect`/`startGarminConnect`. **Requires deploying** `strava-auth-callback` + `garmin-auth-callback` (repo code has the `mosaic://oauth` allowlist + manual Location header; live versions v30/v47 don't) — MCP was read-only so this is a manual `supabase functions deploy`. Plus a fresh native build + device test.

**3. Safe-area sweep.** Ten detail-view sticky headers (`leg-load`, `freshness`, `load-taper`, `sleep`, `mtl-load`, `injury-risk`, `strain`, `rolling-load`, `readiness`, `recovery`) used `position:sticky;top:0`, pinning them under the notch when scrolled on large-Dynamic-Island phones; changed to `top:env(safe-area-inset-top)` (no change at rest, pins below the notch when stuck — no double-inset because the rest position comes from the `.safe-top-bleed` root). Wizard fixed bottom buttons (Back, Return-to-plan) got `bottom: calc(32px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`. Onboarding step tops were already correct (content sits in `#app-root` inside the body's `env()` padding). tsc + lint:ui clean. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-12 — Deep-dive: OAuth + onboarding driven live in a browser (Playwright)

Ran the actual app on the dev server and drove the flows, rather than relying on unit tests alone. Two real native-OAuth bugs found by tracing the path against the installed plugin APIs, plus live confirmation of the JS paths.

- **Fixed — `Browser.open` used `presentationStyle: 'popover'`** (`oauth-native.ts`). Per `@capacitor/browser`, popover is an iPad affordance; on iPhone the right (and default) OAuth style is `'fullscreen'`. Changed.
- **Fixed — callback redirect to a custom scheme could be rejected.** Deno's `Response.redirect()` can reject a non-http(s) URL, so redirecting to `mosaic://oauth` risked throwing. Both `strava-auth-callback` and `garmin-auth-callback` now emit the native-scheme redirect via a manual `Location` header (bulletproof for any scheme); http/https origins keep `Response.redirect` unchanged. (Staged with the rest of the native-OAuth backend change.)
- **Verified live (web JS paths, which the native flow reuses):**
  - Self-heal abandoned branch: set `oauthPending` with no server token → reload → `recoverPendingStravaOAuth` re-checked the server, found no token, cleared the marker (clean retry). ✓
  - OAuth success return (`?strava=connected&sex=M&weight=72`): set `stravaConnected`, prefilled `biologicalSex`/`bodyWeightKg` from the callback params, stripped the URL, surfaced account-save, then advanced. ✓ (This is exactly what the native deep-link return re-enters into.)
  - Onboarding advances cleanly welcome → goals → connect-data → race-target → schedule → review with no dead ends or crashes; review is NaN-safe for a no-activity user (`--` fallbacks, honest "rough estimate" VO2max caption, FRIEND placement). ✓
- **Audit correction:** running mode **deliberately** skips `about-you` (`controller.ts:260-266` — age is captured on the schedule step, sex pre-fills from Strava). An earlier audit wrongly listed `about-you` in the running path; the live drive caught the real routing. No missing-age bug.

## 2026-06-12 — Match Activities header under the iOS status bar (safe-area on full-screen takeovers)

- **Symptom** (device screenshot): the Match Activities screen's header — Cancel, title, Save — rendered behind the iOS status bar clock/battery, so Save was effectively invisible and untappable.
- **Root cause**: `#activity-review-overlay` (`activity-review.ts`) is `position:fixed;inset:0`. Fixed elements escape the body's `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)` scaffold (`styles.css`), so every screen the overlay hosts (matching entry, Activity Review, Match Activities) started its header at y=0 under the status bar. Web unaffected (`env()` = 0), which is why it only showed on device.

Also added `padding-bottom:env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` to the matching screen's scroll body so the last row clears the home indicator.
- **Never again**: audited every `position:fixed` + `inset:0` surface in `src/ui/**` — all others are centered modals, bottom sheets (bottom-inset padded), or `pointer-events:none` flair layers; this was the only top-anchored takeover. Added ui-lint rule `takeover-no-safe-top` (fixed + inset:0 + column layout without `safe-area-inset-top`, centered layouts exempt) and a rule to `UX_PATTERNS.md → Overlays and Modals`. The lint rule is content-level, not line-level: it catches the signature in single-line cssText, multi-line template literals, `['…'].join(';')` styles, and Tailwind `fixed inset-0 flex-col` classes (canary-verified all four shapes fail the lint; lint runs inside `npm run build`). tsc + lint:ui clean.
- **Browser-verified with emulated insets** (Playwright + CDP `Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride`, iPhone viewport 393×852, top=59/bottom=34): seeded the reviewer demo athlete, injected 4 fake pending activities, drove the real `showActivityReview` flow to the Match Activities screen. With the fix: overlay computed `padding-top:59px`, Cancel/Save at y=76–78px (below the status bar), Save hittable at its centre via `elementFromPoint`. Negative control: removing the padding in-page put Save at y=17px (the original bug), confirming the check detects it. WKWebView resolves `env()` natively, so device behaviour should match; a quick on-device glance remains the final confirmation.

Added a bordered "Go back" recovery pill that calls `previousStep()` so they can adjust inputs (e.g. add a PB) and retry.
- **Hardened — Strava OAuth return on native iOS (redirect-independent self-heal)**: the connect flow uses a full-page `window.location.href` redirect (`stravaSync.ts:78`) and relies on the callback bouncing back with `?strava=connected`. On a Capacitor iOS build that bounce can drop the query string (WKWebView reloads the cached app without it), stranding the user mid-onboarding even though the token landed server-side. Rather than rewrite the redirect blind (it works on web and Strava is the daily-used source), added a self-heal that doesn't depend on the redirect: tapping Connect persists `onboarding.oauthPending`, and on the next `connect-data` render `recoverPendingStravaOAuth` re-checks the `strava_tokens` table via `isStravaConnected()` and completes the same success path (advance / Apple-Health nudge) if the token exists, or clears the marker for a clean retry if not. JS-only; the web path is byte-for-byte unchanged. New optional state field `OnboardingState.oauthPending`.
- **Built (gated off) — proper in-app-browser OAuth for iOS** (app-first, per Tristan's "long-term focus is the app"): the ideal native flow now exists end-to-end behind `NATIVE_OAUTH_ENABLED` (default false). On native iOS it opens the authorize page in an `SFSafariViewController` (`@capacitor/browser`, installed) and returns via a `mosaic://oauth` deep link caught by `@capacitor/app` `appUrlOpen` (`src/data/oauth-native.ts`), re-entering the app with the standard `?strava=connected` query so the existing tested return handler runs. The `mosaic://` scheme is registered in `Info.plist`; the `strava/garmin-auth-callback` open-redirect guards have `mosaic://oauth` added to an exact-match `NATIVE_RETURN_ALLOWLIST` (staged, **not deployed**). Gated so the half-deploy state is safe — while off, native keeps the redirect + self-heal; web is unchanged. Enabling = `cap sync` + deploy the two callbacks + flip the flag + rebuild + device-test (full runbook in `docs/RUNBOOK.md → Native OAuth`). `tsc` + `vitest` (3289) + `vite build` + `lint:ui` all green. Native path NOT device-verified (can't be, until the rebuild). ISSUE-284 updated.

## 2026-06-12 — Onboarding intro laggy to flick through on iPhone (both background perf cliffs at once)

- **Symptom**: the post-name onboarding slides (`welcome.ts → renderSlides`) were "super laggy to flick through" on iPhone testing.
- **Root cause**: the intro stacked both documented iOS background perf cliffs (RUNBOOK → "Backgrounds stuttering / flashing / flickering") on the same screen.
  - **Cause 1 (filter + transform animation)**: `buildRingBackground`'s rings had been re-given `feGaussianBlur`/drop-shadow filters (`page-flair.ts` `filterDefs`, applied per `ring.depth`). Those exact ring groups animate their transform (entrance bloom, 9s pulse, 6.5s drift, and a 3.6s `triggerRingWave` fired on *every* "Next" tap), so the filtered region re-rasterized every frame → ~30fps. The RUNBOOK's "all page-flair backgrounds are already filter-free" claim had silently regressed.
  - **Cause 2 (`backdrop-filter` over motion)**: the slide card used `backdrop-filter:blur(24px)` (the heaviest blur in the app) directly over those moving rings, re-sampling the background every frame. The skip button added another `blur(10px)` over the same rings.
- **Fix**:
  - Removed the SVG filters from `buildRingBackground` rings (`page-flair.ts`) — restores the intended filter-free state. Crisp rings hold 60fps and are near-identical at rest. Benefits **every** hero page (stats / plan / forecast / detail views), not just the intro. Added a load-bearing comment so the filters don't get re-added a third time.
  - Lightened the intro slide card from `blur(24px)` glass to a solid `rgba(255,255,255,0.9)` backing (no `backdrop-filter`), and the skip button from `blur(10px)` glass to the same solid. The wave/pulse/entrance flair is kept — with filter-free rings and a non-resampling card, the motion now runs smoothly behind and around the card.
  - Removed `backdrop-filter` from the slide "Next" button (`m-btn-glass`'s `blur(20px)` overridden inline to a solid `rgba(255,255,255,0.92)` fill). Browser frame profiling showed this was the last contributor: its blur reached past the 0.9 card to the rings bleeding through and re-sampled them every frame during the wave. Making the card fully opaque did NOT fix it (the blur radius reaches the moving layer regardless); only dropping the button's backdrop-filter did.
- **Verified in a desktop browser** (RUNBOOK frame-timing method, `requestAnimationFrame` sampling): idle/pulse = 60fps / 0 dropped frames; the per-tap wave animation = 60fps / 0 dropped frames / 17.7ms max. A real "Next" tap leaves a single ~1-frame hitch (33–65ms) at the instant of tap — that's the synchronous `innerHTML` card-content swap (JS), not the background; the animation around it is smooth. tsc + lint:ui clean. Still worth a final flick-test on Tristan's iPhone.
- **Onboarding regression sweep** (the ring + `m-btn-glass` changes touch every wizard step): drove all 5 paths in-browser via `wizardGoTo` — running, triathlon, HYROX, cycling, just-track — 35+ step renders. **Zero crashes, zero blank screens, rings render on every step that should have them.** `review` populates fully after its ~1.8s async data wait ("Here's what we found" + PB percentile cards); `race-target` correctly auto-skips when `trackOnly` is pre-set (`race-target.ts:66`). Visual spot-checks (goals disclaimer, triathlon-setup, intro) confirm the crisp filter-free rings + solid cards read clean app-wide. The triathlon flow was then driven **end-to-end through real plan generation** (triathlon-setup → race pick → tri-past-race → tri-workout-preview → commute → review → initializing → tri-plan-forecast): the plan generated without error and `tri-plan-forecast` rendered live data (projected 70.3 finish 6:00:33 + per-discipline Add-training levers). Every onboarding path verified.

## 2026-06-12 — Apple Health permission popup never appeared (invalid data type aborted the request)

- **Root cause**: `ALL_READ_TYPES` in `appleHealthSync.ts` passed `'appleExerciseTime'` to `@capgo/capacitor-health`'s `requestAuthorization`. That string is not in the plugin's `HealthDataType` union. The native `parseTypesWithWorkouts` throws `invalidDataType` on the first unrecognised type, and the throw happens **before** `healthStore.requestAuthorization` is called, so iOS never presented the permission sheet. Every Apple Health user tapped "Connect Apple Health", saw no popup, and got a silent `permission-denied`.
- **Fix**: removed `'appleExerciseTime'` from the authorization set and added `'workouts'` (which the activity import actually reads via `queryWorkouts` but was never being authorized). The remaining types are all valid capgo identifiers, so the combined sheet now appears for everyone.
- Also wrapped the `queryAggregated('appleExerciseTime')` call in `syncAppleHealthPhysiology` with `.catch(() => ({ samples: [] }))` — that same unsupported type would otherwise reject the whole physiology `Promise.all` and fail the entire sleep/HRV/RHR/steps sync. Apple exercise-ring active minutes degrade to "unavailable" (Garmin still supplies `activeMinutes`); the rest of physiology syncs normally.
- Added a load-bearing comment on `ALL_READ_TYPES`: a single unsupported type string suppresses the popup for everyone, so don't add types the capgo plugin can't map.
- **Prevention (so this bug class can't recur)**: introduced `CAPGO_READ_TYPES` (the plugin's `HealthDataType` union plus `'workouts'`) as a single source of truth and typed `ALL_READ_TYPES` as `CapgoReadType[]` — adding an unmappable type is now a **compile error** instead of a silent runtime failure. The call site's `as any` was narrowed to `as HealthDataType[]` (only bridges the plugin's public type omitting `'workouts'`). New `capgo-read-types.test.ts` parses the plugin's shipped `definitions.d.ts` and fails the build if our mirror drifts, so a future plugin upgrade that renames/drops a type is caught in CI, not on device.

## 2026-06-12 — Apple Health works for all watches, not just Apple Watch (sleep-score gap)

- Audited the whole Apple Health ingestion path (`appleHealthSync.ts`) for Apple-Watch-only assumptions, since HealthKit is an aggregation layer (Garmin, Coros, Polar, Suunto, Fitbit, Strava all sync into it). Found it largely source-agnostic already: `queryWorkouts` returns workouts from **all** sources (no bundle-id filter), resting HR / HRV (SDNN) / steps read universally, the SDNN→RMSSD conversion is correct for every source (HealthKit's HRV type is always SDNN), and missing per-sample HR degrades gracefully to duration/calories TSS.
- **Real gap fixed — sleep score**: `computeSleepScore` weights deep 25% + REM 20%. Watches that write only a generic `'asleep'` state to HealthKit (no stage breakdown — common on non-Apple devices) report `deepSec = 0, remSec = 0`, which hard-capped every night at **55/100** regardless of duration and dragged Readiness down. Now, when a source reports no architecture, the score is computed on duration alone (renormalising the 55% duration weight to 100%; no new constants). Staged nights keep the full 55/25/20 formula, so genuinely poor architecture is still penalised. Guarded by `sleep-score.test.ts` (4 cases). SCIENCE_LOG updated under "Stage-less sources".
- **Expected, documented degradations (inherent HealthKit limits, not bugs)**: VO2max and exercise-ring active minutes are Apple-Watch-only (other brands don't write them to HealthKit). HR zones / iTRIMP / HR-based rep detection require a per-sample HR stream that Garmin/Coros/Polar typically don't bridge to HealthKit — those activities fall back to duration/calories TSS and self-heal via `healMissingITrimp` if RHR/maxHR arrive later.

## 2026-06-10 — Cross-device enrichment sync: a Strava file uploaded on web shows up on the phone

- **Problem**: the plan backup (`user_plan_settings`) is one full-state snapshot, last-writer-wins, restored only when localStorage is empty. So an activity enriched on the web app never reached an already-running phone, and a later phone save could clobber it.
- **Fix**: enrichment is taken out of that blob into its own per-activity table (`activity_enrichments`), keyed by the activity's stable `garminId`. New `src/data/enrichmentSync.ts`: `pushEnrichment` (called from `applyEnrichment`) writes one row; `mergeEnrichmentsFromServer` (launch + foreground) merges rows into local thin activities, **rich-over-thin only** so it never downgrades or clobbers. Safe without conflict resolution because enrichment is monotonic (only adds detail) — per-activity last-writer-wins is correct.
- **Migration required** (not applied — MCP is read-only): create `activity_enrichments` with owner-only RLS. Exact SQL in `docs/SHARE_TO_MOSAIC.md`. The TS no-ops until the table exists, so it ships safely ahead of the migration.
- 5 new tests for the pure merge rule (`applyEnrichmentPayloads`). tsc + lint:ui clean; affected suites green. Not device-verified.

## 2026-06-10 — Drop-a-file import that auto-attaches to the right run + native "Share to Mosaic" seam

- **Goal**: make the manual Strava-file upload as easy as a phone allows, for the users who need it (a non-Apple watch, e.g. Garmin, that isn't in the Strava beta 10 — Garmin bridges only average HR through Apple Health; Apple Watch users are fully covered by the watch's own Health write).

Parses the file, scans live state for a **thin** activity (`isThinActivity`) whose start + duration match (`fileMatchesActual`, ±10 min / ±15%), and enriches that record in place (provenance preserved, matcher guard intact) — so the user never has to locate the run. Imports as a new activity only when nothing matches. Only thin rows are auto-attached; an already-rich run is left to the matcher's dedup so we never overwrite better data.

## 2026-06-10 — Per-activity "Add detail from Strava" now accepts the gzipped file Strava actually gives you

- **Bug**: the per-activity enrich upload (`parseActivityFileToStreams`, `fitImport.ts`) only handled bare `.fit/.gpx/.tcx`. Strava's "Export Original" for a Garmin activity commonly returns a gzipped file (`.fit.gz`), and the iOS picker sometimes strips the `.gz` suffix. The `<input accept=".fit,.gpx,.tcx">` would not even show those files, and forcing one through threw "Unsupported file type". So the headline per-activity flow failed on the exact file Strava hands you, even though the bulk-archive path had gunzipped `.gz` for ages.
- **Fix**: `parseActivityFileToStreams` now transparently gunzips, detecting gzip by extension **or** the magic number (0x1f 0x8b) so a suffix-stripped file still works, then dispatches by inner extension with a content-sniff fallback (XML for GPX/TCX, the ".FIT" tag at byte 8 for FIT). The picker `accept` gains `.gz`; the activity-detail copy notes "a .fit or a .fit.gz, either works". Single fix covers both the per-activity enrich and the single-file importer (shared parser). 3 new gzip regression tests.

## 2026-06-09 — HealthKit-first ingestion: per-activity Strava enrichment + guided history

- **Context (scale, not a bug)**: Garmin ORTO is unapproved and Strava is capped at 10 athletes, so neither API scales. HealthKit is the universal iOS pipe (Garmin, COROS, Polar, Apple Watch all write into Apple Health, no partner approval needed). The catch (device-confirmed): a Garmin watch syncing into Apple Health delivers **average HR + duration only** — HR zones, splits, route and iTRIMP drop at the boundary. So a HealthKit-sourced run is thin.
- **Per-activity "Add detail from Strava" (centrepiece)**: from a thin activity's detail page, the user uploads that activity's original file (Strava "Export Original" .fit) and the rich fields merge into the **existing** record in place — no duplicate. New pure `src/data/activity-enrich-merge.ts` (`enrichActualFromParsedRow`) reuses the Strava-upgrade match window (±10 min, ±15% duration), fills only missing fields, and **preserves `garminId` provenance** so a later live Strava row still wins. Orchestrated by `enrichActualFromFile` in `fitImport.ts` (parse → `streamsToActivityRow` → merge → PBs + `refreshBlendedFitness`, mirroring `importActivityFile`). Load self-corrects: TSS derives from `iTrimp` on read (`computeWeekRawTSS`), so no rescale and the stored `wk.actualTSS` running total is deliberately left untouched (avoids a two-numbers divergence). Gated by new `STRAVA_ENRICH_UPLOAD_ENABLED` flag (turn off once live full Strava access enriches automatically).
- **Guided Strava-history screen**: new `src/ui/strava-history-guide.ts` — a linear, three-step overlay (request export → wait for the email → upload the .zip) that deep-links to Strava's archive page and funnels the emailed zip into the existing `importActivityArchive`. The copy tells users to use **Export Original** (not Export GPX, which strips HR). Reachable from the onboarding connect-data "Upload Strava .zip" button and from Account → Strava History → "Import history from file".
- **Onboarding copy (verified, not oversold)**: the HealthKit reader does NOT filter by source (`appleHealthSync.ts:430` `queryWorkouts` + the native Swift query carry only date/type predicates — no `HKSource` filter), so Garmin/COROS/Polar workouts genuinely flow in. But that requires the user to enable "write to Apple Health" in that watch's own app, and the data is thin. The tile copy was corrected from an initial overstatement ("all sync automatically … sleep, HRV, resting heart rate") to: Apple Watch syncs everything automatically; Garmin/COROS/Polar "route their workouts here once you enable Apple Health in their app".
- **Bulletproofing pass (review-driven)**: (1) **the critical fix** — `activity-matcher.ts:932` re-enrich loop now skips `iTrimp` overwrite when `actual.enrichedFromFile`, so the next Apple Health sync (which re-delivers the same thin `apple-` row) can no longer silently degrade the stream-computed iTRIMP back to an avg-HR estimate; (2) match guard tightened to require start within ±10 min AND duration within ±15% (was duration-alone within a 4h window) so a timezone-less GPX timestamp rejects → "enrich anyway?" confirm rather than silently matching the wrong session; (3) the force-confirm path reuses the already-parsed row (`parseActivityFileToRow` + `applyEnrichment`) instead of re-reading/re-parsing the file; (4) UI re-entrancy guard + the button's "→" affordance no longer wiped on status change.
- **Garmin → Apple Health walkthrough**: new `src/ui/garmin-apple-health-guide.ts` — a simple instructions-only overlay (3 numbered steps: open Garmin Connect → More/Settings/Apple Health → turn it on and share activities/HR/sleep; plus a COROS/Polar note). Opened from a "How do I enable this for Garmin?" link in the connect step's Apple Health card. Closes the gap where a Garmin user who never enabled the Apple Health write would silently sync nothing. Verified in-browser (renders, steps correct, close works, 0 console errors).
- **Deferred (phase 2)**: native iOS Share Sheet ("Open in Mosaic" on a .fit/.zip) — needs `@capacitor/app` + `CFBundleDocumentTypes` + a native rebuild. The existing file picker already reaches Files/iCloud, so it's convenience, not a blocker.
- **Tests**: `activity-enrich-merge.test.ts` (12 pure) + `activity-enrich.integration.test.ts` (3: real GPX→`streamsToActivityRow`→merge field alignment; `matchAndAutoComplete` re-enrich guard with a control that proves the un-guarded loop would degrade an enriched iTRIMP 9000→8445). Full build green (lint:ui + tsc + vite build); suite 3257 green. **Still not device-verified** — the only thing tests cannot cover is live HealthKit ingestion on a real iPhone (does the Garmin watch actually write the workout, what fields arrive).

## 2026-06-09 — Plan re-anchors to training actually done; debrief stops lying about "tracking to plan"

- **Problem (dogfood, Tristan)**: after weeks of not following the plan (injury + not training), the end-of-week debrief still said "tracking to plan", and the next week progressed as if every session had been done. Two root causes: (1) the debrief headline measured whether the *engine* adjusted, not whether the *athlete* kept up — a zero-session week records no `effortScore`, is skipped from the trailing average, and triggers no adjustment, so it reads as "on plan"; (2) the prescription reads VDOT/ability/phase, and VDOT is (correctly) sticky — a one-week miss docks **zero** VDOT (10-day dead-zone), so nothing reduced the plan. The number that *does* react to a missed week — CTL (−15% per idle week) — fed only readiness, never the prescription.
- **Fix — CTL-gap re-anchor (running mode, SCIENCE_LOG §BR)**: next week's prescribed volume now scales in proportion to the chronic load actually carried vs what the plan assumed. `ctlAdherenceRatio` (`fitness-model.ts`) is a one-step expected-vs-actual CTL ratio seeded from the same prior-week CTL, so it isolates last week's adherence; `plan_engine.ctlGapMultiplier` applies it as a reduce-only duration scale. The magnitude is *derived*, not invented (volume ∝ current chronic load — the ACWR ramp-rate principle); a single missed steady-state week is ~−15%, compounding and self-limiting over consecutive weeks.
- **No double-counting (the design constraint)**: the lever is one-sided/reduce-only and partitioned from the other adaptive levers — effort multiplier (intensity of sessions done), ACWR (acute spikes), and VDOT detraining (multi-week gaps, guarded by the new `Week.detrainApplied` flag set in `welcome-back.ts`). The combined effort × CTL effect is clamped to the effort band and floored at the ability deload; suppressed entirely on deload weeks. When `ctlRatio` is absent the plan output is byte-identical to before.
- **Lifecycle**: mirrors `scheduledAcwrStatus` — computed once at rollover (`events.next()`), stored on `Week.ctlRatio`, read back by the on-demand resolver (`generateWeekWorkouts` reads the stored scalar). Recursion-safe; single source `resolveCtlAdherence` (`planned-day-tss.ts`) serves both the engine and the debrief copy.
- **Copy (Tristan: factual, no judgement; headline only)**: the debrief replaces "tracking to plan" with *"{pct}% of last week's planned training completed. Next week scales to your recent load."* when materially behind (< ~80% of planned load). Illness/holiday rest is already excused (zeroed from planned load), so it never reads as a miss.
- **Tests**: `src/workouts/ctl-gap.test.ts` (15). tsc + lint:ui clean.
- **Hardening pass** (same day, adversarial multi-agent review — 6 dimensions, every finding refuted-or-confirmed by an independent skeptic; 19 confirmed, 13 refuted). Fixed: the ratio's expected side now uses the un-reduced baseline plan (was reading the already re-anchored plan via the resolver, drifting the headline %); a mode guard so the running re-anchor never computes for tri/HYROX athletes (`next()` is shared); taper-week suppression (don't shrink race prep); silent calendar-advance now stamps `detrainApplied` so a week skipped without a debrief can't feed a stale re-anchor; the debrief no longer renders "behind" and "scaled up" together. Pushed back on two findings: deload × effort compounding is intentional autoregulation (deeper deload when fatigued, Helms 2018), now locked by a regression test; the Signal-A/Signal-B cross-training seam stays a documented second-order limitation. 362 workouts+fitness-model tests green; tsc + lint:ui clean. Detail in SCIENCE_LOG §BR "Hardening".
- **Mirrored to HYROX + triathlon** (same day, per the mirror rule). HYROX: a single `mtlRatio` (`resolveMtlAdherence` in `mtl.ts`) scales `effectiveHours` in `plan_engine.hyrox` — converges because hours drive both duration and generated MTL; engine-only (HYROX has no week-debrief, so no headline yet). Triathlon: **per-discipline** `ctlRatioByDiscipline` (`resolveTriDisciplineAdherence` in `fitness-model.triathlon.ts`) scales each discipline's durations in `applyTriEffortMultipliers`, so skipping every swim re-anchors swim without cutting the bike; the tri plan-preview debrief gains a per-discipline behind-plan headline. All three modes reuse the pure `ctlAdherenceRatio`, are reduce-only, share the injury/taper/`detrainApplied` excused-week guards, and are mutually exclusive by `eventType` in `events.next()`. Tri needs no baseline temp-clear (it scales duration, not the `aerobic/anaerobic` the ratio reads). Tests: `ctl-gap-mirror.test.ts` (8). tsc + lint:ui clean; 348 workouts+tri+mtl tests green. **Not device-verified** in any mode.
- **Instant application on rollover** (tri/HYROX). Tri/HYROX store their plan and previously re-baked only on incidental triggers (version bump, benchmark refresh, injury modal, session lever) — never on the weekly rollover — so both the new re-anchor AND the pre-existing effort multiplier sat dormant until one of those fired. `events.next()` now calls `rebakeFutureWeeksInPlace` after stamping: it regenerates only the current + future weeks (no matched actuals there, so completions aren't clobbered; user-added/holiday sessions carried over) so the re-anchor and effort multiplier apply the week after a shortfall, matching running. Required wiring fix: `applyTriEffortMultipliersToFutureWeeks` now reads the per-discipline stamp from the stored `state.wks`, not the fresh generated week. (Tristan opted in — this also activates the previously-dormant tri/HYROX effort multiplier, its intended behaviour.) Full suite green.

## 2026-06-08 — iOS bounce switched to real native physics (supersedes the JS spring on device)

- **Why (dogfood)**: the JS overscroll spring felt clunky on device, especially on a bottom-to-top fling. Root cause is structural: once the finger lifts, iOS owns the momentum deceleration and a JS scroll-velocity watcher can only guess the arrival energy back from throttled scroll events, so the bounce never matched the flick. No tuning fully fixes that.
- **Fix**: re-enabled the real WKWebView rubber-band. New `BounceViewController` (`ios/App/App/BounceViewController.swift`) subclasses `CAPBridgeViewController` and, in `capacitorDidLoad()` (fires right after the web view is created), sets `scrollView.bounces = true` + `alwaysBounceVertical = true` — undoing Capacitor's hardcoded `bounces = false`. The scrollView background is set to `--c-bg` (#FAF9F6) so the few px revealed above the page during a top bounce match the off-white page edge; `position:fixed` (tab bar) stays pinned. Wired into the build: storyboard `customClass` → `BounceViewController`, plus four `App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` registrations (build file, file ref, group child, sources phase). Compile-verified: `xcodebuild ... BUILD SUCCEEDED`.
- **JS spring is now web-only again**: `installWebOverscrollBounce` restores its `isNative()` early-return — important because it sets `overscroll-behavior: none`, which would *suppress* the native bounce. The fling-arrival watcher added 2026-06-05 stays in the file for the web path.
- Status-bar bleed fix (`.mosaic-page` / `.safe-top-bleed`) from 2026-06-05 is unchanged and still correct under native bounce. Comments in `capacitor.config.ts` and `styles.css` updated (they briefly claimed there is no native bounce; there is now). FEATURES.md section retitled "Top Overscroll Bounce (native on iOS, JS spring on web)".

## 2026-06-05 — Random-logout fix: refresh failures no longer destroy real sessions (ISSUE-283)

- **ISSUE-283 fix in code**: a token-refresh failure (often just a network blip on iOS resume) used to trigger `signOut()` + `signInAnonymously()` in both `getValidSession()` (`supabaseClient.ts`) and the boot path (`main.ts`) — silently converting a real account into an anonymous guest, after which the SIGNED_IN owner-mismatch check wiped local state and the guest-upgrade auth view showed the misleading "leave your guest training data behind" warning. Now: network-shaped failures (`isAuthRetryableFetchError`) keep the session and let the SDK retry; a genuinely invalid token on a real account signs out locally to the sign-in screen; the anonymous fallback only fires for anonymous sessions.
- **Auth view remembers the email**: last successful sign-in/sign-up email stored in `localStorage` (`mosaic_last_email`) and prefilled; the view defaults to Sign in when a remembered email exists; typed email survives toggle/error re-renders (`auth-view.ts`).
- **"Already registered" auto-switches to sign-in** (Tristan dogfood, same day): sign-up / save-account with an email that already has an account (`email_exists` / message match) no longer dead-ends on the raw Supabase error — the form flips to Sign in, keeps the email, focuses the password field, and shows "This email already has an account. Enter your password to sign in." In guest-upgrade mode the amber "choose Sign up instead" warning is suppressed for that case (its advice is wrong there) and the notice carries the guest-data caveat instead.

## 2026-06-05 — Tab entrances: opacity-only + once per session (TestFlight perf)

- **Why (dogfood, on device)**: Forecast cards "appear really slowly and kind of jump up and out", tab switching feels slow, background "moves quite slowly", Home feels clunky. Two documented perf cliffs at once: glass cards (`backdrop-filter:blur(16px)`) animated `translateY+scale` entrances (moving glass re-samples its backdrop every frame on WKWebView), over a ring background that was itself playing an entrance + a 6.5s drift — and the whole stack replayed on **every** tab switch because each switch fully re-renders.
- **Fix 1 — opacity-only entrances (33 files)**: every `*FloatUp`-style entrance keyframe is now `from {opacity:0} to {opacity:1}` — no transform on anything that can carry glass. Wizard/auth/modal "Rise" overlays intentionally kept (over static scrims, not in the complaint).
- **Fix 2 — first-visit-per-session gate**: new `shouldPlayEntrance(key)` in `page-flair.ts`. All tab-level views (Home incl. just-track, Plan ×3 modes + just-track, Forecast ×3 + no-race std variant, Stats ×3) animate on first visit only; revisits render settled and pass `entrance:'none', pulse:false` to `buildRingBackground` (no ring entrance, no drift, static background behind glass). Forecast also skips the 1.2s chart draw-on and fingerprint chip stagger on revisits; Home skips barGrow/arcSweep (arc jumps to end state via a 0s animation).
- **Fix 3 — first-visit timing (dogfood round 2)**: the fingerprint chips (You/Capacity/Adaptation…) staggered in over 0.20–0.62s delays + 0.45s fades, reading as "data lagging in" rather than an entrance. Chip ladder compressed to 0.04–0.18s at 0.3s duration; Forecast card fade 0.6s → 0.4s. (Round-2 report came from the OLD build — the phone never had fixes 1–2 — but the chip ladder was real and is now tight.)
- **Verified headless (Chromium, demo seed)**: first visit animates (fade + ring entrance + drift), revisit fully settled on Home/Plan/Forecast/Stats; first-visit Forecast entrance samples at ~60fps (avg 16.8ms, 1 frame >32ms). Behaviour choices (opacity-only, first-visit-only) confirmed by Tristan. **Production-bundle first Forecast tap: 141ms to DOM, 272ms to paint** (the ~1s on `npx vite` dev is per-module dev serving, not shipped behaviour; the 2000-trial Monte Carlo is 32ms, cone card 55ms, fingerprint 2ms). NOT device-verified yet — needs a TestFlight rebuild.
- Docs: two new rules in `UX_PATTERNS.md → Rendering performance`.

## 2026-06-05 — Sleep/physiology now refresh on iOS foreground resume

- **Why (dogfood)**: new build on device showed stale sleep/physiology while the DB had today's rows (webhook healthy, `sync-physiology-snapshot` 200s). Root cause: the full physiology sync (`syncPhysiologySnapshot(90)`) only runs at cold launch. On web every page load is a cold launch; on iOS the WKWebView stays alive for days, and the foreground-resume handler's Garmin branch only synced **steps** (the Apple branch already re-synced full physiology). The 3-min sleep poller also died when iOS suspended timers and could never restart (`started` flag).
- **Fix (3 files)**: (1) `main.ts` visibilitychange Garmin branch now mirrors Apple — `syncPhysiologySnapshot(7)` + normalizer refresh + conditional `refreshRecentSleepScores` when today's sleep is missing + sleep-poller restart, still throttled to once per 5 min. (2) `sleepPoller.ts` is restartable: guard is "poll already running", not "ever started". (3) `physiologySync.ts` history write is now a per-date, per-field **merge** instead of wholesale replace — a 7-day call can no longer truncate the 28-day recovery baseline (latent bug: the poller and the manual sleep-sync button did exactly that), and Apple gap-fill values survive where Garmin has no data. Stale "OVERWRITES wholesale" ordering comment in `main.ts` corrected.
- 4 new tests (`physiologySync.test.ts` — merge semantics), suite 3227 green, tsc clean. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-05 — Top overscroll bounce now runs on iOS too (+ fling bounce, + status-bar seam fix)

- **Why (dogfood)**: the elastic top bounce worked on web but not on device. Root cause: `web-overscroll-bounce.ts` no-op'd on native (`isNative()` early return) on the assumption WKWebView rubber-bands the document natively — but Capacitor **hardcodes** `webView.scrollView.bounces = false` in `CAPBridgeViewController.swift` (unconditional, no config flag), so there was never any native bounce to defer to.
- **Fix**: removed the native guard — the JS spring now runs on all platforms. Chosen over re-enabling native bounce via a Swift subclass because the JS spring pins the fixed tab bar and the atmosphere gradient during the pull (native bounce drags the whole viewport, Safari-style) and keeps web/iOS feel identical with no native code to maintain.
- **Fling bounce (dogfood round 2)**: a flicked momentum scroll hit the top and stopped dead — during a native glide the finger is up, so no touch events fire and the drag path never sees it. New scroll-velocity watcher: when a glide crosses into the top above `FLING_MIN_VELOCITY` (0.3 px/ms) with no finger down, the arrival velocity feeds the existing per-frame decay loop as a spring impulse (`flingV`, out phase ~100ms at `FLING_DECAY` 0.72/frame) — out fast, ease back. Slow controlled arrivals still stop cleanly, matching UIScrollView.
- **Status-bar seam (dogfood round 2)**: every page showed a cream strip behind the status bar — body carries `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)`, so page wrappers (which carry the atmosphere gradient) started below the notch and the strip showed bare `--c-bg`. Fix: `.mosaic-page` plus new `.safe-top-bleed` get `margin-top: -env(safe-area-inset-top)` + matching `padding-top` — gradient paints up behind the status bar, content box unmoved, no-op on web. Applied `.safe-top-bleed` to all 18 inline-styled atmosphere wrappers lacking `.mosaic-page` (readiness/recovery/sleep/strain/freshness/leg-load/mtl/rolling-load/load-taper/injury-risk wrappers, forecast-chip details ×3, race-forecast ×3, tri leg detail, hyrox critical-pace).
- Stale comments corrected in `capacitor.config.ts` (claimed `contentInset: 'never'` "restores natural rubber-band bounce" — it never did) and `styles.css` (html background is now a backstop, not a native-bounce companion). New FEATURES.md entry "Top Overscroll Spring".
- tsc + lint:ui clean, suite 3228 green. NOT device-verified.

Bike rung changes scale every "lo–hiW" range by the ladder %FTP ratio (`scaleWattRanges`); swim rung changes set every "/100m" token to CSS + rung offset (`setSwimPaceTokens`), so the card always agrees with the modal's live Target line. - **Follow-up (same session, dogfood round 2)**: (1) the "Original:" caption now shows the original pace too ("Original: 6km @ 6:10/km" under an MP-adjusted card) so the adjustment reads as what → what — every clean-distance original is an easy/long run, so the easy pace is re-derived live at the caption (`plan-view.ts`). ## 2026-06-04 — Max HR: one corroborated-max estimator for all three sync pipes (SCIENCE_LOG §BQ)

- **Why**: dogfood question on the "Ignored lower maxHR=184 (current=201)" warning. The three pipes used three different statistics feeding one up-only ratchet — Garmin edge fn p95 (median below 5 readings: the path that once wrote 144), Strava p95, Apple Health raw `Math.max` (a single wrist cadence-lock spike could ratchet in forever). Live data check: 201 is real (witnessed by 202/203 on other days); a lone 216 is the spike; 184 was just p95-of-session-maxes, which sits below true max by construction — the warning fired on every sync.
- **Fix**: canonical `corroboratedMaxHR()` (`src/calculations/max-hr-estimator.ts`) — highest session max witnessed by a second session within 5 bpm on a *different* day (cross-source duplicate twins can't witness each other), gates ≥150 / <230 bpm. Shared `applyCorroboratedMaxHR` keeps the up-only ratchet; lower estimates log at info, not warn. All three writers switched (`physiologySync.ts`, `stravaSync.ts`, `appleHealthSync.ts`); `sync-physiology-snapshot` now returns the top 40 readings with dates (legacy p95 aggregate kept for old clients; new client falls back to it when readings are absent).
- Downward revision (age-related ~0.7 bpm/yr decline) deliberately deferred — logged as a limitation in §BQ.
- 12 new tests, suite 3185 green, tsc clean. **Edge fn change STAGED, NOT deployed** (deploy permission denied mid-session). NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-04 — ISSUE-270 protections built: save-account onboarding moment + Strava fork guard / history claim

- **Why**: anonymous-by-default auth (`main.ts:213`) forks a user's data on reinstall / device change / storage eviction; verified the onboarding never asks for an email (welcome asks the first NAME; the auth screen only appears on explicit sign-out). One Strava athlete in the dev DB has tokens under 20 user_ids. `garmin_id` is globally UNIQUE, so a forked account cannot even re-sync history the old account owns.
- **Save-account overlay** (`src/ui/wizard/save-account-overlay.ts`): shown ONCE per onboarding at the moment a data source connects (Strava/Garmin OAuth return on connect-data, plus the Continue tap for Apple Health / file-upload users). In-place anonymous upgrade via `supabase.auth.updateUser` (same user_id, data preserved — the auth-view mechanism). Skippable ("Later"); Home guest banner + Account remain the fallbacks. New optional `onboarding.accountSaveOffered` flag. No-data skippers are not prompted.
- **Fork guard** (`strava-auth-callback`): after the token upsert, counts activities held by other non-deleted accounts with the same `strava_athlete_id` and appends `existing=N` to the redirect. Failures degrade to "no hint" — never breaks OAuth.
- **History claim** (new edge function `strava-claim-history` + `src/data/strava-claim.ts`): JWT-verified; ownership proof = the caller's own strava_tokens row (only exists via completed OAuth). Moves `garmin_activities.user_id` from all prior same-athlete accounts to the caller (collision-free: garmin_id unchanged) and retires the old token rows (`deleted_at`) so the refresh cron stops resurrecting forks. `?status=1` for a read-only count.
- **Client wiring** (`main.ts` ?strava=connected): mid-wizard → claim silently, then sync (onboarding benchmarks see full history — also the fix path for the dev account's own fragmentation); main view → confirm overlay (`src/ui/history-claim-overlay.ts`) before merging into an established plan.
- tsc clean, 3173 tests green, lint:ui clean. **Edge functions DEPLOYED 2026-06-04** (Tristan-approved): strava-claim-history v1 (verify_jwt true, unauthed smoke test → 401), strava-auth-callback v29 (verify_jwt false, OAuth flow intact). NOT device-verified — next Strava reconnect exercises the full path.
- **Hardening round 2 (same day, "fix these for users")**: (1) reconnect OAuth upsert clears `deleted_at` — a claimed-from or deletion-cancelled account resurrects on legitimate reconnect; (2) `sync-strava-activities` token select filters soft-deleted rows — a retired fork can no longer sync new activities under the abandoned user_id (two-device re-fork loop closed); (3) daily claim-on-launch convergence check (`maybeOfferClaimOnLaunch` in `strava-claim.ts`, 24h device-local throttle, main view + Strava connected only) — catches forks that form while a device is idle; (4) the mid-wizard silent claim now shows an "Imported N activities from your training history" toast; (5) save-account overlay maps Supabase errors to actionable copy ("email already registered" → use Sign in from welcome) and the success card honestly states recovery requires clicking the confirmation link. Both functions redeployed. **Sign in with Apple assessed and parked as ISSUE-271**: NOT an App Store 4.8 requirement (primary auth is first-party email/password; Strava/Garmin are data connections, not login); the native `signInWithIdToken` path would orphan anonymous data — use `linkIdentity` web flow + dashboard/Apple-portal config when built.

## 2026-06-04 — Onboarding loading screen: always-on motion + live narration

- **Why**: clean-slate rebuild dogfood — the "Reading your training" card sat visually frozen for the entire history import. The fill ring only advances on step *transitions*, and the import is one long await, so for ~90% of the wall time the only motion was a 2.6s opacity breathe (imperceptible). Copy also carried an em dash.
- **Always-on sweep**: a thin teal arc (16% of circumference, existing palette, no new colour) orbits the progress ring continuously via pure SVG transform rotation (GPU-composited, no filter-over-motion). The fill ring still shows step progress on top.
- **Live narration**: each step now shows a one-sentence explainer of the work in progress (`LOADING_STEP_DETAIL`), replaced in-place by real facts as phases complete via `setLoadingDetail` — "187 runs imported across 38 weeks of training.", "Found resting HR 48, max HR 188, VO2max 56.", "3 personal bests found in your race history." Facts reset at each step change so the new phase's explainer leads.
- Timeout copy rewritten without the em dash ("Still syncing. Large training histories take longer to import...").
- **Round 2 ("make it as good as we can")**: (a) **ring creep** — the fill previously credited a step the moment it started, then froze; it now starts at the step boundary and advances asymptotically within the step (`1 − e^(−t/25s)`, capped at 92% of the span) so the boundary is only crossed when the phase genuinely completes; (b) **heartbeat fact-watcher** (`startLoadingHeartbeat`, 1.5s) — reads state every tick and surfaces genuine data the moment ANY async path lands it (runs imported, weekly km, RHR/maxHR/VO2max), one fact per tick, deduped; self-terminates when the card unmounts; (c) **90s escalation** on the long-wait ladder ("Nothing is stuck, large histories simply take a while..."); (d) dev-only console preview `__previewOnboardingLoading()` (and `{slow:true}` for the long-import feel) cycles the whole screen without onboarding — DEV-guarded out of prod.
- Known limitation (deliberate): no per-activity progress during the import itself — it is a single server-side edge call; pagination/progress reporting would be a server change, held until we know first-import slowness is representative rather than a dev-environment artefact.
- tsc + lint:ui + UI tests green. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-04 — Watch LT is trusted until superseded (ISSUE-268)

- **Why**: Tristan's watch holds a measured LT (4:12/km, 168 bpm) but the app showed the VDOT-derived 3:59/km · 177 bpm "low confidence" — threshold prescriptions ~13s/km too fast. Two compounding policies buried watch readings: a 60-day Garmin expiry (but Garmin pushes userMetrics only on CHANGE, so silence means "unchanged", not stale) and a >10s/km conflict-suggestion card that parked the watch value until the user noticed it.
- **Retention** (`lt-derivation.ts resolveLT`): expiry removed. A Garmin reading holds until a newer reading, a manual override, or a derived estimate that clearly beats it (faster ≥3s/km at medium+ confidence, `LT_GARMIN_SUPERSEDE_GAP_SEC_KM` — same gap as the override auto-improve rule). Slower derived never displaces measured.
- **Auto-apply** (`ltSync.ts recomputeLT`): the Garmin-vs-derived suggestion flow is retired; watch readings apply directly, stale pending suggestions are cleared. Shifts ≥10s/km (`LT_NOTIFY_THRESHOLD_SEC_KM`) surface a toast (physiologySync → showAssignmentToast, unit-pref formatted).
- **Webhook hardening** (`garmin-webhook handleUserMetrics`): merge-preserving upsert — a VO2-only push no longer nulls a same-day LT reading (LT events are rare; losing one could mean never seeing another). NOT yet deployed.
- **Deliberately dropped** (Tristan): deep historical userMetrics backfill — the existing 8-week connect-time backfill is enough for future users; LT predating it arrives on their next hard run.
- SCIENCE_LOG "Lactate Threshold Derivation" revised (rationale + detraining limitation). 8 new tests (ltSync.test.ts new, lt-derivation.test.ts stale-expiry test inverted). Suite 3141 green. NOT device-verified; Tristan's own LT still needs the manual override (his change event predates the webhook).

## 2026-06-03 — Playwright dogfood of the plyo/gym batch: 4 bugs found and fixed

Drove a fresh intermediate marathon-plan profile through the new features on an isolated dev server (port 5199). **Verified working end-to-end**: running-mode discipline picker (Run/Gym/Bike/Swim, no HYROX focus), Plyometrics focus + 12–60 slider, Power + Strength past 30 min, intensity tiers, the scheduled build-week contrast power-block, the Account "Plyometrics in gym" toggle (off→on applies immediately — render-time generation), first-time weight guidance, bike cross-train + inline FTP capture (watt targets appear on the same preview), and the suggested-session swaps. Fixed during the run:

- **Plyo rotation defeated the tier ordering** (`running-pool.ts`): the week rotation rotated the whole tier pool, so a base-phase short session could lead with Depth Jump and lose Pogo Hops entirely — which also inflated sets past time-feasibility (the contact-scaler had only low-rep/high-rest moves left to spend contacts on). Rotation now happens WITHIN the low/high groups so variety can never break the tier guarantee. Regression test added (the original tests only used slotIndex 0).
- **Power-pair cue was swallowed by the rest-note classifier** (`running-pool.ts`): `parseStrengthSession` treats the first parenthetical matching /rest/i as the rest note; the pairing cue said "then rest 2 to 3 min", so the squat displayed "3 min rest · 3 min rest" and lost its cue. Reworded to "then take 2 to 3 min"; regression test pins cue + restSec.
- **Slider thumb/state mismatch** (`session-generator.ts`): default 45 min isn't on plyo's 12+2k step grid — the browser displayed 46 while state held 45. Minutes now snap to the step grid on render.
- **Swap card claimed "Recovery is low" on a good day** (`session-generator.ts`): the why-line was written for the old auto-divert design; now that swaps are reachable any day it's recovery-agnostic ("A strength session keeps training productive without the impact of a run.").

**Logged, not fixed**: ISSUE-257 (onboarding gym choice produced `s.gs = 0` — investigate repro without the dev-fill), ISSUE-258 (plan-ready screen shows two different VO2 numbers). Also noted: the ⚡ dev-fill seeds a past London Marathon (race-done banner noise on dev profiles); bike target card says "HR-based" beside watt targets (power-meter copy nit). Full suite 3036 pass, tsc + lint clean.

**Follow-ups same day**: ISSUE-257 downgraded to P3 watch (Tristan's manual onboarding with gym=2 came through fine — likely a dev-fill/automation artifact). ISSUE-258 fixed: the duplicate was `s.initialVO2` (physiological) rendered under `s.v` (VDOT labelled "Starting VO2max"); the `ml/kg/min` row is dropped from `plan-preview-v2.ts` per Tristan ("we shouldn't have 2") — the physiological VO2max stays on Stats. Tristan device-verified: swim CSS capture and Suggested → "Swap for easy gym" → Accept. Suite 3057 pass.

## 2026-06-03 — Suggestion modal UX polish round 3: type scale, real glass, day labels

- **Why**: Device screenshot review (Tristan): "lots of font sizes, not glassy. We should say what day the exercises are that are going to be replaced."
- **Type scale collapsed** (`suggestion-modal.ts`): the modal mixed 11/12/13/14/15px almost arbitrarily. Now three sizes: 15/600 headings (alert title, option titles, Confirm), 13 body, 12 secondary, with 11 reserved for the Recommended chip. "See details" and the ACWR detail rows moved 11→12; alert title 14→15.
- **Actually glassy**: outer card was near-opaque white 0.96 — dropped to `rgba(255,255,255,0.78)` + `blur(24px) saturate(1.4)` (the m-btn-glass saturate) so the dimmed backdrop reads through. Inner surfaces (option cards, ctx card, no-trim note, edge-case panels) became frosted layers: white 0.66 + the `m-btn-glass--inset` two-layer shadow, deliberately **without** per-card backdrop-filter (stacked glass is the documented perf cliff in UX_PATTERNS → Rendering performance).
- **Adjustment rows redesigned with day labels**: each "View changes" row now reads "Tue · Easy Run" (from `Adjustment.dayIndex`, Monday-first `DAY_SHORT`), action right-aligned, and the detail ("Keep 6.1 km, drop to steady pace") as a full-width second line — kills the old right-aligned 3-line wrap. Dropped the redundant workout-type echo ("Threshold Tempo *threshold*") and the "(MP–easy midpoint)" jargon. The box-in-box panel around the list is gone; rows separate with hairlines (last row borderless), and the "View changes" summary gained a rotating ▸ caret matching "See details".
- **Per-option absorption line** (round 4, same day): Tristan spotted that Replace & Reduce and Reduce both listed the identical Tue Tempo downgrade with nothing distinguishing them. That's correct suggester behaviour (both outcomes draw on the same `effectiveRRC` budget; the downgrade is the same best cut — Reduce just runs out of legal moves at the floors), but the modal never showed the difference in total load shed. Each option now carries "Absorbs ≈ X of the Y excess." in the header's easy-km currency — pure proportion of `Σ loadReduction / runReplacementCredit` × the header `equivalentEasyKm`, clamped to the header value, zero new constants. Keep plan shows "Absorbs none of the excess." when other options have absorption lines.
- **Honest denominator + remainder note** (round 6, "what do we do if we can't take it all?"): the round-4 line used the session's full easy-km equivalent as the denominator, which overstated the gap when the suggester had capped the budget to the week's overshoot (only the overshoot needs cutting; the rest fits in planned headroom). The suggester now exposes `effectiveReductionBudget` (post-cap `effectiveRRC`, new optional `SuggestionPayload` field) and the modal converts it to "the ≈ X km that needs cutting" as the denominator; ≥95% coverage reads "Absorbs the full ≈ X km that needs cutting." When even the best option leaves >10% of the need unabsorbed, a footnote under the options states the mechanics: the plan can't cut below run minimums; unabsorbed load stays in fatigue tracking (ATL/ACWR) and carries into next week via `wk.carriedTSS` if the week ends over target (week-rollover, `events.ts:1119`). Keep plan reads "Absorbs nothing. The full load stays as fatigue."
- **Direction-explicit copy + excess explainer** (round 8, "where do these extra kms go?"): "Absorbs" was abstract about direction, so the option lines now name the source: "Cuts ≈ 4.7 km from this week's remaining runs, of the ≈ 15.7 km needed." / "Cuts the full ≈ X needed from this week's remaining runs." Keep plan: "Cuts nothing. The excess stays as fatigue." The "≈ X km easy running equivalent" label is now tappable (dotted underline, mirrors the leg-impact explainer) and toggles the mental model in plain terms: the excess is training stress already done, not upcoming distance; reducing trades planned sessions for it; keeping the plan carries it as fatigue (lower readiness, and an over-target week starts the next one with a smaller budget). Remainder footnote reworded to match ("What isn't cut stays as fatigue…"). Both header variants (ACWR + matched-activity) share the same `equivBtn`/`equivExplainer`.
- **Header owns the ask; unreachable number demoted; Reduce hides when not equivalent** (round 9, "it still looks like we need to cut 15.7 km and we can't"): the per-card "of the ≈ 15.7 km needed" framing read as the app failing its own target. Now the header sentence states the achievable ask in Tristan's framing: "You've been training harder than normal. This week is 140% above your usual load, so the remaining runs come down by ≈ 4.7 km." (`askKm` = the recommended option's actual cut). Cards state only what they deliver ("Cuts ≈ 4.7 km from the remaining runs."). The full 15.7 km excess + where the remainder goes moved into See details (`excessDetail`), and the grey remainder footnote under the options was deleted. **Reduce now hides when it can't reach ≈ the same total as Replace & Reduce** (≥90% gate) — per the option's original intent: spread an equivalent cut across runs; if the run minimums stop it being equivalent, it isn't a real alternative. Reduce desc rewritten ("Trims intensity or distance across your runs. Keeps every run in the plan."), Keep plan's duplicate heavy-severity fatigue note dropped when the cut line already says it (extreme warning kept).
- **"Equivalent of easy running" wording + load-scale discovery** (round 10, 2026-06-04, "it's not just distance, we're replacing intensity — does TSS make sense?"): no missing factor — downgrades cut intensity at constant km, reduces cut km at constant intensity, replaces cut the whole session, and all three land in one load currency (duration × per-minute intensity rate). The display flattening was the lie: "comes down by ≈ 4.7 km" implied literal distance when roughly half the cut is an intensity drop. Header and cards now read "…come down by the equivalent of ≈ 4.7 km of easy running." / "Cuts the equivalent of ≈ 4.7 km of easy running." **TSS display investigated and blocked**: the suggester budgets cuts (Garmin-scale `LOAD_PER_MIN_BY_INTENSITY`, load.ts:94 "match GARMIN scale") against a credit from the universalLoad pipeline (iTRIMP tier: "TSS-equivalent"), while the weekly-target math uses the TSS-calibrated `TL_PER_MIN` — three scales with conflicting in-code conversion comments, and `remainingLoad -= actualReduction` crosses them, plausibly under-cutting. Logged as **ISSUE-263** (P2); TSS becomes the natural display unit (and the cross-mode one — Strain ring, Signal B, carriedTSS) once the scales are reconciled.
- **Load-currency session handover written** (`docs/LOAD_CURRENCY_PLAN.md`, 2026-06-04): Tristan approved a dedicated reconciliation session. The doc carries the verified scale inventory (4 scales with file:line evidence), the live bugs (B1 budget loop, B2 similarity ranking, B3 display divergence), an ordered 8-step plan (audit → canonicalise on TSS → ISSUE-262 profile check → boundary conversion → display sweep → anchor tests → real-data calibration + CTL/ATL freeze-check → SCIENCE_LOG), the in-session decision list, and risks. ISSUE-259 (power-TSS) explicitly out of scope.
- tsc clean, modal file lint-clean, full suite 3093 pass. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Hard unplanned sessions now drive readiness score + sentence (tri post-session override restored)

- **Why**: Dogfood report — 60 min hard bike while injured (run/swim blocked, bike capped 40%) left the Readiness card unchanged: score 50 "Manage Load" with the chronic-load sentence ("Bike load is elevated relative to your baseline…"), while the Strain ring showed the 43 TSS session. Two causes. (1) The tri-mode post-session sentence override ("Trained hard today.") existed in the 2026-05-19 snapshot (`7e9c5ca`) but the home-view wiring was lost in the May crash — `isPostSessionState` survived in `daily-coach.ts` as dead code (zero call sites). Same phantom-loss pattern as the suggestion-modal. (2) The readiness strain floor reads `strainPct = todayTSS / plannedDayTSS`, and with no planned session today (injury-reduced plan; tri mode's planned-day TSS comes from the running generator anyway) the percent stayed 0 — the floor never fired. Injury mode was *not* the cause: it only gates the leg-load floor.
- **Fix (score)**: new adhoc strain anchor in `home-view.ts` — when `plannedDayTSS = 0` and the athlete trained today, `strainPct = todayTSS / (weeklyCTL / 7) × 100` (Banister sustainable daily load; same anchor the trackOnly Strain ring uses; weekly CTL ≥ 10 noise guard mirrors `perDisciplineACWR`). `strainPctEffective` feeds `computeReadiness`, so the existing strain floor (50–100% → 100→54, 100%+ → 54→10) now engages. SCIENCE_LOG §BJ.
- **Fix (sentence)**: tri-mode override restored, upgraded from the snapshot's bare "Trained hard today." to running mode's copy via a new shared `postSessionSentence(actualTSS, pct)` in `daily-coach.ts` ("Solid session today (43 TSS). Rest up and recover." at 100–129%, "Big session…" at 130%+). Running's `derivePrimaryMessage` Tier 1 now calls the same helper (single copy source, mirror rule); dead `isPostSessionState` removed.
- 4 new tests (`daily-coach.test.ts`), full suite 3018 pass, tsc + lint:ui clean. NOT device-verified.
- **Follow-up (same day, after live-state numbers from Tristan)**: ride = 56 min indoor VO2, iTRIMP 5202 → 43 TSS; weekly CTL swim 0 / bike 120.5 / run 81.1 / **cross 143.1**. Two corrections: (1) the anchor now **includes `crossTrainingCtl`** — the numerator counts all sports, and with cross excluded every routine ~48-TSS HIIT day would have read ~167% and pinned readiness at ~17 (cross was his largest CTL component). With cross included the ride reads 43 / 49.2 = 87% of typical daily load. (2) **New 80% acknowledgment tier** (Tristan: "if strain is high from 80% up, we say good training"): on CTL-anchored days `postSessionSentence` returns "Good training today (43 TSS), most of a typical day's load." at 80–99%; gated to `ctlAnchored` so running's planned-target "Nearly at today's target" mid-session copy is untouched. The 87% case now gets acknowledged; score correctly stays put (sub-average measured day). The "felt hard but scored 43" gap is the HR-lag-on-intervals undercount → logged **ISSUE-259** (power-based Coggan TSS for rides with power data; whole-pipe change, coordinates with the day-TSS bug another agent is fixing). 3 more tests.
- **Follow-up 2 (capacity anchor + rehab-cap call-out, Tristan's pick)**: once the parallel planned-day-TSS fix landed (real tri plan via `getPlannedDayTSSContext`, injury-capped day = 20 TSS), pure %-of-plan would have read 42/20 = 210% and floored readiness to ~10 on a physiologically average day. Per the standing ring=capacity ruling: floor now anchors on **`max(plannedDayTSS, weeklyCTL/7)`** (42/45 = 93% → floor ≈ 61 — the score the user saw). The rehab-cap message moved to the sentence layer: new `injuryCapOvershootSentence` (injury active + actual > planned × 1.3) — "42 TSS logged against an injury-capped day of 20. Load is within your normal range, but well above the rehab cap." — wired in tri home-view and mirrored into running's Tier-0 injury branch in `derivePrimaryMessage`. Deliberate side effect: running easy days smaller than CTL/7 no longer pin the floor at 54 on completion. 3 more tests (35 in daily-coach), full suite 3093 green. TEMP `[readiness-debug]` console.log still in home-view pending device verification.
- **Follow-up 3 (canonical module — Home 61 vs detail 10 incident)**: tapping into the Readiness detail page showed **10 "Ease Back"** under a Home ring of 61 — `readiness-view.ts` had its own plan-anchored strain (210%) while Home used the capacity anchor (93%). Root cause is structural: every surface hand-assembled its own `computeReadiness` strain input, so "identical" surfaces only agreed by luck. New **`src/calculations/capacity-strain.ts`**: `computeCapacityStrain(s)` (canonical anchor, guards, injury-overshoot flag) + `capacityStrainNote(cs)` (canonical sentence: overshoot call-out > Big/Solid/Good tiers); `postSessionSentence`/`injuryCapOvershootSentence` moved there (re-exported via daily-coach). All three strainPct producers now consume it: home-view, readiness-view (score input + lead sentence + Today's-Strain card descriptor when injury-capped), daily-coach `deriveStrainContext` (new `StrainContext.capacityStrainPct`; plan-relative `strainPct` stays for copy tiers). Audit also found `coach-workout-modal.ts` and `session-recommendation.ts` building their own readiness with no strain/recovery inputs → logged **ISSUE-260** (full canonical input builder). 4 new tests (`capacity-strain.test.ts`), suite 3098 green, tsc + lint:ui clean. Session handoff brief written to `docs/READINESS_AUDIT.md` (incident timeline, shipped state, ISSUE-259/260 execution plans, decisions log).
