## 2026-06-03 — Tri workout IDs, always-available review, ride auto-matching

Root-cause batch for the dogfood reports "these should merge", "the review button is gone", "I dragged it and got 2 of them", "why can't I log the ride".

- **Tri plan engine now stamps stable workout IDs** (`plan_engine.triathlon.ts:stampTriWorkoutIds`, `W{week}-{type}-{idx}`, mirroring the running generator's id loop). Tri workouts had NO ids, so every consumer keyed on `w.id ?? w.n` — and a week routinely carries duplicate names (two "Endurance ride" bikes, two same-region injury-adapted gym sessions). Consequences fixed: dragging one card moved its same-named sibling ("I got 2 of them"), one day's rating/HR bled onto the other same-named day, a synced recording couldn't bind to its own slot, and an already-rated name hid its sibling from the matching screen. Covers tri + cycling mode (same engine); HYROX (`scheduleHyroxWeek`) still unstamped — follow-up under the mirror rule. **Migration note**: existing name-keyed `rated`/`garminActuals` entries orphan when the ids appear; current-week sessions may flip to not-done and need re-placing via Review.
- **Review is always available** (`activity-review.ts:openActivityReReview`): re-review used to bail when `garminPending` was empty — and a sync consumes pending once everything is placed, killing the Review button exactly when the user wants to change a placement. Re-review now reconstitutes reviewable records from the week's synced `garminActuals` (standalone `garmin-<gid>` cards + slot-bound matches; guided-stub actuals excluded). Home "Review →" button + its week-pick handler updated to match (`home-view.ts`).
- **Synced rides/swims are auto-proposed onto planned bike/swim sessions** (`activity-review.ts:proposeMatchings`): the cross-training step only ever tried named matches and generic `cross` slots, so in tri mode a ride always fell into Excess Load even with a same-day planned "Endurance ride". Now picks the closest-day `bike_*`/`swim_*` slot (same-day = medium confidence); the user can still reassign on the matching screen.
- **Logged ride no longer wears a RUN badge** (`triathlon/workout-card.ts:badgeKindFor`): adhoc synced cross-training has no `discipline`, and the fallback was 'run'. Now classifies bike/swim from the activity-type name ("Indoor Cycling" → BIKE).
- **Follow-up round (same evening, from a live state dump)**: (1) `TRI_GENERATOR_VERSION` bumped 17 → 18 — the id stamping only applies at generation, so persisted weeks kept id-less workouts until a version-bump regen; the bump forces it on next launch. (2) `openActivityReReview` now runs `reconcileCrossSourceDuplicates` BEFORE reconstitution — a mid-session sync can land both pipe-twins of the same ride (different garminIds), and the reconstitution was rebuilding both, auto-assigning the same "Indoor Cycling" to the Wed AND Thu ride slots. (3) New reconcile pass prunes **excess-ledger twins**: an `unspentLoadItems` entry with a raw Garmin-webhook id whose session also exists as a Strava record (same day, duration within 15%) was the same session double-counted into excess load, inflating load warnings.
- **Sync limbo fix — the actual "lost Monday HIIT" mechanism** (`activity-matcher.ts:matchAndAutoComplete`): `globalProcessed` treated EVERY `garminMatched` key as already-processed, including `'__pending__'` markers whose pending record had been destroyed by an undo/re-review cycle. Such a session had no local data anywhere, was invisible in Recent and Review, and every future sync skipped its row — permanent loss until the marker was deleted. A `'__pending__'` marker without a surviving pending record no longer counts as processed, so the next sync rebuilds the record (28-day lookback).
- **Done-but-recordingless slots now show on the matching screen** (`activity-review.ts` slot filter + `matching-screen.ts` "· done" tag): a guided/manual completion with no synced recording attached (absent or `guided-` stub actual) is exactly the slot a late recording should merge into; hiding it made the week look incomplete and stranded the recording. Slots already carrying a synced recording stay hidden.
- **Version-bump regen no longer wipes user-added sessions** (`main.ts`, tri + HYROX regen blocks): replacing `wks[i].triWorkouts` wholesale deleted sessions the user added via the session generator / suggestions / holiday bridge (`adhoc-`/`holiday-` ids live in the same array). Real incident: the v18 regen deleted an added Tuesday gym session. User-added entries are now carried over; only generator-owned slots are replaced.
- **Same-day recordings now win their slot** (`activity-review.ts:proposeMatchings` step 2): gym matching ran as a single greedy pass in pending-array order, so whichever recording the sync listed first could take another day's slot via an adjacent-day match (a Tuesday HIIT consumed the Monday gym slot; the Monday recording overflowed). Now two passes — same-day claims first, leftovers then take adjacent-day matches — with items processed chronologically.
- **`dropActual` clears the dropped copy's rating** (`activity-matcher.ts:reconcileCrossSourceDuplicates`): removing a duplicate's actual/match left `rated[slotId]` behind — a phantom "Logged" plan card with no activity under it (one real ride, two Endurance rides both reading Logged). The surviving copy re-rates the slot when it matches.
- **Logged ISSUE-260** — Tristan's activity-identity invariants spec (all activities on all 3 surfaces, rendered on their actual day, never disappearing on tag, exactly one binding). Root causes fixed today; the remaining surface-consistency work (actual-day rendering in tri/HYROX plan-views, one canonical week-activity join, single-binding invariant) is scoped there for a fresh session.
- Tests: full suite **3051 pass**. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `lint:ui` flags are in `wizard/steps/review.ts` only (untouched by this work — another session's in-flight change). NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Bodyweight progression for beginners/novices (remember + advance)

- **Why**: Weaker athletes got easier sessions but were never coached forward. Progression is weight-based, so their bodyweight work didn't advance — the same static template repeated every week, and the RIR feedback the guided player collects was discarded for bodyweight moves (only weighted lifts persist). Beginners stayed put.
- **What**: A bodyweight progression ladder, the analog of the weight autoregulation. New `src/calculations/bodyweight-progression.ts` defines a per-movement-family ladder (squat / lunge / hinge / calf / plank / step-up), each rung a prescription built from movements + loads that already exist in the beginner/novice templates, sequenced: more reps → harder variant → light load. The app now **remembers a rung per family** (`s.bodyweightProgress`) and advances it from the same RIR tap.
- **Policy** (Tristan): advance one rung after **2 consecutive "reps-left" (easy)** sessions; **"barely" (too hard) steps DOWN one rung** then climbs back up via the normal rule; "about right" holds; base/build phases only (mirrors the weight bump's phase gate). The top rungs introduce a light load, after which weight-tracking takes over.
- **Flow**: capture in `completeStrengthSession` (`persistBodyweightProgress` after `persistStrengthLifts`); read-back in `generateGymWorkouts` (`applyBodyweightProgress` rewrites each beginner/novice line to the earned rung). **Regression-safe**: a movement at level 0 is left untouched, so a fresh beginner's session is byte-identical to today. Threaded through the scheduled plan (`generator.ts`), the on-demand generator, and the recovery-swap gym.
- Tests: 10 in `bodyweight-progression.test.ts` (family mapping incl. exclusions, advance/regress/hold, ladder bounds, persist, read-back). Science: SCIENCE_LOG §BI. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean, full suite 3013 pass. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — "Match heart rate" picker now shows the recording's date

- **Fix**: The HR picker in the strength post-session summary (`strength-summary-card.ts:pickerView`) labelled each candidate recording with time + duration only (e.g. `20:09 · 59m`). When two synced recordings shared the same activity type (e.g. two "Hiit" entries on different days), they were indistinguishable. Each row now leads with the date (`Mon 2 Jun, 20:09 · 59m`) so the user can pick the recording that belongs to the session they just finished. New `dateLabel()` helper alongside the existing `timeLabel()`.
- **Fix**: A synced strength recording that filled a planned gym slot overwrote the slot's stored `displayName` with the watch's generic activity label ("HIIT"), so the session read as "HIIT" in Recent / activity-detail (which resolve the name from the actual via `resolveActivityDisplayName`). The gym slot-fill now keeps the planned session name (`activity-review.ts:1173`, e.g. "Lower-body & core strength").
- **Diagnosis (not yet fixed)**: Root cause of the duplicated Tuesday gym + un-mergeable HIIT recording is a **key collision**: injury-adapted strength sessions are built with no `id` (`injury-strength.ts`), so a non-scheduled guided completion keys `rated`/`garminActuals` by the bare display name (`strength-complete.ts:311`, `workout.id ?? workout.n`). Two same-name gym days then share one key — one day's rating/HR bleeds onto the other, the second recording can't bind, and the already-`rated` slot is hidden from the matching screen (`activity-review.ts:400`). Fix needs day-unique keys at the scheduling/completion layer plus de-duping the added adhoc slot; deferred as a focused change.
- **Feature — merge a floating recording into a done strength session** (`strength-summary-card.ts`): the post-session summary (reachable by tapping a Done gym card) now (1) names the attached recording's date ("From the recording on Mon 1 Jun, 20:09." — a wrong-day attach is visible at a glance), (2) offers a muted **"Change recording"** link when alternatives exist, opening the existing picker even though HR is already attached (before, an attached HR hid the Match button entirely — with the key collision putting Monday's HR on Tuesday's session, the user had no way to fix it), (3) `hrCandidates` now also offers **standalone synced activities** (`garmin-<gid>` actuals with HR) — after a sync clears `garminPending` they're the only remaining copy, and they're exactly the floating "HIIT" card next to the done session, and (4) `attachHR` is now a true **merge**: it deletes the picked recording's standalone copies (actual + adhoc + rated entry) so the session shows once, and releases a previously-attached recording back to `__pending__` so it can be re-bound to its own day.
- **Why the home "Review →" button disappears**: it (and the whole `openActivityReReview` flow, `activity-review.ts:252`) is driven by `garminPending` — once a sync consumes the pending records there is nothing to review and the button hides. Re-review without pending records is part of the deferred re-matching work; the merge above no longer depends on it.

## 2026-06-03 — Phase 2: in-gym contrast power-block (plyo paired with the heavy lift)

- **Why**: Plyometrics existed only as a standalone session; users wanted explosive work *integrated* into their normal strength sessions. The evidence-based way is contrast (complex) training: pairing a heavy lift with a matched jump leverages post-activation potentiation (Science for Sport) for more power per session.
- **What**: In **build phase**, intermediate+ running-strength gym sessions now pair the heavy lead lift with a matched jump as a "power block" — Back/Front Squat → Jump Squat, Trap-Bar/Deadlift → Box Jumps (dynamic correspondence). The pairing instruction lives in the lead lift's **cue** (e.g. "Power pair: after each set, explode into the box jumps below, then rest 2 to 3 min") and the jump follows as its own line — never a bare label line, which the session parser would turn into a junk set. The standalone plyo pick (only present on 60+ min sessions) is dropped so a session never prescribes two jumps. Strict PAP rest timing is deliberately not modelled (Tristan: the training adaptation survives sloppy rest; precise timing only squeezes acute jump height).
- **Default-on for intermediate+, with a Settings off-switch** (Tristan's choice). New optional state `plyoInGymEnabled?` (model: `bodyMassSwapEnabled`). Read at session generation: applies to on-demand running-strength immediately and to the plan as weeks regenerate (no forced rebuild). New Account toggle "Plyometrics in gym" (`renderPlyoInGymRow`), shown only to plan-following intermediate+ runners with strength sessions. Threaded through `buildRunningStrengthWorkout` (new `contrastPairing` arg, build-gated), `generateGymWorkouts` (new `plyoInGym` arg), `generator.ts` (scheduled), and `session-generator.ts` (on-demand).
- **Gating layers**: opt-in (default-on, off-switch) × ability (intermediate+ only — the builder is only reached for them) × phase (build only). Beginners/novices and base/peak/taper are untouched.
- Tests: 4 contrast cases in `running-pool.test.ts` (pairs in build, byte-identical when off, base-phase no-op, never two jumps). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean, full suite 2983 pass. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Plyometrics time control: foot-contact scaling + a slider

- **Why**: Device testing found the gym time control did nothing for plyometrics across most presets. Root cause: plyo has only 5 moves, so the move-count maxed at 5 above 45 min and 45 / 60 / 75 / 90 produced an identical session. Also, offering a 90-min plyometric session is wrong — plyo is a short, sharp stimulus.
- **What**: `buildPlyometricsWorkout` now treats time as a **foot-contact target** over a short window (~12–30 min). Contacts run from a literature floor (60) up to an **ability-scaled ceiling** — beginner/novice 100, intermediate 120, advanced/competitive 140 (the 80→140 plyo progression range). Both the move count (3/4/5) and the per-move **sets** scale to hit the target, so the control always changes the session. Rep counts are untouched; sets are the standard plyometric volume dial (clamped 2–6). Ceiling passed from `session-generator.ts` by `experienceLevel`.
- **Slider**: the gym time control is now a **range slider** instead of preset tiles. Plyo runs 12–30 min (step 2); other gym focuses keep 20–90 (step 5). The minutes label updates live while dragging; the session rebuilds on release (avoids re-render focus-loss mid-drag). Stored minutes are clamped into the active focus's range on render.
- Numbers: floor 60 and ability ceilings 100/120/140 are literature-sourced (Tristan approved 140 + ability-varying). The 12–30 min plyo window and 2–6 set clamp are sensible defaults, not model constants.
- Tests: `running-pool.test.ts` updated to the new scaling (10 plyo cases incl. longer-session-more-sets and higher-ceiling-more-volume). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean, full suite 2979 pass. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Plyometrics as an on-demand gym focus

- **Why**: The running-strength experience felt static — the explosive, running-specific work (plyometrics) that drives running economy was effectively unreachable. A `'plyo'` category already existed in `running-pool.ts` (pogo hops, box jumps, single-leg bounds, jump squat, depth jump) but sat *last* in the category order, so it only surfaced inside a 60+ min "Running strength" session and only as a single auto-picked move. There was no way to deliberately do a plyometric session.
- **What**: A new **"Plyometrics"** focus in the on-demand gym generator (`session-generator.ts` FOCI + dispatch). New builder `buildPlyometricsWorkout` (`running-pool.ts`) draws only from the existing plyo pool. The focus skips goal/rest straight to preview (like Running strength). The existing Easier / As prescribed / Harder lever selects a difficulty **tier** rather than a load shift (plyo is bodyweight, so the load step is already a no-op): Easier is low-CNS only (never depth jumps / single-leg bounds), Harder leads with the high-CNS moves. Move count scales with time (3 / 4 / 5), with week rotation. The `highSoreness` flag already on the two high-CNS moves doubles as the tier signal — **no new constant, no new exercise**.
- **Ability**: low-intensity plyo is safe for everyone, so beginners/novices get the focus too, clamped to the Easier tier (unlike Running strength, which stays intermediate+ only). **Injury**: suppressed when loaded strength is paused (plyo is higher-impact), falling through to the injury-adapted session. Bodyweight lines carry no load marker, so they don't weight-track, but the session still logs and feeds leg-load.
- **Decided — no plyo-specific prediction term.** Investigated whether opting into plyo should improve the race forecast. It shouldn't: the forecast's strength→economy term (`STRENGTH_MAX_ECONOMY_GAIN_PCT = 3`, §BC) is *already* calibrated to plyo-inclusive training (Beattie & Blagrove 2018), and the 2022 head-to-head meta-analysis (*Sports Med – Open*) found plyo-alone has a *trivial* economy effect (g = −0.13) vs heavy resistance's small effect (g = −0.32). A plyo-specific coefficient is indefensible in either direction; plyo sessions already count as gym dose and already feed the existing term. Dropped.
- **Roadmap (not built)**: in-gym contrast "power block" (heavy lift paired with a matched jump) and an opt-in run warm-up primer, both gated by opt-in / ability / phase. Plan at `~/.claude/plans/okay-i-think-we-re-dazzling-cerf.md`.
- Tests: 8 new cases in `running-pool.test.ts` (parse-clean, plyo-only, time scaling, tier safety, no liftKey, base-phase reorder). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean, full suite 2977 pass. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Manual 1RM entry on the Stats strength page

- **Why**: The strength-progress page has four sections, but three (New bests, Lifts, tonnage) need per-lift weight data that only the in-app guided strength player captures. A user whose gym work syncs in as watch-matched activities (HIIT / generic strength, no exercise detail) sees only Consistency — sessions logged + week streak, no lifts, no PRs. They had no way to tell the app what they actually lift.
- **What**: An "Add a lift" / "Add or update a lift" action on the strength-progress drill-down (`strength-progress-view.ts`, `openManualLiftModal`). A centered modal: pick a lift (curated headline list — squat/deadlift/bench/etc., every key real in `strength-exercise-key.ts` — plus any already-tracked lift), choose **Weight & reps** or **1RM**, enter the numbers, see a live Epley-derived 1RM preview, Save. Writes via new `seedManualLift` (`strength-log-persist.ts`): seeds `est1rmKg` + `est1rmReps` + `lastWeightKg`/`lastReps`, marks `est1rmSource: 'user'`, appends a baseline history point. Available in every mode that reaches the page.
- **Provenance / override**: `est1rmSource` widened to `'user' | 'derived'` (mirrors FTP/CSS/VDOT). A manual entry is authoritative (overwrites in either direction — it's the athlete's stated number), but a later logged set still supersedes it via the existing `est1rmReps` comparability gate, flipping provenance back to `'derived'` on a real PR. No new override machinery — the reps-comparable gate is the confidence mechanism.
- **Correctness**: a direct 1RM entry is stored as-is, NOT run through Epley — `estimate1RM(w, 1)` returns `w × (1 + 1/30)`, which would inflate a directly-entered max by ~3%. Only weight × reps gets the Epley estimate. The modal preview special-cases reps=1 the same way so the shown number matches what's saved. (Caught by the new test.)
- **Discoverability / prescription**: a **weight × reps** entry seeds working-weight memory (`lastWeightKg`), so the next session shows "Last: X". A **direct 1RM** seeds the benchmark only — `StrengthLiftEntry.lastWeightKg`/`lastReps` are now **optional**, and a pure 1RM does NOT write them (a 1RM is not a working weight; seeding it would make the next session prescribe "Last: <1RM> × 1" and bump a working set up from a max). Readers guarded for the benchmark-only case (`strength-progression.ts` holds, `strength-lift-detail.ts` shows "1RM set manually — log a working set…", `strength-summary-card.ts` omits the weight). Fills the Lifts section + seeds the per-lift trend with a baseline (a single seed is not a "PR" — New bests still needs a logged advance).
- **Decision (Tristan): no est-1RM decay.** est-1RM stays a one-way PB staircase — it only advances on a comparable-or-stronger set and is never dragged down by a lighter training day (or by time off). The 1RM represents the athlete's demonstrated max and holds. Decay (analogous to the FTP/CSS/VDOT detraining model) was considered and explicitly declined.
- Tests: 9 `seedManualLift` cases in `strength-log-persist.test.ts` (20 in file) + existing `strength-progression` suite green. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean, full suite 2967 pass. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Activity label consistency, sport-change persistence, logged-strength tap recap

Dogfooding surfaced three bugs around synced cross-training (e.g. a "HIIT") and logged strength.

- **Label divergence (Recent vs detail)**: a synced HIIT read "HIIT" in the Home "Recent" list but "General Sport" when opened. Two code paths resolved the name independently. New canonical `resolveActivityDisplayName(actual, fallback)` in `sport-picker-modal.ts` (sport-aware: respects `manualSport`, drops a stale "General Sport", falls back to `formatActivityType`). Both the Recent row (`home-view.ts`) and the detail title + sport row (`activity-detail.ts`) now read from it, so a list row and the detail it opens can't disagree.
- **Sport change never persisted**: `reclassifyActivity` (sport-picker-modal.ts) computed load/leg deltas and saved, but **never wrote `actual.manualSport`** — the field was read in three places (`getEffectiveSport`, the detail title, the run check) yet assigned nowhere in the codebase. So a manual reclassify reverted on the next render/sync. Added the one missing assignment; the choice now sticks everywhere.
- **Logged strength card opened "Start session"**: tapping a gym/strength card always opened the editable detail overlay (Start / Mark-done), even when the session was already logged. Added `buildLoggedStrengthResult` (pure reconstruction of a `StrengthCompletionResult` from the stored `garminActual`) and a shared `openGymCardDetail(id, viewWeek)` helper used by both plan-view card-header bindings: a done session now opens the same recap (`openStrengthSummary` — weights, RPE, HR) the user saw at completion; an undone session still opens the editable detail; HYROX (own recap) falls through.
- **Double-counted sessions (root cause + fix)**: a console state snapshot confirmed each genuinely-completed HIIT existed **twice** — a Strava copy (`strava-…`) and a Garmin-webhook copy (raw numeric id) of the same session, with identical-but-differently-formatted timestamps (`…Z` vs `…+00:00`). This is the dev account receiving the same workout from both pipes (Garmin webhook is single-approved-account only; shipped users are Strava-only until Garmin approval). The Strava-over-Garmin dedup existed but only ran *inside* `matchAndAutoComplete` (during a sync); if `syncActivities` errored (revoked token / RLS) the duplicates persisted across loads, showing twice in Recent and as duplicate adhoc cards defaulting onto Friday in the tri/HYROX plan. Extracted it into `reconcileCrossSourceDuplicates()` (Strava > Apple > Garmin, ±4h start + 15% duration match, pure/local) that **also runs on every app launch** before the network syncs, and now prunes the superseded copy from all three buckets (`garminActuals`, `adhocWorkouts`, `garminPending`) so it can't be resurrected on the next sync. The Garmin pipeline is untouched (it matters post-approval); Strava just wins when both exist. 5 tests in `reconcile-cross-source.test.ts` reproduce the exact dogfooding state.
- **Synced cross-training dumped on Friday**: `addAdhocWorkout` created adhocs with no `dayOfWeek`, so the tri/HYROX plan grouping (`dayOfWeek ?? 4`) placed every synced cross-training session on Friday. Now sets `dayOfWeek` from the activity start time (Mon=0..Sun=6) at creation, and both tri/HYROX plan groupers derive it from `garminTimestamp` when absent so existing adhocs land on their real day too.
- **"Discard activity" silently no-op on a guided session**: `removeGarminActivity` located the activity via `garminMatched[garminId] → garminActuals key`, but a guided/manual completion is keyed by the workout NAME with no `garminMatched` entry, so the permanent-discard path never removed it ("I pressed delete and it didn't delete"). The discard now also scrubs any `garminActuals` entry matching the `garminId` by VALUE (plus its rating, matched entry, and adhoc).
- **Tapping a completed strength session in tri offered to re-start it**: `openTriWorkoutDetail` routed every gym/strength workout straight to the "Start session / Mark as done" breakdown, ignoring done-state (the running plan's `openGymCardDetail` fix didn't cover the tri path). Now a DONE strength session opens what was actually done — a matched **synced** activity (e.g. a HIIT logged onto the slot) opens the rich activity detail (HR zones, stats, sport, Discard bin — the same view Recent opens); a guided/manual strength opens its exercise recap (`openStrengthSummary`). Undone sessions still open the editable breakdown. Diagnosed from a live state dump: the duplicated Tuesday "Lower-body & core strength" was a second, *added* slot (`adhoc-…` id), not a render glitch.
- **Delete from the recap**: added a "Delete this session" action to `openStrengthSummary`. A user-added session (`adhoc-`/`holiday-`) is removed entirely from `triWorkouts`/`adhocWorkouts` (+ rating + actual); a plan slot is un-completed (rating + actual cleared, slot stays). This replaces a per-card "Remove" button that was added and then reverted at the user's request — deletion now lives inside the session, reached by tapping in.
- Typecheck clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean, full suite green. NOT device-verified — **requires a rebuild/redeploy to take effect in the running app.**

Executed `docs/SECURITY_SWEEP_BRIEF.md` — the broad sweep the focused 2026-06-03 edge-function pass did not cover. Full prioritized report in `docs/SECURITY_SWEEP_REPORT.md`.

## 2026-06-03 — Account "Strength sessions" control (post-onboarding gym lever)

- **Gap**: The wizard sets `gymSessionsPerWeek` once and there was no post-onboarding way to change it. Account had runner-type and commute editors but no gym one. A user who onboarded at gym=0 (e.g. a 70.3 athlete whose tri-setup strength slider defaulted to 0) got no planned strength and no lever to add it — only the on-demand generator or an injury nudge. The strength-progress card stayed empty for them because nothing planned strength.
- **Fix**: New "Strength sessions" row on the Account page (`renderStrengthRow` / `showStrengthSessionsModal` in `account-view.ts`). A centered modal (never a bottom sheet) with 0–3 pills and the Beattie & Blagrove 2018 rationale. Saving writes `onboarding.gymSessionsPerWeek` and rebuilds the plan via `applyGymSessionsChange` → `initializeSimulator` (spinner → reload), mirroring the runner-type editor's rebuild flow. `initializeSimulator` dispatches by `trainingMode`, so it rebuilds the correct mode's plan (running / triathlon / cycling) and preserves training history. The row is gated to running / triathlon / cycling (all plan strength off `s.gs`); hidden for track-only (no plan to rebuild) and HYROX (functional stations are the strength stimulus, `s.gs` is forced to 0). Closes the last item from the gym-bulletproofing audit.
- Tri strength planning already existed end-to-end (tri-setup slider → `s.gs` → up to 2 "Strength" sessions in `plan_engine.triathlon.ts`); this is the missing lever, so adding it immediately unlocks planned strength for tri and running users alike, and fills the strength-progress card with planned data.
- Tests: suite 2949 pass (no new tests — pure UI wiring over existing init paths). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Readiness leg-load floor and caption now respect an injury that blocks running

- **Problem (found dogfooding, injured state)**: The Readiness screen contradicted itself. The injury caption read "Running and swimming blocked by injury. Cycling capped at 40%", while the leg-load note beneath it read "Impact risk slightly elevated if running" — a warning about a run the user cannot do. Underneath the copy, the same incoherence drove the *score*: the 54 / Manage Load reading was the leg-load hard floor, whose entire rationale is impact-injury risk on foot strike. Two independent code paths (`buildInjuryCaption` in `injury/modal.ts`, the leg-load note + floor in `readiness.ts`) wrote to the same surface without reconciling.
- **Fix**: New `impactBlocked` signal on `ReadinessInput`, derived at the call site via `isImpactBlockedByInjury(s.injuryState)` (new helper in `injury/engine.ts` — true when an active injury sets run capacity to 0). When set, `computeReadiness` (1) skips the leg-load hard floor entirely (heavy/moderate/soft), so the score reflects what the athlete can still do rather than a moot running risk, and (2) trims the "if running" / "impact risk" clause off the leg-load note, keeping only the factual lead ("Moderate leg load from General Sport yesterday."). Threaded through every running-model readiness surface so score and label stay same-source: `readiness-view.ts`, `home-view.ts`, `daily-coach.ts` (ring label), and `tri-readiness.ts` (run discipline only — the sole tri input that carries leg load). Call sites that pass no `recentLegLoads` (`session-recommendation`, `coach-workout-modal`) were left untouched — the floor can't fire there.
- **Decision (Tristan)**: the readiness *band label* stays capacity-based and is intentionally NOT made injury-aware. An injured-but-fresh athlete reading "On Track" / "Primed" is correct — injury shortens the trainable menu (you can still cycle, lift, train legs), it doesn't mean you can't train. The ring measures recoverable capacity; the injury caption is the separate layer that scopes what you spend it on. Tissue-specific contraindication is the injury-capacity layer's job, not a readiness modifier.
- Rationale in SCIENCE_LOG §BG. Tests: +3 cases in `readiness.test.ts`, suite 2949 pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Stats VO2 bar and Forecast now agree on "do we have data"

- **Problem**: A thin-data athlete (e.g. a cross-trainer with a training-derived VDOT but no entered PBs) could see a "VO2 Max" bar on the Stats card while the no-target-race Forecast showed "No predictions yet." Two surfaces, two independent gates: Stats showed whenever a resolved VDOT existed; the Forecast's `buildStandardPredictionContext` returned `null` for `trackOnly`-without-PBs and, more broadly, produced nothing whenever the blend had no PB/LT/recent/device/HR input. Violated the canonical-source rule.
- **Fix**: One canonical resolver + gate in `physiological-vdot.ts` — `resolveRunningVdot(s)` (physiological chain → `getEffectiveVdot` fallback) and `hasRunningFitnessSignal(s)`. Both the Stats VO2 bar (both sites in `stats-view.ts`) and the Forecast grid (`race-forecast-view.ts`) now gate on `hasRunningFitnessSignal`. To let the Forecast honour the wider gate, `predictDistanceStaged` (`blended-fitness.ts`) adds a last-resort fallback: when the weighted blend is empty, predict from the resolved VDOT via the inverse Daniels model (`predictFromVO2`, whose parameter *is* a VDOT). The fallback fires only when the blend is empty, so no signal is double-counted; the result still passes the calibration/durability/shoe staging. A track-only athlete with a real VDOT now gets predictions (the audience the no-race forecast was built for), and the two surfaces show/hide together.
- VO2max and VDOT are kept physically distinct; only the show/hide gate is unified. Targeted race forecast and the raw-VDOT drill-down trend untouched. Rationale in SCIENCE_LOG §BF.
- Tests: 2946 pass (updated the stale `trackOnly`-no-PB-returns-null test to the new contract + added no-signal and helper-consistency cases). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint:ui` clean. NOT device-verified.

Root cause: `buildNoWorkoutHero` and `buildTodayWorkout` in `home-view.ts` each re-derived the week with a partial re-implementation of the plan resolver (it applied only `workoutMoves`, missing adhoc/holiday-injected sessions, `workoutMods` matched by stable id, illness/holiday suppression, comeback-bridge scaling, and the `forceDeload` flag). The "Next:" filter now also excludes completed (`garminActuals`-matched), skipped, and replaced slots so a logged-early future slot isn't shown as next.

## 2026-06-03 — Personal recovery rate: full intensity-banded redesign (ISSUE-256)

A well-trained, high-frequency user saw "1.63× slower than average" — the model rated a strong athlete as the *worst* recoverer. On-device investigation (n=83) showed this was **structural and near-universal**, not an edge case: the fit divided two quantities on incompatible scales — `predictedHours` (the recovery-countdown's readiness-debt, ~8h/avg session) vs `observedHours` (full autonomic HRV/RHR return, 24h floor, 24–96h). Their ratio is a structural ~4× (his p50 = 3.91), so the clamp pinned *any* athlete with ≥16 closed sessions at `k=13`; fitter = worse. Logged as ISSUE-256. Redesigned with Tristan's sign-off (he chose the largest defensible build):

- **New fit basis**: `index = observedHours / expectedRecoveryHours` (both now on the autonomic-return scale), `k_user = clamp(8 × index, [5,13])`. Typical recoverer centres at 1.0×. `kUserHours` keeps its meaning/range so the countdown and ACWR-ceiling consumers are untouched.
- **Literature-anchored expected recovery by intensity** (`EXPECTED_RECOVERY_HOURS`): easy 24h / moderate 36h / hard 54h, from Stanley, Peake & Buchheit (2013), *Sports Med* 43(12):1259–77 (parasympathetic recovery ~24h low / 24–48h threshold / ≥48h high intensity). Anchors approved by Tristan.
- **Fitness-relative intensity, no invented coefficient**: band derived from `GarminActual.hrZones` (Strava computes time-in-zone against the athlete's own zones) via time-weighted mean zone; RPE fallback (Foster 2001 CR10: ≤4/5–6/≥7). A fit athlete's Zone-2 run is judged against the easy expectation, a beginner's same-pace Zone-4 run against the hard one — fairness to fit/high-volume athletes is structural. `classifySessionIntensity`.
- **Clean-window measurement**: a reading is used only if no other session fell on its intervening recovery days (training-through inflates observed). Morning-measurement-aware (`gap < windowDays`), so a 24h recovery is always clean. A never-rest athlete gets `densityLimited = true` and the card says "training too densely to read" rather than a fabricated slow label (accepted trade-off).
- **Robust log-space aggregation** (kills the right-skew that dragged a naive mean to 11.56). Clamp [5,13] and Bayesian prior unchanged.
- **Retrofit**: `backfillIntensityBands` fills bands on existing 90-day entries from their activities (wired into `refreshAdaptiveRecovery`), so the fix applies to the existing log immediately.
- **Card** (`renderPersonalRecoveryCard`): now an honest fair comparison — "X× the typical recovery time", "…faster/slower than typical, for the intensity of the sessions you do", plus the density-limited state.

Files: `adaptive-recovery.ts` (classifier, expected anchors, rewritten `fitKUser`, `backfillIntensityBands`), `types/state.ts` (`intensityBand`/`expectedRecoveryHours` on `SessionImpactEntry`, `densityLimited` on `AdaptiveRecovery`), `main.ts` (backfill in refresh), `recovery-view.ts` (card). 46 tests in `adaptive-recovery.test.ts` (intensity classification, log-space robustness, clean-window, density-limited, retrofit); full suite **2964 green**; tsc + lint:ui clean. SCIENCE_LOG `k_user` Addendum 2. ISSUE-256 fixed in code.

**Device-verified on Tristan's data**: the value moved from the pinned 1.63× (worst) to **1.02× (typical)** — the correct read for a fit athlete, confirming the redesign works end-to-end. Card polish from that check (`renderPersonalRecoveryCard` / `recoveryCardShell`): (1) now leads with a plain verdict ("Recovers at a typical rate") with the multiplier as 1-decimal subtext — the bare "1.02×" read as "not ready"; the "typical" band = whatever rounds to 1.0× (within 5%, tied to display rounding, not a new constant); (2) swapped the sun/asterisk icon (mistaken for a loading spinner) for the HRV pulse icon; (3) **fixed a real width bug** — the card renders inside the already-padded Detailed Metrics section yet `recoveryCardShell` added its own `padding:0 16px`, so it was double-guttered (32px) and visibly narrower than every sibling card; removed the redundant gutter and matched the HRV/RHR cards' `padding:20px` / `border-radius:16px`.

## 2026-06-03 — Sleep-debt chart hour labels no longer crowd at the top

The cumulative sleep-debt chart (`buildSleepBankLineChart`, `hourReferenceLines: true`) crammed `2h/3h/4h` on top of each other near the target line on a wide deficit range. Cause: the step mixed 1h spacing below 4h with 2h spacing above, so on a ~9–10h range in a 100px-tall chart (~8px/hour) the close-spaced labels overlapped.

- The hour step is now derived from the chart's actual pixels-per-hour with a `MIN_LABEL_PX = 12` floor: `hourStep = ceil(MIN_LABEL_PX / pxPerHour)`. One consistent step for the whole chart instead of a mixed 1h/2h rule. Wide ranges now read `2h/4h/6h/8h/10h` evenly; narrow ranges still get 1h granularity. Same `MIN_LABEL_PX` also gates the target-line collision skip.
- `src/calculations/sleep-insights.ts` only. tsc clean. Web-verified visually; not yet device-verified.

## 2026-06-03 — Illness no longer drops plan adherence (the promised behaviour)

The illness banner promises "skipped workouts don't count against adherence," but it was false: an illness-rested run still sat in the adherence denominator (no completion → adherence dropped), and a rested triathlon session was counted as a completion (inflating the ratio). Both now reconstruct the illness rest days from the persisted `illnessState.schedule` + `planStartDate` (which survive recovery — `clearIllness` only flips `active`):
- New shared predicate `wasIllnessRestDay(illness, dateISO)` in `illness-rules.ts` (built on the existing `getTodayCapacity`).
- **Running** (`plan-adherence.ts`): subtracts full-rest days from each past week's run denominator, like pushed sessions (capped so a fully-rested week is excluded entirely, not scored 0%).
- **Triathlon** (`tri-adherence.ts`): skips sessions whose day was a full-rest day, so a rested session counts neither for nor against — instead of being booked as a completion.
- Known limitation: only the most-recent illness is on state, so an older illness window can't be retroactively corrected. Above-neck "reduced/easy" days are unaffected (those runs were still expected; the existing 95%-of-reduced-distance check already handles them).
- 2 new plan-adherence tests (rest days subtracted; a fully-rested week excluded). Suite 2912 green; tsc + `lint:ui` clean. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-02 — Gym bulletproofing: /persona-qa + /mode-audit fix pass

Ran both audits (12 agents) across the whole gym/strength surface, then fixed every P1 they confirmed. All decisions where coaching judgement was needed were signed off by Tristan.

- **P1 safety — beginner heavy load.** The on-demand "Running strength" focus called `buildRunningStrengthWorkout` (which leads with Back Squat 4×5 @80%) for ALL levels; a total beginner could be prescribed heavy barbell work. Now restricted to intermediate+; beginners/novices route through `generateGymWorkouts` → bodyweight templates. `session-generator.ts`.
- **P1 data — HYROX weight loss.** A pure gym/strength session in HYROX mode completed with no confirm-weights step (working weights lost). Now mirrors triathlon: non-`hyroxComponents` gym/strength routes to the shared `openStrengthWorkoutDetail`; stations/bricks keep their benchmark path and now re-render on completion. `hyrox/workout-detail-modal.ts`.
- **P1 safety — sick runner kept full strength + dead myocarditis rule.** The live illness modal wrote only `{severity}` and the running plan called the legacy run-only mod path, so a sick runner kept "Heavy Lower 3×5 @80%" + plyos, and the below-neck strength-suppression engine was never invoked. **Wired the v2 illness engine** (Tristan's call): the modal now captures symptom location (above/below neck, fever/aches) + severity, builds the classification + day-by-day schedule (`classifyIllness`/`buildSchedule`), and all three plan-views (running/tri/HYROX) call the canonical `applyIllnessMods`, which scales every discipline and RESTS strength for below-neck illness (Schwellnus 2016). The numeric duration/MTL scaling was centralised into `markRest`/`scaleAndCap`; the legacy fallback now scales all disciplines too. `illness-modal.ts`, `illness-rules.ts`, the three plan-views.
- **P1 coherence — acute-injury contradiction.** Acute/shutdown showed "Complete Rest" while the nudge offered a region-safe session. Per Tristan: SHOW the adapted session — the generator now surfaces the region-safe submaximal session in the acute week and rewords the rest card, so plan + nudge agree. `generator.ts`.
- **P1 — false PR / non-monotonic trend.** Epley est-1RM inflates with reps, so a lighter 12-rep day minted a phantom "New best" over a heavier 5-rep day. ## 2026-06-02 — Edge-function security hardening (post-review)

Server-side security review of `supabase/functions/**` + migrations surfaced real issues; fixed the exploitable/quick ones, deferred low-value/high-breakage-risk ones with reasoning.

- **CRITICAL — Garmin webhook had no caller auth.** Anyone knowing the URL could inject health data or trigger a deregistration that deletes a user's `garmin_tokens`. Added a shared-secret check (`GARMIN_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, constant-time). **DONE + enforced.** Garmin's portal STRIPS query strings on save (`?key=` didn't survive) but preserves the path, so the secret rides as a **path segment**: configured URL is `.../functions/v1/garmin-webhook/<secret>` in all 8 active endpoint boxes. Function reads the segment after `garmin-webhook` (query + `x-webhook-secret` header kept as fallbacks). Env set. Verified: no/wrong secret → 401, correct → 200, GET verify → 200. Fail-open design = zero downtime during rollout.
- **CRITICAL (self-inflicted, fixed) — cron secret in a repo file.** `PURGE_CRON_SETUP.sql` held `PURGE_CRON_SECRET` in plaintext. Deleted the file (never committed); secret lives only in Vault + function env.
- **HIGH — `garmin_activities` had RLS disabled.** Cross-user isolation depended on app-code filters only. New migration `20260602000000_enable_rls_garmin_activities.sql` enables RLS + a `user_id = auth.uid()` SELECT policy (service-role writes bypass RLS, unaffected). **Needs Tristan to apply via the dashboard SQL editor.**
- **HIGH — RevenueCat secret compare not constant-time** → `constantTimeEqual`. Also added an `auth.admin.getUserById` existence check on `app_user_id` before writing a subscription row (limits blast radius if the secret leaks).
- **HIGH — `sync-activity-details` had no explicit auth check** → added `auth.getUser()` + explicit `user_id` filter (RLS already covered it; belt-and-braces).
- **MEDIUM — CORS `startsWith` over-match** (`http://localhost` matched `http://localhost.evil.com`). Fixed across 6 user-facing functions to exact-match + a `^http://(localhost|127.0.0.1)(:\d+)?$` regex (any dev port still works; verified `localhost.evil.com` no longer reflected). Also added the missing `https://mosaicrunning.run` origin to `coach-chat`/`coach-generate-workout`/`screenshot-vision` (latent prod-web CORS bug) and deduped `coach-narrative`'s list.
- **MEDIUM — OAuth callbacks leaked provider/DB error bodies** to the client (`details: text`/`raw: tokenJson`). Now logged server-side, generic error returned. `garmin_tokens.raw` no longer duplicates the token blob.
- **MEDIUM — `coach-chat` accepted arbitrary client tool definitions** (prompt-injection vector) → `sanitiseTools` now allowlists the 6 canonical tool names.
- **LOW — Garmin access token logged in full** → redacted to first 8 chars; `userMetrics` raw log strips credential fields. `sync-today-steps` switched to a user-scoped client (RLS double-protects); `garmin-backfill` CORS tightened.
- **Deferred (logged in OPEN_ISSUES):** wildcard CORS on the 3 load-bearing sync-pipe functions (`sync-activities`, `sync-strava-activities`, `sync-physiology-snapshot`) and the `garmin-backfill`/`sync-today-steps` service-role-for-auth pattern — JWT-gated defense-in-depth, not exploitable; deferred to a device-tested pass to avoid risking the data pipe. Also: move coach-chat tool *definitions* server-side (name allowlist is the interim fix).
- All 13 changed functions redeployed (`--use-api`, clean bundle). CORS + webhook behavior smoke-tested. NOT device-verified in-app.

## 2026-06-02 — Gym leg load feeds recovery (gym ↔ endurance flow) — SHIPPED
- Built the leg-load flow designed in `docs/LEG_LOAD_FLOW_DESIGN.md`. The gym is now a writer + reader of the existing `s.recentLegLoads` ledger (which runs + cross-training already feed; 48 h decay, RBE, readiness floors). Previously the gym was invisible to recovery — a heavy squat day moved readiness by zero.
- **Write side** (`src/calculations/strength-leg-load.ts`): `legLoadRaw = K_STRENGTH(0.9) × legScore × intensityMult × effortMult`. `legScore` = leg-muscle hard sets from the canonical `deriveWorkedMuscleGroups` (an upper/core day scores 0 and writes nothing); `intensityMult` from mean %1RM (ref 80%); `effortMult` from session RPE (ref 7). Calibrated so a canonical hard leg day ≈ 16 units (matches the prior `legFeel: 'heavy'` 0.35/min × ~45 min anchor). Stamped on `actual.legLoadRaw` at completion (`strength-complete.ts`) and written via the shared `buildStrengthLegLoadEntry` (RBE + heavy-day slower decay 1.05/1.20). `computeLegLoad` (`sport-picker-modal.ts`) returns the stamp for strength so the reconcile/launch sweep handles it uniformly — single source, no divergence. Tracking only (not added to CTL/ATL/TSS → no double-count).
- **Read side** (`buildGymLegLoadNudge` → `plan-view.ts`): a passive muted caption on a leg-day gym card when the legs are already loaded (planned raw ≥ 7 AND decayed total ≥ 20): "Legs are still loaded from {source}. Consider easing today's leg session. Drop a set or back off the weight." Suggest-only, no plan mutation.
- **Tri coverage closed (end-to-end trace fix)**: an end-to-end audit found the write happened in tri mode but was invisible — `computeTriReadiness` never read the ledger, and the nudge was running-plan-view only. Fixed: the leg-load floor is now threaded into the **run discipline only** in `computeTriReadiness` (swim is non-impact, bike tolerates tired legs — flooring them would over-flag), and the nudge is now on the tri gym card too via a shared `gymLegLoadNudgeForWorkout` helper (one source for both plan-views, can't drift). HYROX uses the running readiness model so its floor already applied; stations stay on their own MTL ledger (no double-write). `tri-readiness.test.ts` (2) proves run-only flooring.
- Science self-determined (Tristan delegated the constants), logged in `SCIENCE_LOG.md → §BE`. Running + HYROX-readiness + tri (run-discipline floor + nudge); HYROX *stations* (MTL) deferred. New `GarminActual.legLoadRaw` field. 20 tests (`strength-leg-load.test.ts` 18 + `tri-readiness.test.ts` 2), full suite green (2925). ⚠️ Not device-verified.
- **Re-completion dedupe hardening**: a pure `dropSupersededStrengthEntries` drops the same activity (by garminId) and any strength entry within ±10 min before writing the fresh one, so re-rating a gym session updates its one leg-load entry instead of stacking a second (previously self-healed only on the next reconcile sweep). Mirrors the ±10-min same-sport rule reconcile uses; run/cross-training entries untouched.

## 2026-06-02 — Cross-user data leak closed (RLS on garmin_activities) — LAUNCH BLOCKER

- **Bug (found while debugging an FTP issue):** a freshly-signed-in empty account displayed a forecast computed from OTHER accounts' activities. Root cause was multi-tenant data isolation, NOT FTP/Strava. `public.garmin_activities` had **RLS disabled**, and three reads did no `user_id` filter — `loadActivitiesFromDB` (`tri-activity-loader.ts`), onboarding `fetchRecentActivities` (`review.ts`), and the `sync-activities` edge fn (the main launch sync) — so every authenticated user loaded the union of all users' activities (capped 500). The FTP "193 vs 295" saga was a symptom: 193 was a leaked ride from another account.
- **Full read-only audit** → `docs/DATA_ISOLATION_AUDIT.md` (RLS coverage of every table, all leak sites, fix sequence). Most tables were already correctly locked (`user_plan_settings`, tokens, `daily_metrics`, sleep, coach, etc.). `metric_overrides` + `physiology_snapshot_daily` are also RLS-off but latent (no readers).
- **Fix shipped:**
  - *Stage 1 (client filters):* new `getUserId()` in `supabaseClient.ts` (session user id, awaits hydration). `loadActivitiesFromDB` + `fetchRecentActivities` now `&user_id=eq.<id>`; `sync-activities` now `.eq('user_id', user.id)` on both reads. Corrected the loader's false "RLS handles it" comment.
  - *Stage 2 (RLS — the server-side lock):* enabled RLS + `garmin_activities_own` policy (`FOR ALL using (user_id = auth.uid())`) on `garmin_activities`, verified live. Scopes every read path at the DB level. Ingestion unaffected (webhook + Strava sync write via service role → bypass RLS; client dedup-delete covered by the FOR ALL policy).
- **Remaining (not blocking):** redeploy edited `sync-activities` (optional — RLS already covers it); RLS on the two latent tables; migrate `garmin_activities`/`activity_details` unique key from global `garmin_id` → composite `(user_id, garmin_id)` (P1, closes a cross-user upsert-clobber path). ⚠️ Not yet verified on a real 2-user test.
- Also surfaced: `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` env var has a stray leading space that breaks the Supabase MCP + CLI (trim with `tr -d '[:space:]'`). Deployed `sync-strava-activities` v90 (avg-watts FTP eligibility fallback) earlier in the session — harmless, kept.

## 2026-06-02 — Strength training now improves the race forecast (surfaced in onboarding)

- **Planned strength sessions raise the projected race time.** Strength + plyometric work improves running economy (~2-4% RE, ~2-5% TT performance — Beattie & Blagrove 2018), so the forecast now credits it. Added as a **future-projection term in the training-horizon model** (`applyTrainingHorizonAdjustment`, `training-horizon.ts`), NOT a retroactive pace multiplier — the blend's current predictors (VDOT/LT/PB/Tanda/HR) already contain present economy, so a retroactive factor would double-count. The run-volume horizon term carries no strength signal, so the strength term is additive. `strengthGainPct = 3% × (1 − e^(−weeks_eff/10)) × min(sessions/2, 1)`, folded under the existing `max_gain_cap_pct` clamp + VDOT-barrier guardrails. Magnitude (3% ceiling) signed off by Tristan. Constants `STRENGTH_MAX_ECONOMY_GAIN_PCT`, `STRENGTH_TAU_WEEKS` in `strength-constants.ts`.
- **Gated on planned `gymSessionsPerWeek` (`s.gs`)**, threaded through every forecast site (`calculateLiveForecast` + `calculateForecast` → `refreshBlendedFitness`, the forecast-trajectory builder, `renderer.ts`, `events.ts`, onboarding `forecastForSessions`) so all surfaces stay coherent. `0`/omitted strength → byte-identical output for non-lifters (regression-locked).
- **Onboarding callout.** The plan-preview shows a `pp-note-card` isolating the benefit ("Your N strength sessions are worth about X of the projected finish… Beattie & Blagrove 2018"), computed by differencing the forecast with vs without strength at the same run count. Reinforces the schedule-step nudge.

"Set this goal" commits both deltas in a single regen (`bumpSessionsAndGymAndRegen`, runs cap 7 / strength cap 3). The goal slider's fast end now also covers max strength so the goal can't run off the range.
- **Fixed the goal-overlay chance jumping / moving the wrong way when adding sessions** (user-reported, both steppers). `goalChanceForState` used to clone the sim state with bumped `rw`/`epw`/`gs`; `runMarathonForecastSim` then re-derived its own mean improvement from that bumped count, and the cone's spread scales with the mean — but the nonlinear VDOT→time map compresses a higher-mean spread into a *narrower* cone in seconds, so for an aggressive goal more sessions could *lower* the chance (e.g. +1 run → 50%, +2 → <5%). Fix: stop mutating the sim's session counts; let only the strength/run-aware forecast **override** move the cone centre while the spread stays pinned to the base plan. Chance is now a smooth, monotonic function of the displayed forecast. New regression test (`race-forecast-simulation.test.ts`): chance is monotonic and steps by <0.5 across an override ramp. Suite 2888 green.
- **Tests**: 6 new training-horizon tests (monotonic in sessions, dose caps at 2/wk, saturates in plan length, approaches the 3% ceiling at full adoption, 0-gym regression lock, stays within the 15% global cap). Full suite 2887 green; tsc + `lint:ui` clean. Science: `SCIENCE_LOG.md → §BC`. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-02 — Injury cross-training substitute hardening (intensity scaling + allow-list)

- **Limited capacity now scales intensity, not duration.** When an injury frees aerobic time, the cross-training substitute (`buildAerobicOffer`, `src/calculations/capability-substitution.ts`) keeps the full freed minutes (aerobic-engine maintenance is the point) and dials the prescribed RPE down in proportion to the substitute discipline's capacity: `rpe = max(1, round(baseRPE × cap/100))`. A 50%-capacity bike holds the same minutes at ~half the RPE, with "kept very easy" copy. Previously a "limited" (50%) discipline got the same full-effort 1:1 session as a fully-able one (it only gated on `capacity > 0`). Science: `SCIENCE_LOG.md → §BB`.
- **`preferredCrossTraining` is now a hard allow-list** (`pickAerobicSubstitute`, `src/injury/engine.ts`). If the athlete named one cross-training sport and the injury blocks it, no aerobic substitute is offered rather than silently falling through to a bike/erg they may not own. An unknown preference string still falls through to the capacity ladder. Shared by running rehab and tri/HYROX capability offers, so the behaviour is identical across modes.
- **Acute phase unchanged** (deliberate, per Tristan): tri/HYROX still surface offers during acute; the user can ignore them. Tri/HYROX use gates-not-phases and don't do hard complete rest.
- **Tests**: extracted the pure `buildAerobicOffer` (generator-free) and added 10 positive-path tests covering intensity scaling, full-duration invariance, RPE floor, copy switch, discipline badges, and the allow-list. `capability-substitution.test.ts` 14 → 24 tests; full injury suite 152 green. Closes the audit gap where `buildCapabilityOffers` had only empty-return coverage.

## 2026-06-02 — Adjust now feeds training load (harder done = more fitness), forecast stays plan-neutral

- **Question (Tristan)**: should the Adjust Harder/Easier choice affect fitness and forecast? Agreed model: the **slider is intent, not fact** — it must not move the forecast on its own (that would be phantom fitness, and gameable). Completing the session is what moves fitness, through the load you actually accumulate. Forecast stays plan-neutral; fitness (CTL) responds only to realized load.
- **Part 1 — planned load reflects the rung.** `applyObjectScale` (workout-adjust-overlay.ts) now recomputes a bike/swim session's `aerobic`/`anaerobic` from the chosen rung via the **existing** `loadForBike`/`loadForSwim` helpers (now exported) — the same per-kind TSS/min the plan engine uses (bike endurance 0.85 → threshold 1.7 → VO2 1.9 TSS/min, with rung-appropriate anaerobic share). A pure duration change scales existing load proportionally (load ∝ duration). So a harder-planned week shows heavier load bars. Originals stashed (`originalAerobic`/`originalAnaerobic`) so Reset restores. No invented constants.
- **Part 2 — manual "Mark as Done" deposits load (synced activity overrides).** Tri/cycling fitness CTL is rebuilt at launch from the synced activity log; a manually-completed session (rated, no synced activity) previously deposited **zero** fitness. New `manualDoneTriActivities(wks, planStartDate)` (tri-benchmarks-from-history.ts) emits synthetic swim/bike/run activities for those sessions (planned `aerobic+anaerobic` encoded as `iTrimp = TSS×150`), fed **only** to the per-discipline CTL call in `main.ts` — never to benchmark (CSS/FTP) derivation. Override guard: any session with `matchedActivityId`/`status==='completed'` is skipped, so a real synced activity always wins (Strava-canonical, no double-count). Net: doing a harder session deposits more fitness → better forecast; easier deposits less. The effect is a fitness consequence, never an adherence penalty (choosing to adjust is still "done, not missed").
- Decisions confirmed with Tristan (both "yes"). 13 new tests (`manual-done-tri-load.test.ts` 6, intensity ladders 7). tsc clean (app code), full suite 2846 passing, lint green. SCIENCE_LOG §AR addendum extended. Not yet device-verified.

## 2026-06-02 — Triathlon onboarding forecast step: per-discipline session lever + goal time

- **New feature:** triathlon onboarding now has an interactive forecast reveal, mirroring running's plan-ready page (`plan-preview-v2`). A new wizard step `tri-plan-forecast` shows after `initializing` (so the plan + prediction exist) and before the main view: a live projected finish, three **per-discipline session steppers** (swim / bike / run), and an optional **goal time** slider with a live chance-of-beating Monte Carlo.
- **Why per-discipline, not "+1 session" like running:** triathlon's plan is driven by a total-hours budget + volume split, with no integer session count to bump. A swim and a long ride are very different doses, so the lever is per-discipline. Each +1 adds that discipline's representative session length (`TRI_AVG_SESSION_HOURS`, the same constant the generator divides by) and regenerates the plan **in memory** so the forecast and each row's impact update immediately. The per-discipline horizon model decides how much each discipline moves the number — no invented multiplier. The generator's 3-session cap bounds each stepper.
- **Persistence (mirrors running's `bumpSessionsAndRegen`):** Continue commits the chosen volume for real — writes the bumped split + hours into the onboarding record and re-runs `initializeSimulator` so the generated weeks gain the sessions — then pins the goal to `triConfig.targetFinishTimeSec` (carries to the post-onboarding Forecast tab).
- **New module** `src/calculations/tri-session-lever.ts` (pure, testable): `computeBumpedVolume` (session delta to split + hours, never shrinks a discipline, caps respected), `applyTriSessionDelta` (in-memory clone+regen, preserves historical activity by week index so current fitness is unchanged), `forecastTriWithDelta`, `goalChanceTriWithDelta`. New step `src/ui/wizard/steps/tri-plan-forecast.ts`. Constants `TRI_AVG_SESSION_HOURS` / `TRI_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_DISCIPLINE` + `countSessions` now exported from `plan_engine.triathlon.ts` (single source). `liveTone`/`liveLabel`/`deriveBounds` exported from `triathlon/goal-time-overlay.ts`.
- 13 new tests (`tri-session-lever.test.ts`), full suite green (2836 pass). SCIENCE_LOG §AZ. ⚠️ Not device-verified.
- **Device-feedback iteration (same day):** (1) the hero now shows the Monte Carlo **likely range** ("Likely 7:05 to 7:42 on race day", interquartile p25–p75) so the simulation is visible without setting a goal; the goal-chance MC still appears behind "Do you have a goal time?". (2) Capped disciplines (bike/run at the 3-session cap) no longer show a silently-disabled +: the caption now reads "N sessions/week · the plan builds volume over the block" so the deliberate cap is legible. The 3-session cap is **kept on purpose** (not raised): there is no physiological threshold at 3-vs-4 sessions, but adding unaccustomed frequency at onboarding spikes the chronic-load baseline (ACWR, Gabbett 2016), running is the highest overuse-injury discipline, and past ~3 sessions/discipline gains come from duration + intensity distribution (Seiler 80/20), not extra sessions. Rationale added to SCIENCE_LOG §AZ.

## 2026-06-02 — Endurance readiness reads 0 across all disciplines after sign-in (user-reported)

- **Bug (user-reported):** after a fresh sign-in the **Endurance** forecast factor showed **0 / Not ready** for swim, bike, AND run — even though run weekly volume correctly read 15 km/wk. Root cause: the readiness score is a weighted geometric mean of `volumeRatio × longestRatio`, so a zero on either axis collapses the whole score. Run volume survives sign-in because `collectRunsFromState` falls back to the persisted `onboardingRunHistory`, but the **longest-session** and **swim/bike volume** signals read `wks[].garminActuals` *only* — which is empty until activities re-match forward after sign-in. So run's longest read 0 (→ score 0) and swim/bike read 0 on both axes.
- **Fix (two parts):**
  - **Run longest-session** now uses `getLongestRunSec` (the same source the run forecast uses — reads `garminActuals` *and* `onboardingRunHistory`), so the readiness longest matches the forecast and survives sign-in. Closes a "two numbers, same source" gap.
  - **Swim/bike parity:** new optional state field `recentDisciplineActivity` — a slim per-discipline activity summary (last 12 weeks, no polylines/splits) distilled from the DB activity log (`loadActivitiesFromDB`) at launch in `main.ts`. `iterateRecentActuals` (tri-volume-by-discipline) now tops up from it when `garminActuals` is sparse, deduped against actuals by sport + ±10 min so an actively-syncing user sees no change. This gives swim/bike the same sign-in resilience run already had via `onboardingRunHistory`.
- **Cold-sign-in re-render:** the launch activity-summary distillation is a fire-and-forget startup task, so a cold sign-in that lands directly on the Forecast (or the Endurance chip detail) could render *before* the summary persisted and stick at 0 until a manual navigate-away/back. `main.ts`'s post-tri-sync re-render block now also detects the tri Forecast view (`tri-fc-account-btn`) and the open chip detail (`tri-fcd-view` + new `data-chip` attribute → re-renders the same chip), matching the existing stats/progress/home refresh pattern.
- New tests: `tri-volume-by-discipline.test.ts` sign-in-resilience block (4) — recovers swim/bike/run hours + longest from the summary when `garminActuals` is empty, excludes out-of-window entries, dedupes overlaps. 231 tests pass across prediction/durability/horizon/readiness/tri-volume; typecheck clean for changed files (remaining `_holiday-p1.integration.test.ts` + `manual-done-tri-load.test.ts` errors are pre-existing / concurrent-agent WIP, unrelated). ⚠️ Not device-verified.
- **Separately surfaced during testing (NOT fixed here):** Bike FTP disagrees across surfaces from the same Strava — Capacity card shows the held curve-path value (295 W) while the Bike FTP card shows the rejected low-confidence fallback (193 W). This is documented FTP Problem Class 6 (`docs/FTP.md`) and drives the readiness ability-band flicker (193 W → Novice band, 295 W → higher). Awaiting the `[FTP health]` console line to confirm `withCurve` before any code change.

## 2026-06-02 — Plan engine: easy-run floor + consolidation (no more 15-min fragments)

- **Root cause of the 15-min easy runs.** Reported: week 1 of a 40-week marathon plan (athlete 14 km/wk, VDOT 52, 3:22 forecast) prescribed 3.0 km / 15-min easy runs, and the Adjust slider only stretched them to 17 min. Diagnosis: the archetype ramp anchors week 1 at ~14.7 km → a ~76-min weekly minute budget; the untrimmable quality session plus the long run ate almost all of it, so the old `applyHoursBudget` shrank every easy run to its 15-min soft floor and overflowed anyway. (The 17-min slider cap is separate and correct: `DURATION_SCALE_MAX = 1.15`, a deliberate +15% guardrail so a per-session tweak can't change training load/prediction.)
- **Fix part 1 — single 25-min floor + consolidation.** `applyHoursBudget` (`src/workouts/plan_engine.ts`) now holds a single `EASY_FLOOR_MIN = 25` floor and, when the budget is tight, *consolidates*: picks the fewest easy run-days so each survivor lands in `[25 min, natural length]`, drops the rest, and splits the easy budget across them. Fewer, longer easy runs instead of fragments. No upper target — easy runs are still sized by `easyRunMinutes` and only shrunk toward the floor. Quality work is never trimmed; the long run keeps its 40/30 floors.
- **Surfaced.** New `buildRunDayRampNote` on the Plan view (`src/ui/plan-view.ts`) explains when an early week has fewer run-days than the athlete's chosen frequency ("Week N has X runs rather than Y … Run days increase as your volume ramps"). Suppressed during injury/illness/holiday/commute, where the reason differs and another surface owns it. Base/build current+future weeks only.
- **Fix part 2 — the real upstream cause (seeing it rendered: week 1 was two intervals + a stub long run, zero easy).** `qualityCap` was volume- and phase-blind, so a 14 km/wk week got Threshold + VO2, eating the whole budget. Three coordinated, budget-driven changes, designed to scale across the whole plan arc and across plan lengths: (1) **volume-aware quality cap** — a quality session only earns its slot if the budget can also seat a long run + one easy run, floored at 1, climbing to the ability cap as volume ramps; (2) **no VO2 in the base phase** — base quality is tempo, VO2 enters in build/peak; (3) **keep ≥ 1 easy run** — consolidation never drops to zero, accepting a small overflow. Net week 1 for the reported athlete: one tempo + long + one easy (ACWR ~1.2) instead of two intervals + stub long (ACWR ~1.8). Science (tissue-vs-cardio, Gabbett ACWR, Seiler 80/20, base-first periodisation) in SCIENCE_LOG §AX.
- Budget tests rewritten + extended (`plan_engine.budget.test.ts`, 11 tests, incl. quality cap + base-VO2 suppression). Full suite **2840 pass**. Science in SCIENCE_LOG §AX. ⚠️ Not device-verified.

## 2026-06-02 — No-race forecast drill-down readability

- **Trend headline showed raw seconds (`1107.1`).** The "Predicted time over time" chart on the per-distance forecast drill-down (`renderStdDistanceDetail`) was passing a finish-time-in-seconds series straight through `buildBenchmarkTrendChart`, which prints the latest value verbatim — so it read `1107.1` with a `+0.0 since first sample` delta. Added `buildPredictedTimeTrendChart` (parallel to the existing LT/CSS/CP pace wrappers in `benchmark-charts.ts`): headline now formats as a finish time (`18:27`), and the delta as a signed time (`−0:12 since first sample`, or `No change yet` when flat, faster = green). Card title is now distance-specific ("Predicted 5K time over time"). `src/ui/triathlon/benchmark-charts.ts`, `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
- **"+2.0% (long-run shortfall)" on a 5K read wrong.** The long-run durability penalty is real science (Pfitzinger/Daniels — a 5K racer who can't sustain ~35 min easy has an economy deficit) but (a) calling it "long-run shortfall" on a short race is misleading, and (b) the full max penalty was firing because there was *no* run history in the 12-week window, not because a short long-run was measured. Per Tristan: keep the penalty, name it honestly. Durability factor is now `aerobic durability` for 5K/10K and `long-run shortfall` for half/marathon, with a one-line hint that distinguishes the no-history case ("No recent runs of 35 min+ on record, so the endurance base for 5K is unproven") from a measured-short-run case ("Longest recent run is under 35 min…"). Surfaced `durabilityThresholdSec` + `durabilityLongestRunSec` on `StandardForecastDetail` so the copy reflects what was actually measured. `applyLongRunCap` itself is unchanged (the targeted forecast still relies on its zero-data = max-penalty behaviour). `src/calculations/blended-fitness.ts`, `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
- **"What feeds this" labels clarified.** `Capacity` → `Aerobic capacity`, `Threshold pace` → `Lactate threshold pace`, so each row is self-explanatory rather than jargon-shorthand. `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
- **Added a "How we reach {hero}" waterfall.** The page showed factor percentages you couldn't trace to the hero time. Now a waterfall decomposes the finish into ordered stages — Capacity (blend) → Race calibration → Durability → Supershoes → Predicted finish — each row showing the running cumulative time and the signed delta (slower = red, faster = green), mirroring tri's `legWaterfall`. The final row equals the hero because both read the new `StandardPredictionStages` from one `predictDistanceStaged` call. Refactored `predictStandardDistances` + `getStandardForecastDetail` onto a shared `buildStandardPredictionContext` + `predictDistanceStaged` so the grid tile, the hero, and the waterfall total are guaranteed to agree (no parallel recompute). Durability moved into the waterfall (with its relabel + hint); the feeds card is now "What feeds your capacity" (VDOT / LT / volume / calibration status only). `src/calculations/blended-fitness.ts`, `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`. (Discussed but **not** changed: Tristan kept the no-data = max durability penalty — recency of training is exactly what the long-run signal checks, and a stale PB shouldn't dodge it.)
- **Trend chart gated.** With only two points a day apart the chart drew a flat green line that read as filler. Now requires ≥3 points spanning ≥7 days; below that it shows a "needs a few weeks of recorded fitness" message. `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
- **Supershoes toggle on the drill-down.** The grid had the Standard/Supershoes toggle but the detail page silently inherited the choice. Added `buildStdShoesCard` to the detail; toggling re-renders it in place so hero, pace, and waterfall all move by the 3% boost. `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
- Two new reconciliation tests (`blended-fitness.test.ts`, now 17): waterfall stages reconcile to the hero, and the supershoes stage shifts only via `shoeMul` (capacity blend unchanged).
- **Added a forward "if you hold the plan" projection** (Tristan's idea). The trend card now extends the raw trajectory forward as a **dashed line** to a selectable **4 / 8 / 12-week horizon** (segmented selector, re-renders in place), with a headline like "17:52 projected · −0:36 in 8 weeks". `getStandardForecastProjection` (blended-fitness.ts) reuses the targeted forecast's VDOT-gain model (`applyTrainingHorizonAdjustment`) sampled per week with `taper_weeks: 0` (no race to taper into) and recent weekly km as the dose — no new constants. New `buildForecastTrajectoryChart` (benchmark-charts.ts) draws solid history + dashed projection on one time-true axis with a "now" divider. Hidden for users with no plan to project along (`s.rw ≤ 0` / no VDOT) — falls back to the historical-only trend. 5 more tests (now 22). Science: SCIENCE_LOG §BA. `src/calculations/blended-fitness.ts`, `src/ui/triathlon/benchmark-charts.ts`, `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
- **Projection chart redesign (Tristan: "these are not UX… cramped and squished").** Rebuilt `buildForecastTrajectoryChart` with the canonical **liquid-glass sparkline treatment** (glassy card + sheen, vertical gradient fill, layered glow stroke without `feGaussianBlur`, glowing dot+halo marker on the projected endpoint, light-beam drop-line) — the same recipe as the marathon population card, replacing the flat dashed wireframe. De-cramped (card padding + 64px chart height + larger headline). **Clarity fix**: it was unclear that the hero (e.g. 19:24) was "now" and the projection the future. The projection is now **anchored on the adjusted hero** (scaled multiplicatively so "Now" reads identically to the headline) with **both endpoints labelled** ("Now 19:24 → +12 wk 19:14"). Dropped the historical solid lead-in from this card (it conflated raw-trajectory and adjusted scales and added clutter); the standalone historical trend remains the no-plan fallback. SCIENCE_LOG §BA updated. `src/ui/triathlon/benchmark-charts.ts`, `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
- **Projection model fix — half/marathon projected getting *slower* and "fell off a cliff" (Tristan).** Root cause: the projection fed `applyTrainingHorizonAdjustment` **recent weekly km** as the dose. A thin-history user reads as near-zero volume → the model's `undertrain_penalty` (volume-gated, applied at full strength regardless of weeks) exceeded the gain → negative projection for half/marathon (high `min_sessions`), with a week-1 discontinuity (w=0 pinned to the hero, w=1 takes the full penalty). Fix: dose is now **plan-prescribed volume** (`getPlanPrescribedMeanWeeklyKm`, the same input the targeted forecast uses), and the gain is **floored at 0** ("holding the plan" is at minimum maintenance — never project a runner getting slower for training). Curve is now monotonic-improving for every user/distance, and gains are larger (also addresses "−7s, it sucks"). SCIENCE_LOG §BA. `src/calculations/blended-fitness.ts`.
- **Toggles no longer refresh the page (Tristan).** The Supershoes toggle and the 4/8/12-week selector called `renderStdDistanceDetail` (full app-root rebuild → scroll-to-top + flash). Refactored the detail body into `buildStdDetailInner` inside a `#stdd-content` container; both toggles now rebuild only that region with scroll preserved, so the chart's line/dot animations replay in place ("points move, like the swim CSS sparkline") without a page jump. `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`, `src/ui/triathlon/benchmark-charts.ts`.
- **Projection line now fills edge-to-edge (Tristan: "squished… doesn't fill LHS to RHS").** The chart's horizontal padding was inset too far, so the "Now" dot and line started well inside the card. Switched to asymmetric padding — `PAD_L 3` so the curve starts at the left edge, `PAD_R 14` for just enough room for the glowing end marker + halo (the card clips overflow). Matches the marathon-population-card reference. `src/ui/triathlon/benchmark-charts.ts`.
- **Projection chart switched to the canonical sparkline renderer (Tristan: pointed at the swim/CSS "Trend" card — "these move and I like these").** The bespoke liquid-glass/dashed chart kept fighting the edge-to-edge fill, so `buildForecastTrajectoryChart` now defers entirely to `buildBenchmarkTrendChart` (the same full-width area-fill + solid-line sparkline as the CSS/LT trends), in a plain white card, drawing in via `animateChartDrawOn` on load and on every horizon/shoe change. The projected series is still scaled onto the adjusted hero and time-formatted (headline "{projected} in N wk", delta "−Xs in N weeks"); x-axis is weekly synthetic dates so the fill spans full width. `src/ui/triathlon/benchmark-charts.ts`, `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
- **Projection draw animation fixed + curve shape corrected (Tristan: "line jumps and doesn't finish… are these shapes normal?").** (a) The draw stalled/snapped on the `preserveAspectRatio="none"` + `non-scaling-stroke` chart — both `getTotalLength()` (shared `animateChartDrawOn`) and a `pathLength="1"` stroke-dashoffset draw misbehaved (one snapped, the other stuck mid-line). Dropped stroke-based drawing entirely; the chart now reveals with a pure-CSS **`clip-path` left-to-right wipe** (`.std-proj-wipe`, ~1.05s) that runs on insert and re-runs on every horizon/shoe rebuild — bulletproof regardless of SVG stretch, no JS. (b) The dead-flat-then-kink shape was an artifact: sampling the horizon model per week and flooring each at 0 let the constant undertrain penalty pin early weeks flat. Now the total gain is computed once at the horizon (floored ≥0 = volume-appropriate ceiling) and distributed across weeks by the model's own `week_factor` saturation, giving the physiologically correct concave rise from week 1 (Hickson 1981; Joyner & Coyle 2008). Under-volume lowers the ceiling, not the onset (Pfitzinger/Daniels), so a low-volume plan still projects honestly — smaller gain, same shape. SCIENCE_LOG §BA updated; new test for the rises-from-week-1 shape (now 23). `src/calculations/blended-fitness.ts`, `src/ui/race-forecast-view.ts`.
