## 2026-06-01 — Manual VO2max / LT overrides now flow through to race predictions

- **Bug (user-reported)**: manually changing VO2max on the stats view did not move any race-time projection. Same for a manual LT override. Two independent breaks, both fixed.
- **Break 1 — VO2 override never reached the blend.** Every `blendPredictions` call read `s.vo2` directly, which holds only the *device* VO2max; the manual override lives in `s.vo2Override` (resolved at tier 0 by `getPhysiologicalVdot`) and was silently missed. Added `effectiveVo2max(s)` in `physiological-vdot.ts` (override → device → null; deliberately no HR/mosaic fallthrough to avoid double-counting other blend slots) and routed the running prediction call sites through it: `blended-fitness.ts` ×2 (`predictStandardDistances`, `refreshBlendedFitness`), `stats-view.ts` race-estimate table, `session-generator.ts` time-trial. Behaviour is unchanged when no override is set (`effectiveVo2max` = `s.vo2` then), so blast radius is override-only.
- **Break 2 — overrides never recomputed the cached prediction.** The VO2 override handler (`triathlon/benchmark-detail-pages.ts`) and the LT override handlers (`stats-view.ts`: save / reset / conflict-pick) updated state but never called `refreshBlendedFitness`, so the cached `s.forecastTime` / `s.blendedRaceTimeSec` that the home card, forecast hero and stats table read stayed stale until next launch. Added a `refreshBlendedFitness(m)` call after each. (The new no-race standard-distance view already recomputed live on render, so it only needed Break 1.)
- LT input was already correct (`recomputeLT` updates `s.lt`, which the blend reads directly) — LT just needed the recompute (Break 2).
- 2 new tests in `blended-fitness.test.ts` prove a higher `vo2Override` yields a faster prediction at every distance, and that the override beats a stale device `s.vo2`. **Full suite: 2687 pass, 0 fail.** **NOT device-verified.**
- **Cross-mode (Mirror rule) audit + triathlon parity fix.** Checked all modes: **Cycling** is FTP-driven and doesn't consume VO2/LT (N/A by design). **HYROX** run pace reads `s.lt` + VDOT and recomputes live, so LT flows (VO2 only indirectly — HYROX doesn't read VO2 directly). **Triathlon** had the identical running bug: `race-prediction.triathlon.ts:1293` passed `state.vo2` (now `effectiveVo2max(state)`), and the VO2 override handler didn't invalidate the cached `triConfig.prediction` the way the CSS/FTP handlers do (now cleared in the save + reset handlers). So a manual VO2max override now moves the triathlon run-leg prediction too. Full suite still 2687 pass.
- **Deferred**: the earlier-approved "fall back to VDOT-as-VO2 when no device VO2max" (align forecast path to the time-trial's `?? vdot`) was NOT bundled here — broader calibration shift, revisit separately. Also deferred: an LT-override entry point in triathlon mode (LT override is running-stats-only today; a tri-set LT would need its own `triConfig.prediction` invalidation).

## 2026-06-01 — Onboarding: "Do you have a goal time?" on the plan-ready screen (Monte Carlo)

- **What**: a user-initiated goal-time entry on the running plan-ready screen (`plan-preview-v2.ts`). A quiet bordered "Do you have a goal time?" button opens an overlay with two interacting controls — a goal-time slider and an "Add quality sessions" stepper — both re-running the existing Monte Carlo (`runMarathonForecastSim`) live. The predicted finish and the **chance of hitting the goal** slide in real time as the user drags the goal or adds sessions. Reuses the chance ladder (`liveTone`/`liveLabel`, now exported from `goal-time-overlay.ts`) and `fmtProbPct`.
- **Saving** persists `s.raceGoalTimeSec` (the canonical running goal field, so it carries straight through to the post-onboarding Race Forecast page) and reframes the hero: "TARGET TIME" + goal + "X% chance · Honest stretch" + "On current plan {forecast}". Honest-% even when the goal is a stretch; the prediction is always shown alongside.
- **Added sessions are now REAL, not cosmetic.** The plan is built before this screen and only regenerates through `initializeSimulator`. New shared `bumpSessionsAndRegen()` bumps the onboarding record's `runsPerWeek` (capped at 7) and re-runs `initializeSimulator` so the prescribed weeks actually gain the session. The pre-existing auto "MILESTONE NEARBY → Target it" handler was routed through the same helper — it had been bumping `s.rw`/`s.epw` only, which never reached the generated plan.
- **Coherence**: the headline `forecastTime` is now seeded onto `s.forecastTime`/`s.forecastTimeAdjusted` during the plan-ready render so the goal Monte Carlo anchors its cone to the same number the hero shows (previously it had no anchor at onboarding and drifted to a bare-VDOT trajectory). Single shared `forecastForSessions()` feeds the hero, the milestone feasibility check, and the overlay so the numbers can't diverge.
- **Coexistence** (Tristan's call): the automatic milestone popup keeps firing as before; the manual button is the always-available path for an arbitrary goal.

- **Fixed two Monte Carlo cone bugs this surfaced (`race-forecast-simulation.ts`).** (a) For an athlete whose PBs outpace their synced-run VDOT, the cone sloped the *wrong way* — headline 17:55 but simulated median 19:37, predicting regression over the block and collapsing the goal probability to "<5%", because today's anchor was `blendedRaceTimeSec` (PB-fast) while race-day read a stale `forecastTime` (VDOT-slow). (b) After a first fix that recomputed race-day from the blend, the cone landed ~2.5 min *slower* than the displayed forecast (the recompute omitted the calibration/shoe/course adjustments the headline bakes in), so a goal set equal to the forecast read ~32% instead of ~50%. **Final fix**: anchor the cone to the forecast the UI actually displays (`forecastTimeAdjusted ?? forecastTime`), with the blend-derived value (`blendedRaceTimeSec − horizonDelta`, course ratio applied) as a fallback *only* when the stored forecast is missing or slower than today. Now goal == forecast reads 50% (marathon 3:24:22 median on a 3:24:22 headline), a 5-min-faster goal reads 20%, and the PB-divergent state reads ~86% (was <5%). (c) Anchoring to the stored forecast then broke the overlay's "add a session" preview — the forecast caption moved but the chance didn't (sim still pinned to the base forecast). Added an optional `forecastOverrideSec` param so a what-if scenario centres the cone on the forecast computed for that session count: +0/+1/+2 sessions now reads forecast 3:24:22/3:22:19/3:20:46 and chance 24%/37%/46% for a 3:20:00 goal. 6 regression tests in `race-forecast-simulation.test.ts`. SCIENCE_LOG §AV.
- **Distance-aware goal slider** (`deriveBounds` in `goal-time-overlay.ts`, now shared with the onboarding overlay). The old bounds used a marathon-era "min 30-min span" floor, so a 17-min 5K slider spanned 15:00–45:00 and one 60s step leapt the probability 85%→11%. Now per-distance step + window (5K 5s/±10%, 10K 10s/±10%, half 20s/±12%, marathon 30s/±12%) → ~40–50 explorable notches per race. The onboarding overlay also passes an optional `fastestSec` (the forecast at max addable sessions, cap 7 runs) so the fast end of the slider covers the whole add-session span from the start — adding sessions never runs the goal off the end of the range, and the bounds are fixed at open time so they don't shift under the user.
- `tsc --noEmit` + `lint:ui` clean, 2630 tests pass. **NOT device-verified.**

## 2026-06-01 — On-demand mode: rename + multi-discipline session generation

- **Why**: "Just track" undersold the mode. Reframed as **"On demand"** for athletes who want to train but have no event on the calendar, and opened it up so they can actually generate sessions in every discipline we support, not just log activity.
- **Rename** (user-facing only; internal `trackOnly` flag unchanged): mode tile `goals.ts` and focus option `race-target.ts` → **"On demand"**, sub-copy reframed to "no race on the calendar / generate sessions when you want them".
- **Capability correction**: an initial read assumed bike/swim needed FTP/CSS and gym wasn't generatable for a no-plan user. Wrong — `generateBikeSession`/`generateSwimSession` take **optional** `ftp?`/`cssSecPer100m?` (degrade to RPE/duration), and `generateGymWorkouts` needs neither. All four disciplines work for On-demand. The gap was purely UI gating (`isTri`), not the generators.
- **Session generator** (`session-generator.ts`): On-demand "Pick your own" now opens the **discipline picker** (Run / Bike / Swim / Gym). The `isTri` gates generalised to `hasDisciplinePicker = isTri || isOnDemand`; Run/Bike/Swim reuse the exact tri renderers. New: `renderBenchmarkPrompt` (optional, skippable FTP/CSS capture before bike/swim when none set — stores a `'user'`-sourced value on `triConfig`, which `eventType` gating keeps from leaking into tri UI) and `renderGymSession` (single screen via `generateGymWorkouts`, injury-aware → rehab message when strength is paused). `saveTriAdhoc` forks: On-demand sessions land in `adhocWorkouts` + main view (single store), tri stays `triWorkouts` + tri plan view.
- **On-demand home** (`home-view.ts → getTrackOnlyHomeHTML`): prominent whole-card **"Generate a session"** CTA at the top, naming run/bike/swim/gym. Hero subcopy "Tracking only." → "Sessions on demand." Header pill "Tracking" → "On demand". No accent fill (in-page action, per colour rules).

## 2026-06-01 — Forecast-factor direction audit (after the heat bug, "are the others working?")

- **Why**: the heat bug had two failure modes — wrong sign, and double-counting the empirical venue factor. Tristan asked whether other forecast factors hide the same class of bug.
- **Directional coverage was the blind spot**: the heat sign error survived because there was *no* heat directional test. Audited every factor for an existing direction guard; five that move the predicted time had **zero**: per-leg calibration bias, open-water adaptation, brick adaptation, IM marathon-depth credit, and empirical course factors. Added one isolating test each (perturb one input, hold volume/co-location constant, assert the leg moves the right way) in `race-prediction.triathlon.test.ts`. **All five pass** — they fire in the correct direction. No new sign bugs found.
- **Structural double-count finding (the reassuring part)**: traced every adjustment applied *on top of* the venue course-factor. Heat was the **only** one that overlapped what the empirical venue number already contains (race-day weather), which is why it double-counted. Every other on-top adjustment — durability cap, race-readiness penalty, calibration bias, horizon projection, open-water, brick, marathon-depth — is **athlete-specific** (describes the athlete, not the venue), so it structurally cannot double-count the calibrated venue factor. The heat bug was a one-off, not a pattern.
- **Noted, not a bug**: the durability cap and the readiness penalty both respond to low training volume (longest-session vs weekly-volume). They stack for a severely undertrained athlete, but each is bounded (durability +5%, readiness ≤15% IM) and they measure different things, so the overlap is intentional.
- **Files**: `src/calculations/race-prediction.triathlon.test.ts` (new direction block + the heat-symmetry block). Full suite 2576 pass.

## 2026-06-01 — HYROX now adapts to execution (RPE-driven load multiplier) (P2)

- `plan_engine.hyrox.ts` was purely phase-driven — crush a week or bomb it, next week was identical. New `hyroxEffortMultiplier` (`effort-multiplier.hyrox.ts`) reads trailing RPE-vs-expected across **all** HYROX sessions (stations + bricks + runs) and scales the weekly hours budget: `effectiveHours = hours × phaseMult × deload × effortMult`. Same formula/bounds as running and tri (`1 − score × 0.05`, clamped [0.85, 1.15]), same under-duration guard. Reuses existing lookback + bounds constants; none invented.
- **Why volume is the right lever for HYROX**: race implements are fixed at division weight, so progression is work-capacity (rounds/reps/density) at that weight, not added load. Scaling the hours budget scales rounds — the actual HYROX lever. (D5b resolved: yes, HYROX should adapt.)
- **RPE-primary, by necessity.** A data map confirmed the objective station signal doesn't exist for synced activities (Strava/Garmin give only "station session" + total time, no per-station reps/times) and would need a structured target-capture refactor for guided sessions. RPE is the only signal on every session. An objective 60/40 blend (D4/D5) is a deferred, guided-only enhancement. HR rejected for stations (lags intermittent work, no per-station target IF).
- Scoped to weeks ≥ current (past weeks keep real load); non-compounding (regen rebuilds baseline first). Mirrors tri's future-week scoping.
- **Surfaced inline** (same day): a muted note on the HYROX plan-view current-week summary fires when the shift is ≥5% ("Load raised/eased N% this week after recent sessions were rated easier/harder than planned"), per the adaptation-transparency rule. HYROX has no week-debrief, so an inline caption hosts it (UI pre-flight done; mirrors the existing "Hours per discipline" caption; 0 non-neutral colours; lint:ui green). Science: `SCIENCE_LOG §AU`. Tests: effort-multiplier.hyrox.test.ts (11). tsc clean, full suite passing. NOT device-verified.

## 2026-06-01 — Post-holiday return parity for tri / cycling / HYROX + holiday detraining (P1)

- **Comeback bridge for all modes.** Returning from a holiday, tri/cycling/HYROX athletes used to get their full week-N prescription on day one (the exact ACWR spike running's bridge prevents). New `applyBridgeModsAllDisciplines` (holiday-modal.ts) scales swim/bike/run-leg/station volume (`estimatedDurationMin` + `musculoTendonLoad`) and run km on the 1–3 comeback weeks, reading the same `_holidayBridgeScale` running uses. Wired into the tri + HYROX plan-view render paths. Reuses running's existing 0.50–0.85 scale constants; none invented.
- **FTP / CSS / VDOT detraining on holiday return.** Previously FTP/CSS never detrained (a cyclist returned from 2 weeks off with unchanged FTP). New shared `detrainingLossFraction(daysAway, retentionRatio)` curve (welcome-back.ts) drives all three: ~1.2%/wk (wks 1–2) / 0.8%/wk after (Mujika & Padilla 2000), with a **10-day dead-zone** (a normal week off is a taper, costs nothing) and **activity-while-away attenuation** (kept training → detrain less). `computeVdotLoss` now delegates to it, fixing the old `ceil`-weeks over-dock where a 3-day trip lost 1.2% VDOT.
- **Holiday-only, never while following the plan** (Tristan's call): detraining keys off a declared break (a real load drop), not effort-age — so a compliant athlete doing prescribed endurance never sees a benchmark silently fall.
- **Anchor-gate** (`ftpDetrainAnchorISO` / `cssDetrainAnchorISO`, optional state): the launch refresh will not restore a docked FTP/CSS from a *pre-holiday* effort — only a ride/swim after the return proves recovery and clears the anchor. Stops the dock being clobbered on the next launch.
- **Mode-aware welcome-back copy:** the modal no longer promises running-only behaviour to tri/HYROX; the detraining summary names only the markers that actually moved (HYROX never claims an FTP change).
- Science in `docs/SCIENCE_LOG.md §AS`. Tests: welcome-back.test.ts (+5), illness-holiday-disciplines.test.ts (+5). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, full suite 2593 passing, `npm run lint:ui` green. Docks + anchor-gate + bridge are integration-level — **NOT device-verified**. Decisions: D1 (render-time bridge), D2 (reuse VDOT shape), dead-zone 10d, D3 (stations/MTL don't detrain), activity-scaling — all per `CROSS_MODE_PARITY_PLAN.md`.

## 2026-06-01 — Heat acclimatisation: made symmetric (penalty for training cooler than the race, not just zero credit)

- **Found via the leg waterfall (Tristan)**: the Ohio run showed a −40s "Heat acclimatisation credit" off a 14°C training temp for a 24°C race. Investigating surfaced three problems, fixed in two passes.
- **First pass (superseded)**: stopped crediting cooler-than-race training and gated the term to the physical-course path. Tristan then pushed back with the science — racing *hotter* than you train is a real *penalty*, not just the absence of a credit.
- **Final model — symmetric, both paths**: the climate penalty (+4% warm etc.) is the average field; the athlete's own heat preparation shifts their exposure to it. Pivot at race temp: train hotter → credit (better adapted than field), at race temp → no adjustment, train cooler → **penalty** (under-adapted). `acclimFraction = clamp(tempGap/30, −0.5, +0.5)`, magnitude ±50% of the climate penalty at ±15°C. Science: Périard/Racinais/Sawka 2015 + Racinais 2015 consensus (acclimatised-vs-unacclimatised gap is ~symmetric, ~4–7%); Ely 2007 (under-prepared runners slow more than the field).
- **Both paths without double-counting**: because the adjustment is zero at race temp, it adds only the athlete's *personal deviation* from the field, not the absolute weather — so it's safe on empirical venues (Ohio) where field weather is already baked into the calibrated factor.
- **Net effect for Ohio**: the phantom −40s credit becomes a small *penalty* — Tristan trained ~10°C cooler than the Ohio race, so the run gets slightly slower, as an earned, labelled "Heat: trained cooler than race" step ("Trained ~14°C vs 24°C race"). The 14°C is real: `computeTrainingTempC` averages `ambientTempC` from the last 4 weeks of synced activities (≥4 readings).
- **Mirror Rule**: the running predictor (`course-factors-running.ts`) had the same credit-only logic — made symmetric to match.
- **Copy**: the Venue card's "vs flat, cool, sea level" baseline now reads "vs an ideal flat, cool, sea-level course (not this venue)" so it isn't mistaken for a description of the venue.
- **Files**: `src/calculations/race-prediction.triathlon.ts`, `src/calculations/course-factors-running.ts`, `src/ui/triathlon/forecast-chip-detail-view.ts`. SCIENCE_LOG §T4 + running heat section revised. 4 heat-direction tests (cooler→penalty, hotter→credit, race-temp→neutral, cool-race→none); full suite 2571 pass.

## 2026-06-01 — Workout Adjust: persistence fix + all-modes (tri / cycling / HYROX)

- **Bug (Tristan, reproducible)**: adjusting a run from 40 min → 20 min stuck for the session, then **reverted to 40 min on reload**. The user's ask: "make this actually work for all modes."
- **Root cause (verified, not the handoff's guess)**: running workouts are regenerated every render; the Adjust change persists as a `WorkoutMod` re-attached by matching `(name, dayOfWeek)`. But run names collide ("Easy Run" ×N) and `assignDefaultDays` reshuffles `dayOfWeek` whenever the week's set changes between sessions (a session completes, trailing-effort shifts the plan, deload fires). When the day moves, the mod no longer finds its run and the change evaporates. The handoff hypothesised `generateWeekWorkouts` never sets `estimatedDurationMin`; a reproduction test disproved that — `intentToWorkout` sets it on every slot and the standard case persists. The real fragility is the match key.
- **Fix (running)**: match user-scale mods by the **stable slot id** (`W{week}-{type}-{idx}`, already on the Adjust button as `data-workout-id`) first, falling back to name+day for legacy mods or when the id genuinely changed. New `WorkoutMod.workoutId` field; the matching is now one shared, tested helper `findWorkoutForMod` in `workout-scaling.ts`, used at all three render-time re-application sites (`computeRenderedWorkouts`, the today card, the km-nudge recompute) so they can't drift.
- **Fix (all modes)**: the Adjust control now exists in triathlon, cycling, and HYROX. Tri/cycling/HYROX sessions live as persisted objects in `wk.triWorkouts` (not regenerated), so the scale is written **straight onto the stored object** in place — the same reload-safe mutation the drag-to-reorder handlers use, no match key needed. `openWorkoutAdjust` gained `AdjustOptions { persist:'mod'|'object', workoutId, allowIntensity, store, rerender }`. The Easier/Harder **intensity ladder is gated to running only** (it is built on running pace types with no defined mapping for swim / bike / stations); tri/cycling/HYROX get duration scaling only. HYROX exposes Adjust on run + cross (bike/erg/swim) sessions; station / brick / strength are round/rep-structured and deferred. Entry points: an "Adjust" button in the tri detail modal and an inline "Adjust" in the HYROX detail modal, each with an "Adjusted for this session. Planned X min." caption when scaled.
- **Minimum**: kept the existing 50 % relative floor (`DURATION_SCALE_MIN`, sourced from the taper long-run multiplier). No new constant (Tristan).
- 5 new helper tests (`workout-scaling.test.ts`, 19 total) covering reshuffle-survival, name-collision, legacy-fallback, id-gone-fallback, and no-match. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, full suite 2570 passing, `npm run lint:ui` green. **Running device-verified by Tristan 2026-06-01** (the 40→20 run now sticks). Gym harder/easier/longer/shorter is a separate Phase 2 (needs a sets/reps/load model).
- **Follow-up (Tristan, same day)**: injury-generated cross-training (the bike/erg/swim aerobic substitute from the capability nudge) couldn't be adjusted in tri/HYROX. Those sessions live in `wk.adhocWorkouts`, not `wk.triWorkouts`, but the detail-modal Adjust wiring hardcoded `store:'triWorkouts'`, so `findStored` missed them and the adjust silently no-oped. `findStored` now searches both arrays (hinted store first), so accepted-offer / adhoc sessions are adjustable too. Running was unaffected (its cross sessions carry `t:'cross_training'`, which the run-type checks treat as a run, so they already showed Adjust and persisted via the mod path).
- **Copy fix (Tristan, screenshot)**: the aerobic-substitute description read "Holds your aerobic engine while your **other** recovers, with no impact on it." — `inj.location` fell back to the literal `'other'` when no specific body part was set. New `recoveryClause(inj)` (`capability-substitution.ts`) emits "while your knee recovers" for a real location and "while you recover" otherwise; the tail is now "without loading the injury" (reads correctly in both cases). 14 capability tests still green.
- **Harder/Easier for bike & swim (Tristan)**: the Adjust intensity control was running-only (its ladder is running pace types). Bike and swim object-mode sessions now get a discipline-aware Harder/Easier that steps a **sourced** intensity ladder — bike by %FTP (`BIKE_INTENSITY_LADDER`: endurance 0.65 → tempo 0.82 → sweet-spot 0.91 → threshold 1.00 → VO2 1.15, Coggan & Allen 2019), swim by sec/100m offset from CSS (`SWIM_INTENSITY_LADDER`: technique +18 → endurance +6 → CSS 0 → speed −6). Both mirror the `pct`/`cssOffsetSec` values already in `session-generator.ts`'s pickers (canonical copy now lives in `triathlon-constants.ts`). The overlay shows the live target ("Tempo · 180–210W" / "CSS intervals · 1:38/100m"), recomputed from the athlete's current FTP/CSS so it tracks benchmark improvements; the tri/HYROX detail modals show the same "Target:" line. Chosen rung persists as `Workout.intensityLevel`; nothing is baked into the description (so duration scaling stays clean) and **no new constants were invented** — the watt band reuses `BIKE_ADHERENCE_BAND`. Per Tristan, injury aerobic-maintenance sessions are **allowed to go harder** too (athlete's call over the prescription). No RPE is fabricated — the watt/pace target is the prescription (matches the bike "power is the primary signal" rule). 7 new tests (`intensity-ladder.test.ts`). tsc clean, suite 2583 passing, lint green. Not yet device-verified.
- **Session-action consistency across modes (Tristan)**: running cards expand inline with a clean Mark as Done · Adjust · Skip row, while tri/HYROX opened a modal with a different, inconsistent button set. Decision (Tristan): match the action row everywhere, keep each layout. Tri and HYROX detail modals now show the same **Mark as Done · Adjust · Skip** row (Adjust renamed from "Adjust duration"); tri/HYROX "Mark as Done"/"Skip" write the shared `wk.rated` map (rpe number / `'skip'`) that the running card already writes and the shared status chip reads — a lightweight manual completion flag (effort/adherence still derive from a matched activity when one arrives). HYROX keeps its guided Start + Mark-as-done flow for station/brick/strength (set-by-set); only the time-defined run/bike/erg/swim sessions get the action row. **"Move to day" removed** from the running card (Tristan — drag-and-drop reorder already covers it and the Mon–Sun picker cluttered every expanded card). ## 2026-06-01 — HYROX + triathlon now honour illness and holiday (parity with running)

- **Trigger (Tristan)**: heard from another agent that HYROX lacks holiday/illness/injury logic. Audit verdict: injury already works on HYROX (regen-on-save + discipline capacity gates). Illness and holiday did **not** — and the gap was not HYROX-specific: render-time illness/holiday workout suppression lived **only** in running's `plan-view.ts`. Triathlon had the same gap. Both modes showed the banner (home-view is mode-agnostic) but left the underlying plan workouts at full prescription.
- **Root cause**: the legacy `applyIllnessMods`/`applyHolidayMods` helpers skip everything in `NON_RUN_TYPES` (swim, bike, row, strength, …), so even if they had been called on tri/HYROX they would only ever touch the run legs and silently ignore stations, bricks, swims, and bike legs.
- **Fix — discipline-aware helpers (reuse existing ratios, no new constants)**:
  - `applyIllnessModsAllDisciplines(workouts, severity)` in `illness-rules.ts` — classifies each workout via the existing `classifyWorkoutKind` (`hyrox_station/brick/assessment` → strength; bike/swim/run) and applies the same severity tiers across all disciplines. `resting` rests every sport session; `light` scales volume to 0.6 and caps intensity to easy. Crucially it scales the numeric `estimatedDurationMin` and `musculoTendonLoad` fields (not just the `d` string `scaleAndCap` rewrites), because the HYROX/tri cards render from those fields.
  - `applyHolidayModsAllDisciplines(workouts, canRun, holidayDays, canSwim)` in `holiday-modal.ts` — **facility-access model (Tristan)**, not a blanket reduction: running is the holiday-safe spine and honours `canRun` (no/maybe/yes → rest / optional / keep easy, quality downgraded). **Bike always rests** — you don't travel with a bike or a trainer. **HYROX stations + bricks always rest** — a hotel gym isn't a HYROX box (no sled, ski-erg, wall balls), and a brick's station half is unavailable. **Swim is conditional on `canSwim`**, a new question asked only of triathletes: pool/open water → easy reduced swim; none → rest. Reuses the running 0.7 ratio, no new constants.
  - **Holiday questionnaire**: triathletes now get a "Will you have a pool or open water?" step (`renderStepSwim`), which also notes bike sessions pause. Running and HYROX skip it. `holidayState.canSwim?: boolean` added (optional, no migration).
- **Wired in**: `src/ui/hyrox/plan-view.ts` and `src/ui/triathlon/plan-view.ts` (both render entry points — main render + `buildTriDayList`, via a shared `applyTriRenderMods`) now apply illness (current week) + holiday (week-in-holiday) exactly as running does. Render-time only, not persisted.
- **Holiday deload parity (engine)**: `plan_engine.hyrox.ts` and `plan_engine.triathlon.ts` now read `wk.forceDeload` and OR it into their deload computation (`deload = forceDeload || isDeloadWeek(...)`), matching running's `plan_engine.ts:331`. Previously the holiday modal set `forceDeload` on overlapping weeks but the tri/HYROX engines ignored it and regenerated at full load.
- **Files**: `src/calculations/illness-rules.ts`, `src/ui/holiday-modal.ts`, `src/ui/hyrox/plan-view.ts`, `src/ui/triathlon/plan-view.ts`, `src/workouts/plan_engine.hyrox.ts`, `src/workouts/plan_engine.triathlon.ts`, `src/types/state.ts`, new `src/calculations/illness-holiday-disciplines.test.ts` (11 tests). ## 2026-06-01 — Top overscroll bounce on web + swipe between tabs (pending device/web confirmation)

- **Ask (Tristan)**: every page should bounce when you scroll up to the very top (web felt like a "dead wall"), and users should be able to swipe between pages.
- **Bounce** (`src/ui/web-overscroll-bounce.ts`, wired once in `main.ts` bootstrap): web-only spring; no-op on iOS native, which already rubber-bands the document. Pulling up at `scrollY === 0` translates the page's in-flow content down with Apple's documented UIScrollView rubber-band curve (constant `0.55`), capped at `MAX_BOUNCE_PX = 130`, then springs back. Trackpad/wheel uses a per-frame decay so the momentum tail eases back instead of being held then snapped (fixed a "sag at the bottom" report). Crucially, it translates the content *inside* each `min-height:100vh` page wrapper, not the wrapper itself, so the atmosphere gradient stays pinned and the gap revealed at the top shows the sky end of the gradient (fixed a "goes white at the top" report). Skips bouncing when an overlay is open (gesture target outside `#app-root`).
- **Swipe** (`src/ui/page-swipe-nav.ts`, wired in bootstrap): horizontal flick navigates the adjacent main tab (`home → plan → forecast → stats`, no wrap). Flick-to-slide, lightweight: the outgoing `#app-root` is repositioned as a fixed overlay and slides off in the flick direction while the next page renders beneath it (only the always-present outgoing layer animates, robust to the per-tab async import). Bails on vertical-dominant gestures, horizontal scrollers, draggable workout cards (running/tri/hyrox), and open overlays. New tab-bar exports: `navigateToTab`, `getActiveTab`, `SWIPE_TAB_ORDER`.
- **Plan week-swipe retired**: the per-week touch swipe in `plan-view.ts` was removed so it no longer double-fires against the global tab swipe. Weeks still change via the chevron buttons (`#plan-week-prev`/`#plan-week-next`) and the numbered week pills.
- **Bounce iterations**: (1) momentum "sag at the bottom" → 130px cap + per-frame wheel decay; (2) "white at the top" on gradient pages → translate content inside the wrapper, not the wrapper, so the gradient stays pinned; (3) white only when flinging from the bottom all the way to the top → touch eligibility was locked at touchstart (mid-page = bailed, native overscroll showed white), now we anchor when the scroll reaches the top mid-gesture, and `overscroll-behavior: none` is set on both `html` and `body` so any momentum fling we can't intercept stops cleanly instead of flashing white.
- **Status**: not yet confirmed on device or in the browser by Tristan; iterated three times on bounce feel. Files: `src/ui/web-overscroll-bounce.ts`, `src/ui/page-swipe-nav.ts`, `src/ui/tab-bar.ts`, `src/main.ts`, `src/ui/plan-view.ts`.

## 2026-06-01 — Fix: absurd bike weight made the bike prediction faster + CdA explainer on the calibration card

- **Problem (Tristan, stress-testing)**: setting bike weight to 100 kg made the predicted bike split *faster*. Also, the CdA number had no in-place explanation on the calibration card for users who don't know the term.
- **Root cause (weight)**: when CdA is calibrated from a ride, mass and CdA are coupled in the inversion (`bike-physics.ts:solveCdA`). A higher mass makes the solver attribute more power to rolling/climbing, leaving less for aero, so it computes a *lower* CdA. The prediction reuses that artificially-low CdA, and on a flat course the aero term (∝ v³) dominates the rolling penalty, so the net result is faster. HTML `min`/`max` on the weight inputs don't actually clamp typed values, so the absurd 100 kg got through.
- **Fix (weight)**: clamp rider (30–200 kg) and bike (4–30 kg) weight to their already-declared input bounds in both the on-change handler and the save sweep (`bike-setup-view.ts`). Out-of-range typed values are now corrected in the field and never reach the calibration. Wizard path was already guarded (out-of-range → `undefined` → default).
- **Fix (CdA explainer)**: added the existing `infoButton` "i" toggle to the "Estimated CdA from a recent flat ride" card, revealing an inline explainer. Extracted the explainer copy to a single `CDA_EXPLAINER` constant reused by both the riding-position caption and the calibration card so the two can't drift.
- **Files**: `src/ui/triathlon/bike-setup-view.ts`, `src/ui/triathlon/bike-setup-preview.test.ts`. Science note added (mass / CdA coupling limitation).

## 2026-06-01 — Fix: triathlon Forecast fingerprint wrongly showed "Needs markers" for Transitions / Endurance / Durability

- **Problem (Tristan)**: the triathlon Forecast fingerprint card showed Transitions as "Needs markers" (and Endurance / Durability as "Pending · Needs markers"), yet tapping into Transitions showed a live estimate (~5:54). Nothing was logged — this was the prediction, and transitions never need user markers (they come from the empirical distribution / slider defaults in the engine).
- **Root cause**: the card and its drill-down read the prediction from two different sources. The fingerprint got `tri.prediction ?? null` (`forecast-view.ts:115`); when `triConfig.prediction` was not yet stored, every prediction-derived chip blanked. The drill-down and the transitions overlay both fall back to `predictTriathlonRace(s)` (`forecast-chip-detail-view.ts:1202`, `forecast-view.ts:153`), so they showed a real estimate. Classic two-numbers-from-different-sources divergence.

## 2026-06-01 — Fix: planStartDate drift (anchor later than first activity) shifted every week by one

- **Problem (Tristan, triathlon)**: the plan calendar was off by a week. Week 4 showed activities from 18–31 May (two calendar weeks) and the first logged activity (27 Apr) sat in "week 1", yet `planStartDate` was `2026-05-04`. Diagnosed live: every week's stored activities aligned to an **April-27** anchor, but `planStartDate` had drifted to May 4, so the user was shown as week 5 when really in week 6, and `weekIndexForDate` filed activities a week late.
- **Root cause**: `derivePlanStartDate` (`persistence.ts`) sets the anchor from the earliest activity known *at the time*, but only runs when the anchor is absent. When an earlier activity arrives later (history backfill, late Strava/Garmin sync), the anchor is never re-derived and ends up **after** the first activity, which is impossible (week 1 cannot start after your first session) and never self-corrects.
- **Fix — anchor invariant guard**: new `reconcilePlanAnchorToEarliestActivity()` in `welcome-back.ts`, called on launch *before* `advanceWeekToToday` (`main.ts`). If the earliest logged activity (across `garminActuals`, `adhocWorkouts`, `garminPending`) predates `planStartDate`, it pulls the anchor back to that activity's Monday and bumps `s.w` by the same number of weeks. The `s.w` bump is load-bearing: without it, `advanceWeekToToday` would read the re-anchoring as N missed weeks and apply spurious VDOT detraining for training the user actually did. Fires only when the anchor is provably too late; a `planStartDate` that legitimately precedes the first activity (rested opening weeks) is untouched.
- **Tests**: 8 new cases in `welcome-back.test.ts` (16 total pass): the real Apr-27/May-4 incident, mid-week snap-to-Monday, adhoc/pending date sources, the `s.w` bump, and all no-op guards.
- **Known follow-up (Tristan's existing data)**: the anchor fix corrects the date labels and week number on reload, but already-stored activities still have week-edge **bleed** (week 4's bucket holds late-May sessions that belong to week 5) from the period the anchor was wrong. Leftover corruption, cleaned with a one-time re-bucket, not shipped code: fresh users with a correct anchor never accumulate it.
- **Verified**: `tsc --noEmit` clean for the changed files (one unrelated pre-existing error in `race-prediction.triathlon.ts` from concurrent WIP), `welcome-back.test.ts` green. **Not device-verified.**

## 2026-06-01 — Fix: triathlon week-debrief backdrop tap silently marked the week done

- **Problem (Tristan)**: "It's Monday and I'm not being prompted to complete a week." Diagnosed live from state: `planStartDate` was a correct Monday (2026-05-04), `s.w` had correctly advanced to week 5, and `lastDebriefWeek = 4` — the week-4 debrief was already recorded as complete, so `fireTriDebriefIfReady` (`tri-week-debrief.ts:49`) returned early. Nothing was wrong with week-anchoring.
- **Root cause**: the triathlon debrief recorded the week as debriefed on a **backdrop tap**. `showTriWeekDebrief` wired the overlay so a click on the dimmed area (`e.target.id === OVERLAY_ID`) called `_closeAndRecord`, writing `lastDebriefWeek`. A stray tap outside the modal card permanently consumed the week's wrap-up and suppressed the prompt. The explicit ✕ / cancel buttons only `.remove()` (no record), so the behaviour was inconsistent within the same modal.
- **Mirror-rule violation**: running's `week-debrief.ts` never records on a backdrop tap — only the explicit "Accept plan" / "Continue" buttons call `_closeAndRecord`. Triathlon now matches: backdrop tap only `.remove()`s the overlay; `lastDebriefWeek` is written solely by the "Accept plan" button (`tri-week-debrief.ts:500`).
- **Recovery for the affected state**: reset `lastDebriefWeek` to 3 and reload so the week-4 debrief re-fires through the normal launch path. (`__showTriDebrief(n)` dev helper also re-opens any week's debrief on demand.)
- **Verified**: `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Not device-verified** — wants a real iOS check that the backdrop tap dismisses without recording and the Monday prompt returns.

## 2026-06-01 — Plan reorder: long-press to drag on iOS + a one-line hint (all three plan views)

- **Problem (Tristan)**: scrolling the plan on iOS often grabbed a day-card by accident, because touch drag armed purely on distance (finger moves ≥8px in any direction). Scrolling and reordering are both vertical, so distance alone couldn't tell them apart.
- **Fix — long-press gate**: a drag now arms only after the finger rests for `TOUCH_DRAG_HOLD_MS` (350ms, Tristan's pick). Until the hold elapses, any real movement (≥8px) is treated as a scroll: the drag candidate is abandoned and the page scrolls normally (no `preventDefault`). After the hold, a small intentional move starts the drag. Timer is armed on `touchstart`, cancelled on scroll-detect and on `touchend`. Applied to all three touch DnD paths: running (`src/ui/plan-view.ts`), triathlon (`src/ui/triathlon/plan-view.ts`), HYROX (`src/ui/hyrox/plan-view.ts`). HTML5 (desktop mouse) drag is unchanged. The 350ms lives as a local `TOUCH_DRAG_HOLD_MS` const in each file (a UI-interaction timing, kept off the collision-prone shared files) with a cross-referencing comment.
- **Discoverability — reorder hint**: a tiny, muted, right-aligned caption ("Hold and drag to reorder") now sits above Monday on the current week only (`viewWeek === s.w`). Neutral `var(--c-faint)`, 10px, no icon, no accent, sentence case. Placed outside the re-rendered day-list container so a drag re-render doesn't wipe it. Past/future weeks omit it (reordering history/drafts isn't the point).
- **Verified**: `tsc --noEmit` and `lint:ui` clean for all three plan views; the running edit (collision-prone file) persisted, insurance patch at `/tmp/running-plan-view.before.patch`. **Not device-verified** — the hold feel and the scroll-vs-drag discrimination want a real iOS check.

## 2026-05-30 — Flow-through audit: every settable factor must move the predicted time (all modes)

- **Problem (Tristan)**: the bike-dropdown bug was emblematic of a wider class — change a setting, the number you're staring at doesn't move. Two distinct failure modes: (1) the control saves state but never recomputes/re-renders the cached prediction (plumbing), and (2) a factor is collected but genuinely has near-zero effect, so you can't tell a bug from physics.
- **Plumbing fixes shipped (no new science)**:
  - **Cycling IF/distance** (`race-prediction.cycling.ts`): intensity factor now interpolates from the *effective* race distance via `intensityForDistanceKm`, instead of being keyed by the stale onboarding distance bucket. Picking an event that overrides distance no longer leaves the effort fraction (and therefore race watts) wrong. Uses the existing `CYCLING_EVENT_INTENSITY_FACTOR` anchors as the single source of truth — no new constants.
  - **HR save** (`account-view.ts`): now recomputes per mode after save — running calls `refreshBlendedFitness` (HR-calibrated VDOT → forecast), triathlon/cycling invalidate `triConfig.prediction`. Previously an HR edit did nothing until the next app boot.
  - **Bike & aero from Account**: passes the `onSaved` refresh callback (completes the earlier Forecast-only fix so the modal works from both entry points).
  - **HYROX goal modal**: re-renders the forecast on save/clear so the target-delta chip updates immediately instead of staying stale under the modal.
- **CdA consistency** (`bike-setup-view.ts`): the position caption, the what-if table, and the headline forecast now all show the *same* CdA. Previously the caption led with the position preset (0.24) while the prediction silently used a calibrated value (0.48), and the what-if table forced presets for every row — three surfaces, three numbers. The caption now leads with the CdA actually in use (`cdaCaption`), and the what-if rows anchor on the calibrated/user CdA shifted by each position's published preset delta, so the active row equals the headline. This is the pure-bug half of the "is my 2:14 bike split genuine?" question: 2:14 was the optimistic preset number; the calibrated 0.48 says ~2:57. (Whether 0.48 itself is trustworthy is a separate calibration-bounds science item, pending.)
- **Running**: its interactive controls were already sound — HR (fixed above, mode-agnostic), carbon-shoes toggle (refreshes via `forecast-chip-detail-view`), runner-type change (`initializeSimulator` + reload), units (display-only). `btn-reset-vdot` is deferred-by-design (it tells the user the score updates with the next training data). `getEffectiveVdot` is computed live on every render, so `physioAdj`/pace-zone changes are picked up on the next view render. No running plumbing bug found.
- **Permanent guard** (`prediction-sensitivity.test.ts`, 20 tests): perturbs one factor at a time from a known-good baseline and asserts the predicted output moves (and, where physics dictates a sign, moves the right way). Triathlon (8): rider/bike weight, CdA/position, tyres, course, FTP, CSS. Cycling (6): shares the bike physics. Running (6): race distance, marathon PB, runner type, **carbon shoes (~0.97×)**, weekly volume. Locks the "I change a setting and nothing budges" class out of CI.
- **Verified**: 84/84 across the bike/tri/running prediction suites green; new test file is `tsc`-clean. Bike & CdA fixes verified in Chromium via Playwright earlier (TT→hoods moved finish 4:50:19 → 5:09:43 in-place, no tabbing). **WebKit/device confirmation still needed.**
- **Still pending Tristan's sign-off (won't invent)**: science for the genuinely-dead inputs (HYROX `athleteBias`, HYROX weekly-run-volume hardcoded 0, body-weight-on-run/HYROX-time) and the CdA plausibility bounds (current 0.15–0.50 accept range is too loose to reject a 0.48 on a TT bike). Plus an agent prompt for the missing post-onboarding controls (change race/date, edit PBs, skill sliders, cycling distance, HYROX format/run-pace).

## 2026-05-30 — Fix: race-forecast goal card was inert (tiles + edit-goal) — running and triathlon

- **Problem (Tristan)**: on the Forecast tab's "Race-time progression" card the interactive elements didn't behave. The three outcome tiles (Optimistic / Median / Conservative) did nothing, and "Edit goal time" did nothing. Intended behaviour: **tapping an outcome tile jumps the goal straight to that time** (one tap, no dialog); **"Edit goal time" / "Set a goal time"** open the editor overlay.
- **Two distinct bugs:**
  1. **Triathlon overlay never opened** (`triathlon/goal-time-overlay.ts`). Every entry point routes through `openTriGoalOverlay`, which read the predicted finish from the **stored** `tri.prediction?.totalSec` and returned early if missing/zero. The cone card always renders because `runTriForecastSim` recomputes via `predictTriathlonRace(s)`, so the card showed real numbers while the overlay's silent early-return killed edit-goal + set-goal. **Fix**: overlay now derives the predicted total from `predictTriathlonRace(ms)` (the card's source), falling back to the stored value. Satisfies "two numbers that mean the same thing come from the same source." Running's overlay was not affected — it and its sim both read the same canonical `forecastTimeAdjusted/forecastTime/blendedRaceTimeSec` fields.
  2. **Outcome tiles opened the overlay instead of setting the goal** — both modes. `wireTriConeCard` / `wireRunConeCard` called `open(preSec)` from the tiles. Now the tiles write the goal directly (`triConfig.targetFinishTimeSec` / `raceGoalTimeSec`), `saveState()`, and re-render so the goal line, chance %, and selected-tile highlight update. Edit-goal / set-goal still open the overlay.
- **Scope**: the tap-to-set outcome-tile pattern exists only in running (`ui/race-forecast-cone-card.ts`) and triathlon (`ui/triathlon/race-forecast-cone-card.ts`). HYROX sets its goal via a modal CTA (no outcome tiles); cycling-only mode uses `renderCyclingFinishCard` and has no cone card. No parity work needed there.
- **Verified**: my three edited files are `tsc`-clean and add zero new `lint:ui` violations. **Not yet device/in-app verified.** (The pre-existing `tsc` error in `activity-matcher.ts:1294` and the new `lint:ui` violation in `race-forecast-marquee.ts:56` are another agent's in-flight work, not from this change.)

## 2026-05-30 — Plan-card status flags reach triathlon and HYROX (done / logged / missed / today)

- **Problem (Tristan, with screenshots)**: running plan cards flag their state top-right (Logged/Done green, Missed orange, Today terracotta, Adjusted, Skipped, Replaced, Holiday, Added), but triathlon cards showed nothing and HYROX was unverified. A completed, missed, and upcoming session looked identical, so "what did I actually do this week" was unreadable on the tri/HYROX plan.
- **Shared helper**: extracted the status logic into `src/ui/workout-status.ts` — `computeWorkoutStatus` (pure label+colour cascade, mirrors running's precedence exactly), `deriveWorkoutStatus` (booleans from a workout + week object: matched activity → Logged, `status:'completed'`/positive rating → Done, past+undone → Missed, etc.), `computeWeekStatusContext` (today/past weekday math, local-midnight parse), and `renderWorkoutStatusChip`. Single source of truth so the modes can't drift.
- **Wired into tri + HYROX**: `triathlon/workout-card.ts` and `hyrox/workout-card.ts` gained an optional `statusChip` slot in the badge row; their plan-views (`renderDay`) build the chip per workout from the week context and pass it in. Future (draft) weeks render no chip; past weeks correctly flag undone sessions as Missed. The full vocabulary (incl. Replaced/Holiday) is supported so the parallel injury/replace-flow work surfaces automatically.
- **Follow-up fix — Saturday's session wrongly flagged "Missed"**: `computeWeekStatusContext` originally gated the current week on a `todayInRange` flag derived from `planStartDate`. When `planStartDate` was missing or unreadable, `todayInRange` went false and the *entire* current week was treated as past, so today's (and every later day's) undone sessions read "Missed". Replaced `todayInRange` with `weekEnded`: current-week today/past is now driven by the weekday alone (`isToday = isCurrentWeek && !weekEnded && dow === actualToday`; `isPast` for current week only when `weekEnded` or `dow < actualToday`). `planStartDate` can mark a week past only when it proves the week's last calendar day has elapsed (`weekEnded = now > wkEnd`); a missing date stays false instead of poisoning the whole week.
- **Running left untouched**: its inline status logic is byte-identical to the new helper and the file was being edited by a concurrent agent, so refactoring it was deferred to avoid collision. Behaviour matches across all three modes regardless. (If running also shows the Saturday-Missed bug, that's a separate fix in `plan-view.ts`, coordinated with the concurrent agent.)
- **Second fix — couldn't drag a session onto an empty rest day (e.g. Saturday → Sunday)**: confirmed desktop, symptom "card picks up but won't drop." Root cause was structural, not the Missed flag (cards stay `draggable="true"` regardless of status). Tri's empty rest row nested a thin `.tri-day-header` inside `.tri-day-row`; the row's `drop` listener early-returns whenever the drop target is inside a `.tri-day-header`, which for an empty row is the *entire* visible content, so the row never handled the drop and the only fallback was a ~16px header sliver that's easy to miss. Running's equivalent (`src/ui/plan-view.ts`) uses a single `.plan-drop-zone` element with an unconditional `preventDefault` on dragover and a generous hit area, and has no such bug. Fix mirrors running: the empty-day branch of `renderDay` now drops the inner `.tri-day-header` wrapper so the `.tri-day-row` is itself a clean drop zone (its drop handler is no longer suppressed), and the pad grew from `6px 8px` to `16px 8px 10px` for a larger target. Populated days keep their header (stacking still needs it). Touch DnD still resolves empty rows correctly (it falls through to `data-tri-day-drop` when no `.tri-day-header` is present).
- **Third fix — drag triggered a full-page refresh**: every successful drop called `renderTriathlonPlanView()`, which rebuilds the whole page and replays the `.hf` `floatUp` entrance animation, reading as a refresh/flash. Mirrored running's `rerenderWeekListLocal`: the day-by-day list now sits in a stable `#tri-plan-day-list` container, the build + handler-wiring are factored into `buildTriDayList` / `wireTriDayList`, and all six drop handlers (3 desktop HTML5 + 3 touch) call a new `rerenderTriDayListLocal()` that swaps only that subtree and rebinds the fresh cards. A day move doesn't change weekly totals, so the summary strip and the rest of the page stay put and the entrance animation no longer replays. Dead duplicated work removed from the main render (`byDay` loop, `injStatus`, `dismissedTests` now live only in `buildTriDayList`; `injState` stays for the injury banner).
- **Verified**: 26 tests in `workout-status.test.ts` pass (incl. 4 new Saturday/`weekEnded` regression cases); `tsc --noEmit` and `lint:ui` clean for all edited files. (Unrelated concurrent-agent work fails `tsc`/`lint:ui` in `empirical-transitions.test.ts`, `race-prediction.triathlon.ts`, `home-view.ts`, and `race-forecast-marquee.ts:56` — none of our files.) **Neither fix is device/in-app verified yet** — the drag fix in particular wants a real drag-and-drop confirmation in the browser.

Follow-up to the same-day per-workout Adjust build, driven by Tristan's feedback on a real tempo card.

Distance-defined runs show "8.0 km · 38 min"; structured sessions (tempo / intervals) show time only, since they have no single honest distance. Triathlon (`triathlon/workout-card.ts`) and HYROX (`hyrox/workout-card.ts`) cards already displayed `estimatedDurationMin`, so time is now present in all three modes. The duration knob is now a single **scale factor** applied to the whole session: every distance (km / m) and duration (min) token scales proportionally and the total minutes scale with it; paces (e.g. "3:52/km") are left untouched. "Scale everything proportionally" was Tristan's chosen model over trimming the main set or cutting reps. So a tempo at 75% becomes "1.5km warm up ... 10min @ 3:52/km (~2.5km) ... 1.5km cool down".
- **Engine reshaped**: `workout-scaling.ts` drops distance-only helpers for `scaleDescriptionProportional` + `scaleDurationMin` + `isSimpleDistanceDesc` + `hasScalableToken`; the slider is now % of original total time. `Workout` and `WorkoutMod` gain optional `originalDurationMin` (the plan-time anchor so a reopened overlay scales from the plan, not the already-scaled state). Tests rewritten (14, incl. pace-preservation, metre reps, factor clamps).

## 2026-05-29 — Per-workout "Adjust" control (running): scale a single session for this session only

- **Feature**: every running workout card now carries an **Adjust** link (next to Mark as Done · Skip) that opens a centered overlay to scale just that session. Two knobs, confirmed with Tristan: a **continuous duration slider** (50%–115% of the prescribed distance) and **stepped Easier / Harder intensity notches** along the pace ladder. Two one-tap presets sit under "Got less time": **Less time, easier** (75% duration, intensity unchanged) and **Less time, same effort** (75% duration + one notch harder). Intensity stayed stepped (not a slider) deliberately — running intensity is zone-defined, and a free slider would re-pace a session out of its zone and corrupt the load the prediction reads.
- **Scope — this session only**: scaling writes a standard `WorkoutMod` (the same persistence the AI coach uses, `coach-tools.ts`), stamped `userScaledAt`, re-applied each render. It never recomputes the plan, weekly load targets, or the race prediction. Fitness/prediction still respond only to the activity actually completed. Because the scaled distance becomes the live `w.d`, distance-based running adherence scores the session against the **scaled** target, so a deliberately trimmed run never reads as a "miss"; the original is preserved (`originalDistance`) and shown via the existing "Adjusted" chip + "(was Xkm)" caption + "Undo adjustment".
- **Honesty boundaries**: the duration slider only appears for runs described primarily as a distance (easy / long / MP / recovery). Structured interval sessions (`5x1km @ threshold`, `WU + 6x800m + CD`) expose only the Easier/Harder notches — length there is governed by the interval structure, not one distance. Status is always `'reduced'` (never `'replaced'`, which plan-view strikes through and filters out), so longer/harder scales don't make the run vanish.
- **Bug fixed in passing**: the reduced-distance card readout used bare `parseFloat(w.d)`, which would render a structured `6x800m` session as "6.0 km". Now uses a km-anchored regex.
- **New**: `src/workouts/workout-scaling.ts` (pure helpers, 15 tests) + `src/ui/workout-adjust-overlay.ts` (overlay). `WorkoutMod` gains optional `userScaledAt` + `newDurationMin`. All magnitudes anchored to existing constants (taper 0.5 floor, effortMultiplier 1.15 ceiling, 3 km `MIN_DISTANCE_KM`, 0.75 reduction tier) — none invented.

## 2026-05-29 — Session generator opens on a "Suggested vs Pick your own" chooser

- **Change**: the running/fitness (incl. Just-Track) session generator now opens on an entry chooser — **Suggested session** vs **Pick your own** — instead of dropping straight into the type picker. Pick-your-own is the existing flow, untouched. Suggested builds a concrete typed session from the recovery read: effort band from `buildSessionRecommendation().recommendedSlot` (the readiness/ACWR/HRV/sleep composite), type via a new `SUGGESTED_SLOT_BY_EFFORT` map (easy → Easy Run, steady → Progressive Run, hard → Threshold), duration from the type's own `defaultMinutes`. No invented numbers. The map walks up the existing RPE ladder (3 → 5 → 7) and deliberately stops short of VO2 (rpe 8) and Time Trial — the system never proposes the highest-risk sessions unprompted; those stay opt-in via Pick-your-own.
- **Card**: shows the type label, duration + distance, the existing readiness caption, and a one-line effort-framed "why this session today". **Accept** commits the session (mirrors `renderStep2`'s non-effort save path exactly — same `buildSessionIntent → intentToWorkout → adhocWorkouts` push, so the suggested and manual paths can't diverge). **Adjust** pre-selects the suggested type and drops into its duration/effort step. **Back** returns to the chooser.
- **No-data fallback**: when there's no recovery signal yet (`readinessScore == null`), suggests the lowest-risk option (Easy Run) rather than the band default of steady — suggesting a structured session to someone we know nothing about is the wrong default.
- **Scope**: the chooser fronts the single-discipline run/fitness flow only. Tri opens straight to its discipline picker (recovery can't pick swim vs bike vs run), hyrox to Run by Feel — both unchanged.
- **Verified**: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `lint:ui` clean for `session-generator.ts` (the one remaining linter delta is the pre-existing committed violation in `triathlon/race-forecast-marquee.ts:56`, unmodified here). Not yet device/in-app verified.

## 2026-05-29 — Logging a triathlon/cycling injury now regenerates the plan so the forecast chips reflect it

- **Problem**: the "X sess/wk · S · B · R" Training chip on the triathlon race-forecast (and the cycling equivalent) counted every entry in the stored `triWorkouts` over the next 4 weeks. The injury discipline gates (`applyTriInjuryGates`) only bake into stored `triWorkouts` at plan-generation time, and the injury modal only force-regenerated **HYROX**. A paused run still counted in the chip's per-discipline session count, and the plan view's "Paused" greying was cosmetic only. Past weeks are preserved — the gate skips them and regen carries over each week's actuals/rated/skip. Corrected the stale comment that claimed triathlon "regenerates weeks on demand" (it does not; it only regenerated on version bump or activity sync).
- **Verified**: `tsc --noEmit` clean for `modal.ts`; injury-recovery + tri-discipline-floor tests green (20 passed). `lint:ui` clean for `modal.ts` (no UI markup changed). Not yet device-verified.

## 2026-05-29 — Bike & aero setup didn't refresh the forecast on save (looked like "it doesn't flow through")

- **Symptom**: changing Riding position (e.g. TT bike → hoods) in the Bike & aero modal appeared to do nothing — the position seemed to "stay on hoods" and the predicted time only moved "after tabbing between pages". Read first as a dropdown revert; it was actually a missing refresh.
- **Root cause**: the Save handler (`bike-setup-view.ts`) called `persistForm(form)` (which invalidates the cached `triConfig.prediction`) then `overlay.remove()`, but **never re-rendered the Forecast page underneath**. So the headline kept showing the stale cached split until the user navigated away and back, which forced a recompute. The change *was* flowing through — it just wasn't visible without a manual tab-switch.
- **Fix**: `openBikeSetupOverlay(onSaved?)` now takes an optional callback, invoked after `persistForm` + `overlay.remove()`. The two Forecast call sites (`forecast-view.ts`, `race-forecast-fingerprint.ts`) pass `() => renderTriathlonForecastView()` so the headline updates instantly on save. Mirrors the methodology-view back-callback pattern; no new import into the modal (callback closes over the render fn at the call site), so no circular import.
- **Also**: deferred the three select `change` handlers' rerender to the next macrotask (`deferRerender = () => setTimeout(rerender, 0)`) as a WebKit safeguard — destroying a native `<select>` synchronously inside its own change event can swallow the commit on Safari/WKWebView (Chromium tolerates it).
- **Verified** in Chromium via Playwright: TT bike → hoods + Save updated the forecast in place, no navigation — finish 4:50:19 → 5:09:43, bike split 2:14:38 → 2:32:47 (hoods far less aero than a TT bike). Needs device/Safari confirmation.

## 2026-05-29 — Bike & aero setup now flows into the triathlon bike split without a power-meter flag

- **Problem**: `estimateBikeSpeed` (`race-prediction.triathlon.ts`) gated the full power-balance physics on `tri.bike.hasPowerMeter === true`. For any triathlon user without that flag set, the predictor dropped to a linear FTP-only fit, so changing rider weight, bike weight, riding position, tyres, or course profile in the Bike & aero modal had **zero effect** on the predicted split. The modal preview (which always runs physics) and the headline forecast silently diverged.
- **Fix**: gate the physics path on data presence only — `ftp && aero && bodyWeightKg && bikeWeightKg` — matching the cycling predictor (`race-prediction.cycling.ts`), which never required `hasPowerMeter`. FTP can be derived without a dedicated meter, and the modal always writes an aero profile + masses on save, so the physics path fires after any save. Removed the now-unused `hasPower` param from `estimateBikeSpeed` and its call site.
- **Result**: all the Bike & aero controls (weight, position, tyres, course, calibrated/manual CdA) now flow into the triathlon split, and the modal preview agrees with the headline forecast (ISSUE-189 test still green). Triathlon and cycling now use identical physics gating.
- **Not changed**: the no-FTP/no-mass fallbacks still ignore some inputs (tri fallback ignores course; tyre change doesn't re-invert a calibrated CdA). Logged but deferred per scope.

## 2026-05-29 — Re-fixed injury edit advancing the plan week (ISSUE-248 regression)

The ISSUE-248 fix documented on 2026-05-27 was not actually in the codebase — neither on `feat/revenue-cat-iap` nor on `main` (both still had the unconditional `await next()`; `advanceWeekAfterSave` existed nowhere). The doc entry survived a multi-agent rollback that reverted the code. Re-reported by Tristan ("if you update your injury it kicks you forward a week") and re-applied.

- **Bug**: `handleSaveInjury` (`src/ui/injury/modal.ts`) called `events.ts:next()` — the full complete-week-and-advance flow (`s.w++`) — on every save of an already-active injury. Banner/button edits, which never intend to advance, advanced anyway. Each edit pushed the user forward one week, permanently (the launch corrector `advanceWeekToToday()` only moves forward, so it never pulled `s.w` back).
- **Fix**: `openInjuryModal({ advanceWeekAfterSave })` opt-in flag. Only the weekly check-in gate (`events.ts:873`, acute/rehab/test_capacity phases, where saving the check-in resumes the paused advance) passes `true`. All other entry points (plan-view / main-view banners, triathlon plan-view, daily check-in overlay) stay bare → re-render in place via `render()`, no advance. The dedicated return-to-run / graduated-return gate modals are unchanged.
- **Also seen in this incident**: `planStartDate` had drifted forward a week, so `s.w` and the calendar anchor disagreed. Tristan's local state was reset via console (planStartDate → 2026-04-27, s.w → 5) back to "Friday, week 5".
- **Key files**: `src/ui/injury/modal.ts`, `src/ui/events.ts`. `tsc` + `lint:ui` clean on touched files. ISSUE-248 still ⚠️ awaiting device verification (two paths to confirm: banner edit must NOT advance; completing a week while injured MUST advance once).

## 2026-05-29 — Guided HYROX sessions log as matchable activities + in-app finish dialog

Follow-on to the HYROX guided-session learning work. Three pieces:

**1. Verified learning → prediction (no code change, added a test).** Confirmed the station benchmark a session writes (`stationBenchmarksSingles`) is the exact scalar the predictor reads (`race-prediction.hyrox.ts:189`). New test in `hyrox-guided-flow.test.ts` proves it end-to-end: a session that beats a station benchmark (600s → 300s) lowers the predicted finish by >120s. The station-detail / forecast / stats views read the same scalar, so they update too.

**2. Native `confirm()` → in-app dialog.** The "Finish the session?" prompt was a native `confirm()` (renders as "localhost says…" and behaves poorly in the iOS WKWebView). Replaced both with an in-app centered card (`showFinishConfirm` in `guided-strength-overlay.ts`): "Finish the session? / Your time so far will be logged." + Keep going / Finish. Verified live.

**3. Guided sessions now log as matchable activities.** Finishing a guided HYROX session previously only marked the workout rated + updated benchmarks — it never created an activity record, so nothing appeared in history and a later watch sync had nothing to dedupe against. Now:
   - `completeStrengthSession` writes a `GarminActual` to `wk.garminActuals[workoutId]` (`garminId` prefixed `'guided-'`), carrying duration + a `hyroxSession` recap (per-station best round + run legs).
   - The matcher (`activity-matcher.ts` HYROX block) treats a workout whose actual is a guided one as an **upgrade candidate**: when the watch/Strava recording of the same session syncs, it **replaces** the guided actual with the richer data (HR, GPS) instead of creating a duplicate — mirroring the Strava-beats-Garmin rule. The `hyroxSession` recap is preserved across the upgrade.
   - `activity-detail` renders the recap (run legs with pace + per-station best round) so the session is reviewable later, not just on the finish screen.
   - **Verified live**: guided session creates a `guided-` actual with a 3-station recap; a simulated HIIT sync upgrades it (`garminId` → `sync-999`, `avgHR` 165) with the recap preserved and **no duplicate** (still 1 actual).
   - Tests: `buildHyroxSessionRecap` (2) in `hyrox-session-benchmarks.test.ts`; prediction-chain test in `hyrox-guided-flow.test.ts`. Full suite 2426 pass, typecheck + `lint:ui` clean.
   - **Follow-up**: a synced HYROX activity's own per-station splits (via the existing-but-unwired `applyParsedBenchmarks`) could also feed benchmarks on upgrade — not wired yet. And the whole flow wants real-device verification with an actual watch sync.

## 2026-05-29 — Fixed injury painting onto historic weeks (looked like history rewritten / logs lost)

Old bug, re-introduced, in two independent places. An active injury was being applied to **past** weeks, not just the current/future ones. Injury must only look forward.

- **Triathlon display (the one Tristan actually saw)**: `src/ui/triathlon/plan-view.ts:146` computed the per-discipline injury status (`injStatus`) from `isInjuryActive()` alone, ignoring `isPastWeek` (already derived two lines above at :88). It was then handed to `renderDay` for every week, so scrolling to a previous week painted "Easy intensity only. Injury management" over already-trained swim/bike/run cards. Fix: gate `injState` on `!isPastWeek` so past weeks render their original cards untouched.
- **Running generator**: `src/workouts/generator.ts:326` applied `applyInjuryAdaptations` whenever `injuryState.active`, with no check on which week was being generated. Running plans regenerate on the fly at render time (`computeRenderedWorkouts`), so rendering any past week while injured collapsed it to acute rest, orphaning that week's matched actuals. Fix: only adapt when `weekIndex >= getState().w`. The triathlon and HYROX *engines* already guard this (`plan_engine.triathlon.ts:354` / `plan_engine.hyrox.ts:353`); the running generator and the tri *display* layer were the two gaps. The illness path (`plan-view.ts:2305`) was already correctly gated on `isCurrentWeek`.
- **Hardening (unified the rule so it can't drift again)**: extracted the forward-only check into one shared `injuryAppliesToWeek(weekIndex, currentWeek)` in `src/injury/engine.ts` (`weekIndex == null || weekIndex >= currentWeek`). Both fixed sites now call it — the running generator and the tri display — instead of two hand-written `isPastWeek` checks. Confirmed completeness: the running plan header `injured` flag already takes `isCurrentWeek`; `week-debrief`'s `generateWeekWorkouts` call inherits the generator guard; no other unguarded past-week injury site.
- **Tests**: `injuryAppliesToWeek` unit tests (`engine.test.ts`) + 3 output-level regression tests in `generator.test.ts` (past week not collapsed while injured; past-week plan matches the no-injury baseline; current/future weeks still adapt). The tri display gate can't be output-tested (vitest env is `node`, no DOM) — it is protected by routing through the shared helper. Full suite green (2451 tests). Typecheck + UI-lint clean.
- **Key files**: `src/injury/engine.ts` (+test), `src/ui/triathlon/plan-view.ts`, `src/workouts/generator.ts`, `src/workouts/generator.test.ts`. Not yet device-verified.

## 2026-05-29 — HYROX forecast: restored the lost chip-hero + Race/Station-order build, added injury-aware projection

The HYROX forecast was "all over the place" because a crash-restore commit (`4b57684`) rolled `forecast-view.ts` back to an older monolith, wiping out a chip-hero rebuild that already existed (the FEATURES.md description and the chip-detail sub-pages survived; the view that rendered them did not). Recovered it from the `7e9c5ca` auto-snapshot (2026-05-19) and added injury handling on top.

The legacy "Sharpen this forecast" banner, standalone "Race-day projection" card, and "Course factors" card stay folded into the chips. Matches the screenshots Tristan provided.
- **Restored the Race order / Station order toggle**. Race order = passive pacing clock (16 rows in race sequence, each with a cumulative Total-time column, run rows keep the fatigue bar). Station order = where you'll gain (8 stations then 8 runs, each row `now → race day` with the gain delta). Per-event roxzone+venue overhead distributed uniformly so the cumulative clock lands on the headline finish.

Blocked region → no projected gain on its stations. Today's "race now" number is unchanged; only the race-day gain shrinks. Hero shows a one-line recovery note (`renderHyroxInjuryNote`).
- **No new constants**: the recovery math, per-region capacity table, and resume-window capture (the HYROX injury modal already shows run/upper/lower sliders) all predate this. The only new artefact is the anatomical station→region map. No-injury path is bit-for-bit unchanged (verified by test).

### Follow-up after first device test (same day)

Testing showed injury wasn't reaching HYROX at all: the plan still prescribed runs and station circuits (ski/row) the athlete had marked off-limits, and the forecast didn't move. Root causes, all fixed:

- **Plan never regenerated on injury** (the big one). HYROX plans are gated only at generation time, and nothing rebuilt them when an injury was logged (running/triathlon regenerate on demand; HYROX did not). Fix: `src/ui/injury/modal.ts` `handleSaveInjury` now regenerates the current + future HYROX weeks via `regenerateHyroxWeek` after every save, so `applyHyroxInjuryGates` runs — blocked run → runs dropped; blocked upper/lower → station circuits dropped (a mixed circuit can't be split, so `min(upper,lower)` governs); reduced → durations scaled. Past weeks preserved.
- **Forecast debit depended on a saved resume window.** The per-station/run build-week debit is `resumeWeeks × (1 − capacity/100)`, so a capacity slider set without a "back to X in N weeks" value debited nothing → full projected gain for a sport you can't train. Fix: `injuryWithResumeFallback` (`src/calculations/hyrox-injury.ts`) fills any restricted discipline lacking a window with the injury protocol's typical-recovery midpoint — the SAME clinical band the modal uses to pre-fill the field, so no new constant. Run + station debits and the hero injury note all route through it, so the forecast now responds to an injury whether or not a window was entered. (SCIENCE_LOG §AQ updated.)
- **Station/brick cards de-cluttered** (`src/ui/hyrox/workout-card.ts`): the redundant prose paragraph is suppressed when a component list is present. Station cards now show badge + name + the clean bullet list only; runs keep their one-liner.
- Tests: `hyrox-injury.test.ts` now 17 (added protocol-fallback unit tests + an integration test proving an arm injury with NO saved window still reduces the projected stations gain). Full suite 2441 passing; tsc clean.

## 2026-05-29 — Manual-entry onboarding: invalid PB time no longer "reloads" the page

Tristan reported that typing an invalid time into a Recent Personal Bests field made the onboarding step flash/reload and the validation error never appeared.

- **Root cause** (`src/ui/wizard/steps/manual-entry.ts`): the PB-field `blur` handler called `rerender()` unconditionally, rebuilding the entire step via `renderManualEntry`. That replayed the `m-rise` entrance animations (the visible "page reload"), wiped the user's typed text, and destroyed the inline error message the `validate()` call had just shown. The full re-render was also the only thing keeping the closed-over `state` fresh between edits.
- **Fix**: on blur, validate first. An invalid value keeps its inline error visible and is not committed or re-rendered, so both the typed text and the error survive. A valid value commits and refreshes only the experience-consistency notice in place (`refreshNotice()` updates a new `#exp-notice-slot`, re-wiring its apply button) instead of rebuilding the page. Experience-pill selection and the "Use suggested level" CTA now also update in place via `applyExperience()` (toggles pill styling + refreshes the notice). `commitPbs` reads live state via `getOnboardingState()` since there's no longer a full re-render to refresh the captured `state`.
- No new state fields. Typecheck clean, `lint:ui` clean for this file.

## 2026-05-29 — HYROX station sessions: round count fills the budget, timed rest, live dual timer

Three issues Tristan reported on the Higher Ops plan's station session.

**Issue 1 — "55m doesn't add up; just two sets of two."** Root cause: `generateStationDensity`/`generateStationTechnique` prescribed a fixed round count (2 / 3) but set `estimatedDurationMin` to the scheduler's raw slot budget. A ~26-min session (2 rounds × 2 stations, intermediate) was labelled 55m. Fix (SCIENCE_LOG §AO): round count now **fills the time budget** — `rounds = clamp(floor(budget ÷ roundDuration), bandMin, bandMax)`, mirroring the brick generator. Band ranges sourced from research §3.5 (beginner 2–4, novice/intermediate 4–6, advanced/competitive 6–8). Headline duration is recomputed from the actual work+rest sum. Density bumped to 2 discriminator stations + 1 erg (was 2 total); technique up to 4 (was 3). MTL now scales with actual rounds. Per Tristan's "what would a coach do — prescribe enough work" steer.

**Issue 3 — inter-station timer should be 30s, not "as long as you like".** `parseHyroxSession` previously set `manualAdvance: true` + `restSec: 0` for every HYROX session, triggering the unbounded pause. Now rests are prescribed: components carry `restAfterSec` (30s density / 60s technique), the last component of each round uses `hyroxRoundRestSec` (2–3 min), and `manualAdvance` is true **only** for the calibration assessment (`hyrox_assessment`). The adapter expands the component list by `hyroxRounds`, reusing the original component index so the GPS bridge + progress rings still resolve.

**Issue 2 — see current-exercise time alongside session time.** Added `StrengthGuideController.currentSetElapsedSec`; the active screen now shows a live session clock and a live current-station clock side by side.

- **Types**: `HyroxComponent.restAfterSec?`, `Workout.hyroxRounds?` / `hyroxRoundRestSec?` (all optional, fresh-install safe).
- **Modal**: detail-modal round/rest copy now reads from the workout instead of hardcoded "2 rounds"/"3 rounds".
- **Tests**: new `hyrox-generators.test.ts` (6 — duration follows work, band-clamped rounds, rest encoding); `strength-model.test.ts` +5 (rounds expansion, rest pattern, assessment-only manual advance, backward-compat); `strength-controller.test.ts` +1 (dual timer). Full suite 2378 pass, typecheck clean, `lint:ui` clean for touched files.
- **Not device-verified yet.** Brick/mini-brick also now expand rounds + use timed rest (consistency with the Mirror rule); Tristan only tested the density session, so the brick guided flow (GPS run legs × multiple rounds) needs an on-device pass. Pre-existing `race-forecast-marquee.ts:56` lint violation is unrelated (not in this changeset) and left untouched.

### Guided HYROX sessions now learn from your times (SCIENCE_LOG §AP)

Tristan: "we're not logging the times… we should be learning from how well someone's doing." Three broken links found and fixed:
1. **The capture was dead.** `writeHyroxStationHistory` guarded on `components.length === records.length`, which the rounds-expansion above always breaks (records now = rounds × stations), so nothing was written. It also targeted `triConfig.stationBenchmarkHistory` while the predictor/UI read `hyroxConfig`, and it never updated the scalar benchmark the prediction actually uses.
2. **New learning module** `src/calculations/hyrox-session-benchmarks.ts`: takes the **best (fastest) round** per station, and **only from race-pace sessions** (density, brick) — technique (65% pace) is shown but never feeds the benchmark. **PB-only** (a slow day never degrades it; an un-benchmarked station is calibrated), with a **sanity floor** (elite seed time) to reject timing slips. When the best round beats the stored benchmark it auto-updates the scalar slot + appends a `'session'`-sourced history entry, written to the correct `hyroxConfig` object.
3. **Real end-of-session summary**: `buildHyroxFinishSummary` in the overlay shows each station's best round, how it ranks vs the field (percentile), and a "Benchmark updated. Ns faster than your best." line when it improved. Technique rows are labelled "technique pace".
- Conservative by design: logs the **raw** fatigued best round (no invented un-fatigue multiplier); surfaces the update in the summary the user is already viewing (no launch-toast threshold to invent). Tracking, not planning. New source `'session'` ("Session best") added to the benchmark history enum + station-detail label.
- **Tests**: `hyrox-session-benchmarks.test.ts` (9) + `hyrox-guided-flow.test.ts` (5, full real pipeline: generate → parse → controller walk → benchmark). Typecheck + `lint:ui` clean.

### End-to-end verification (density + brick) + one fix

Drove both session types through the real app (live store + overlay + Save button, walked via a controllable clock):
- **Density**: 3 rounds / 3 stations, duration 58 min (fills the 55-min slot), dual timer, timed rests, finish summary; Save wrote `wall_balls 9999 → 300` with a `'session'` history entry. Calibration path ("New session best recorded") confirmed for stations with no prior benchmark.
- **Brick**: 4 rounds × (run + station) = 8 sets all walked; GPS bridge degraded to manual tap in headless without breaking the interleaved run/station walk; station benchmark updated (runs correctly skipped).
- **Fix found in verification**: the finish subtitle counted components, so a brick read "4 rounds across 2 stations" (one is a run). Now counts stations and phrases run-bearing sessions as "N rounds of run + M station(s)" (`guided-strength-overlay.ts`).
- **Run legs in the brick summary (built)**: `summariseHyroxRuns` surfaces each run leg in round order with time + pace (unit-aware via `formatPace`), no benchmark — run fitness lives in pace/VDOT. The brick finish summary now lists "Run · round N · 1 km · 4:10/km" per leg above the station row, so fade across the brick is visible (verified live: 4:10 → 4:22 → 4:34 → 4:46/km across 4 rounds). 3 tests added to `hyrox-session-benchmarks.test.ts` (12 total). Density/technique unaffected (no run components).
